title: 禪宗經典
note: Three texts served sequentially: 信心銘 (Faith in Mind) → 金剛經 (Diamond Sutra) → 六祖壇經 (Platform Sutra)

passages.text: 至道無難唯嫌揀擇但莫憎愛洞然明白毫釐有差天地懸隔欲得現前莫存順逆違順相爭是為心病不識玄旨徒勞念靜圓同太虛無欠無餘良由取捨所以不如莫逐有緣勿住空忍一種平懷泯然自盡止動歸止止更彌動唯滯兩邊寧知一種一種不通兩處失功遣有沒有從空背空多言多慮轉不相應絕言絕慮無處不通歸根得旨隨照失宗須臾返照勝卻前空
passages.translation_en:
The Great Way is not difficult —
it only avoids picking and choosing.
Simply do not hate or love,
and it will be thoroughly clear.

A hair's breadth of difference,
and heaven and earth are set apart.
If you wish it to appear before you,
do not hold to for or against.

Conflict between for and against —
this is the mind's disease.
Without recognizing the profound principle,
you toil in vain to quiet your thoughts.

Perfect like great emptiness,
with nothing lacking, nothing in excess.
Only because of grasping and rejecting
do we fail to see its suchness.

Do not chase after entanglements,
do not dwell in the patience of emptiness.
In oneness and equanimity of heart,
all things dissolve of themselves.

When you stop movement to return to stillness,
that stopping only creates more agitation.
If you linger in either extreme,
how will you ever know oneness?

Without penetrating oneness,
both paths lose their function.
Banish existence and you drown in it;
follow emptiness and you turn your back on it.

Excessive words, excessive thinking —
only take you further from accordance.
Cut off words, cut off thinking,
and there is nowhere you cannot penetrate.

Return to the root and grasp the meaning;
chase after appearances and lose the source.
One moment of inward reflection
surpasses the emptiness that came before.

passages.text: 前空轉變皆由妄見不用求真唯須息見二見不住慎勿追尋纔有是非紛然失心二由一有一亦莫守一心不生萬法無咎無咎無法不生不心能隨境滅境逐能沉境由能境能由境能欲知兩段元是一空一空同兩齊含萬象不見精麤寧有偏黨大道體寬無易無難小見狐疑轉急轉遲執之失度必入邪路放之自然體無去住任性合道逍遙絕惱繫念乖真昏沉不好
passages.translation_en:
That prior emptiness was transformed —
all from deluded views.
No need to seek the true;
simply cease to cherish opinions.

Do not dwell in dualistic views;
be careful not to pursue them.
The moment right and wrong arise,
the mind is lost in confusion.

Two comes from one,
yet do not cling even to the one.
When the one mind does not arise,
the myriad things are without fault.

No fault, no things;
no arising, no mind.
The subject dissolves with its object;
the object sinks with its subject.

Object exists because of subject;
subject exists because of object.
If you wish to know both sides,
know they are originally one emptiness.

In one emptiness both are the same,
each containing the myriad forms.
Do not distinguish coarse from fine,
and how can bias arise?

The Great Way is vast in substance,
neither easy nor difficult.
Small views breed doubt;
the more you hurry, the more you fall behind.

Cling to it and you lose measure,
surely entering a crooked path.
Let it go naturally,
and its essence neither departs nor abides.

Surrender to your nature and accord with the Way,
wandering free, beyond vexation.
Bound-up thinking strays from the real;
sinking into dullness is equally no good.

passages.text: 不好勞神何用疏親欲取一乘勿惡六塵六塵不惡還同正覺智者無為愚人自縛法無異法妄自愛著將心用心豈非大錯迷生寂亂悟無好惡一切二邊良由斟酌夢幻空華何勞把捉得失是非一時放卻眼若不眠諸夢自除心若不異萬法一如一如體玄兀爾忘緣萬法齊觀歸復自然泯其所以不可方比止動無動動止無止兩既不成一何有爾究竟窮極不存軌則
passages.translation_en:
It is no good to weary the spirit —
what use is there in estrangement or intimacy?
If you wish to travel the One Vehicle,
do not despise the six sense-objects.

The six sense-objects, not despised,
become identical with true awakening.
The wise act without contrivance;
the foolish bind themselves.

Dharma has no separate dharmas;
delusion creates its own attachments.
Using the mind to grasp the mind —
is this not the great mistake?

From confusion arise stillness and turmoil;
in awakening there is no good or bad.
All dualities
come from deliberate thinking.

Dreams, illusions, flowers in the sky —
why trouble yourself to grasp them?
Gain and loss, right and wrong —
let them all go at once.

If the eyes never sleep,
all dreams naturally cease.
If the mind makes no distinctions,
the myriad things are one suchness.

One suchness is profound in its essence,
unmoving, free from conditions.
Contemplate the myriad things as equal
and you return to your natural state.

When their reasons are dissolved,
no comparisons can be made.
Stop movement and there is no movement;
set movement going and there is no stillness.

When both cease to exist,
how can the one stand alone?
Pursue this to the ultimate end:
no rules or measures remain.

passages.text: 契心平等所作俱息狐疑淨盡正信調直一切不留無可記憶虛明自照不勞心力非思量處識情難測真如法界無他無自要急相應唯言不二不二皆同無不包容十方智者皆入此宗宗非促延一念萬年無在不在十方目前極小同大忘絕境界極大同小不見邊表有即是無無即是有若不如是必不須守一即一切一切即一但能如是何慮不畢信心不二不二信心言語道斷非去來今
passages.translation_en:
Align the mind with equanimity,
and all striving comes to rest.
Doubt is cleansed completely;
true faith stands upright.

Nothing whatsoever is retained,
nothing that can be remembered.
Empty, luminous, self-illuminating,
no effort of the mind is needed.

This is not a place of thinking —
consciousness and sentiment cannot fathom it.
In the true suchness of the Dharma-realm,
there is no other and no self.

To swiftly accord with this,
only say: not two.
In not-two, all is the same;
nothing is excluded.

The wise in all directions
all enter this teaching.
This teaching is beyond haste or delay;
one thought encompasses ten thousand years.

It is nowhere, yet it is everywhere;
the ten directions stand before your eyes.
The infinitely small equals the infinitely large,
when the boundaries of the world are forgotten.

The infinitely large equals the infinitely small,
when edges can no longer be seen.
Existence is precisely emptiness;
emptiness is precisely existence.

If it is not like this,
you must not hold to it.
One is all;
all is one.

If you can simply be like this,
why worry that it is not complete?
Faith and mind are not two;
not-two is the faithful mind.

Words cannot open this road;
it is not of the past, the present, or the future.

passages.text: 如是我聞。一時，佛在舍衛國祇樹給孤獨園，與大比丘眾千二百五十人俱。爾時，世尊食時，著衣持缽，入舍衛大城乞食。於其城中，次第乞已，還至本處。飯食訖，收衣缽，洗足已，敷座而坐。
passages.translation_en: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the Jeta Grove of Anathapindika's Garden in the state of Shravasti, together with a great assembly of 1,250 monks. At mealtime, the World-Honored One put on his robe, took up his bowl, and entered the great city of Shravasti to beg for food. After begging sequentially through the city, he returned to his place. When the meal was finished, he put away his robe and bowl, washed his feet, arranged his seat, and sat down.

passages.text: 時，長老須菩提，在大眾中，即從座起，偏袒右肩，右膝著地，合掌恭敬。而白佛言：「希有世尊！如來善護念諸菩薩，善付囑諸菩薩。世尊！善男子、善女人，發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心，應云何住？云何降伏其心？」佛言：「善哉，善哉。須菩提！如汝所說：如來善護念諸菩薩，善付囑諸菩薩。汝今諦聽，當為汝說：善男子、善女人，發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心，應如是住，如是降伏其心。」「唯然，世尊！願樂欲聞。」
passages.translation_en: At that time, the elder Subhuti, who was among the great assembly, rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt on his right knee, and with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Buddha: "How rare, World-Honored One! The Tathagata skillfully protects and is mindful of all bodhisattvas, and skillfully entrusts and instructs all bodhisattvas. World-Honored One, when good men and good women give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, how should they abide? How should they subdue their minds?" The Buddha said: "Excellent, excellent! Subhuti, it is just as you say — the Tathagata skillfully protects and is mindful of all bodhisattvas, and skillfully entrusts and instructs all bodhisattvas. Now listen carefully, and I shall explain it for you. When good men and good women give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, they should abide thus, and thus subdue their minds." "Yes, World-Honored One! We joyfully wish to hear."

passages.text: 佛告須菩提：「諸菩薩摩訶薩，應如是降伏其心：所有一切眾生之類，若卵生、若胎生、若濕生、若化生；若有色、若無色；若有想、若無想、若非有想非無想，我皆令入無餘涅槃而滅度之。如是滅度無量無數無邊眾生，實無眾生得滅度者。何以故？須菩提！若菩薩有我相、人相、眾生相、壽者相，即非菩薩。」
passages.translation_en: The Buddha told Subhuti: "All bodhisattva-mahasattvas should subdue their minds thus: All living beings — whether born from eggs, from wombs, from moisture, or by transformation; whether with form or without form; whether with perception, without perception, or neither with nor without perception — I vow to lead them all to nirvana without remainder, liberating them completely. Yet when immeasurable, countless, boundless beings have thus been liberated, in truth no being has been liberated. Why? Subhuti, if a bodhisattva holds to the notion of a self, a person, a sentient being, or a life span, then that one is not a bodhisattva."

passages.text: 「復次，須菩提！菩薩於法，應無所住，行於布施。所謂不住色布施，不住聲、香、味、觸、法布施。須菩提！菩薩應如是布施，不住於相。何以故？若菩薩不住相布施。其福德不可思量。」「須菩提！於意云何？東方虛空，可思量不？」「不也，世尊！」「須菩提！南、西、北方，四維上下虛空，可思量不？」「不也，世尊！」「須菩提！菩薩無住相布施，福德亦復如是不可思量。須菩提！菩薩但應如所教住。」
passages.translation_en: "Furthermore, Subhuti, a bodhisattva should practice giving without abiding in anything. That is to say, one should give without abiding in form, and give without abiding in sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects. Subhuti, a bodhisattva should give in this way — without abiding in any characteristic. Why? If a bodhisattva gives without abiding in characteristics, the merit is beyond reckoning." "Subhuti, what do you think? Can the space to the east be measured?" "No, World-Honored One." "Subhuti, can the space to the south, west, north, or in the four intermediate directions, above and below, be measured?" "No, World-Honored One." "Subhuti, the merit of a bodhisattva who gives without abiding in characteristics is likewise beyond reckoning. Subhuti, a bodhisattva should abide only as instructed."

passages.text: 「須菩提。於意云何？可以身相見如來不？」「不也，世尊，不可以身相得見如來。何以故？如來所說身相，即非身相。」佛告須菩提：「凡所有相，皆是虛妄。若見諸相非相，即見如來。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be seen by means of bodily characteristics?" "No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata cannot be seen by means of bodily characteristics. Why? What the Tathagata calls bodily characteristics are not bodily characteristics." The Buddha told Subhuti: "All that has characteristics is illusory. If you see all characteristics as non-characteristics, then you see the Tathagata."

passages.text: 須菩提白佛言：「世尊！頗有眾生，得聞如是言說章句，生實信不？」佛告須菩提：「莫作是說。如來滅後，後五百歲，有持戒修福者，於此章句能生信心，以此為實，當知是人不於一佛、二佛、三四五佛而種善根，已於無量千萬佛所種諸善根，聞是章句，乃至一念生淨信者，須菩提！如來悉知悉見，是諸眾生得如是無量福德。何以故？是諸眾生無復我相、人相、眾生相、壽者相。」「無法相，亦無非法相。何以故？是諸眾生若心取相，則為著我、人、眾生、壽者。」「若取法相，即著我、人、眾生、壽者。何以故？若取非法相，即著我、人、眾生、壽者。是故不應取法，不應取非法。以是義故，如來常說：汝等比丘，知我說法，如筏喻者，法尚應捨，何況非法。」
passages.translation_en: Subhuti addressed the Buddha: "World-Honored One, will there be beings who, upon hearing these words and passages, can give rise to true faith?" The Buddha told Subhuti: "Do not speak thus. In the last five hundred years after the Tathagata's passing, there will be those who uphold the precepts and cultivate merit who can give rise to faith in these passages and accept them as truth. Know that such people have planted good roots not with just one, two, three, four, or five Buddhas, but have already planted good roots with immeasurable millions of Buddhas. Upon hearing these passages, those who give rise to even a single thought of pure faith — Subhuti, the Tathagata fully knows and fully sees them. These beings attain such immeasurable merit. Why? Because these beings no longer hold to the notion of a self, a person, a sentient being, or a life span." "They hold neither to the notion of dharmas nor to the notion of no-dharmas. Why? If these beings seize upon characteristics in their minds, they cling to self, person, sentient being, and life span." "If they seize upon the notion of dharmas, they cling to self, person, sentient being, and life span. Why? If they seize upon the notion of no-dharmas, they likewise cling to self, person, sentient being, and life span. Therefore, one should not grasp at dharmas, nor should one grasp at no-dharmas. For this reason, the Tathagata always says: You monks should know that my teaching of the Dharma is like a raft. Even the Dharma should be let go of, how much more so what is not the Dharma."

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提耶？如來有所說法耶？」須菩提言：「如我解佛所說義，無有定法，名『阿耨多羅三藐三菩提』，亦無有定法，如來可說。何以故？如來所說法。皆不可取、不可說；非法，非非法。所以者何？一切賢聖，皆以無為法而有差別。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? Has the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi? Has the Tathagata spoken any Dharma?" Subhuti said: "As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, there is no fixed dharma called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, nor is there any fixed dharma the Tathagata could speak. Why? The Dharma the Tathagata has spoken cannot be grasped and cannot be spoken; it is neither dharma nor not-dharma. How so? All sages and saints are distinguished by the unconditioned."

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？若人滿三千大千世界七寶以用布施，是人所得福德，寧為多不？」須菩提言：「甚多，世尊！何以故？是福德即非福德性，是故如來說福德多。」「若復有人，於此經中受持，乃至四句偈等，為他人說，其福勝彼。何以故？須菩提！一切諸佛，及諸佛阿耨多羅三藐三菩提法，皆從此經出。須菩提！所謂佛法者，即非佛法，是名佛法。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? If someone filled the three-thousand-fold great-thousand world with the seven precious treasures and used them for giving, would the merit gained by this person be great?" Subhuti said: "Very great, World-Honored One. Why? This merit is not the nature of merit itself; therefore the Tathagata says the merit is great." "If, on the other hand, someone receives and upholds even as few as four lines of verse from this sutra and explains them to others, that person's merit surpasses the former. Why? Subhuti, all Buddhas and all the Dharma of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi of all Buddhas come forth from this sutra. Subhuti, what is called the Buddha-Dharma is not the Buddha-Dharma; it is called the Buddha-Dharma."

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？須陀洹能作是念：『我得須陀洹果』不？」須菩提言：「不也，世尊！何以故？須陀洹名為入流，而無所入；不入色、聲、香、味、觸、法，是名須陀洹。」「須菩提！於意云何？斯陀含能作是念：『我得斯陀含果』不？」須菩提言：「不也，世尊！何以故？斯陀含名一往來，而實無往來，是名斯陀含。
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? Can a stream-enterer have the thought 'I have attained the fruit of stream-entry'?" Subhuti said: "No, World-Honored One. Why? A stream-enterer is called 'one who has entered the stream,' yet there is nothing entered. One does not enter into form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects — this is what is called a stream-enterer." "Subhuti, what do you think? Can a once-returner have the thought 'I have attained the fruit of once-returning'?" Subhuti said: "No, World-Honored One. Why? A once-returner is called 'one who comes and goes once more,' yet in truth there is no coming or going — this is what is called a once-returner."

passages.text: 」「須菩提！於意云何？阿那含能作是念：『我得阿那含果』不？」須菩提言：「不也，世尊！何以故？阿那含名為不來，而實無不來，是故名阿那含。」「須菩提！於意云何？阿羅漢能作是念：『我得阿羅漢道』不？」須菩提言：「不也，世尊！何以故？實無有法名阿羅漢。世尊！若阿羅漢作是念：『我得阿羅漢道』即為著我、人、眾生、壽者。世尊！佛說我得無諍三昧，人中最為第一，是第一離欲阿羅漢。世尊！我不作是念：『我是離欲阿羅漢。
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? Can a non-returner have the thought 'I have attained the fruit of non-returning'?" Subhuti said: "No, World-Honored One. Why? A non-returner is called 'one who does not return,' yet in truth there is no non-returning — therefore one is called a non-returner." "Subhuti, what do you think? Can an arhat have the thought 'I have attained the way of the arhat'?" Subhuti said: "No, World-Honored One. Why? There is in truth no dharma called 'arhat.' World-Honored One, if an arhat were to think 'I have attained the way of the arhat,' that would be clinging to self, person, sentient being, and life span. World-Honored One, the Buddha has said that I have attained the samadhi of non-contention, that I am foremost among people, the foremost arhat free from desire. Yet, World-Honored One, I do not think 'I am an arhat free from desire.'"

passages.text: 』世尊！我若作是念：『我得阿羅漢道。』世尊則不說須菩提是樂阿蘭那行者。以須菩提實無所行，而名須菩提，是樂阿蘭那行。」。
passages.translation_en: "World-Honored One, if I were to think 'I have attained the way of the arhat,' then the World-Honored One would not say that Subhuti delights in the practice of dwelling in peace. Because Subhuti in truth has no such practice, Subhuti is said to delight in the practice of dwelling in peace."

passages.text: 佛告須菩提：「於意云何？如來昔在燃燈佛所，於法有所得不？」「不也，世尊！如來在燃燈佛所，於法實無所得。」「須菩提！於意云何？菩薩莊嚴佛土不？」「不也，世尊！何以故？莊嚴佛土者，即非莊嚴，是名莊嚴。」「是故，須菩提！諸菩薩摩訶薩，應如是生清淨心，不應住色生心，不應住聲、香、味、觸、法生心，應無所住而生其心。」「須菩提！譬如有人，身如須彌山王，於意云何？是身為大不？」須菩提言：「甚大，世尊！何以故？佛說非身，是名大身。」
passages.translation_en: The Buddha told Subhuti: "What do you think? When the Tathagata was with Dipankara Buddha, did he attain any dharma?" "No, World-Honored One. When the Tathagata was with Dipankara Buddha, he in truth attained no dharma." "Subhuti, what do you think? Does a bodhisattva adorn buddha-lands?" "No, World-Honored One. Why? Adorning buddha-lands is not adorning; it is called adorning." "Therefore, Subhuti, all bodhisattva-mahasattvas should give rise to a pure mind thus: they should not give rise to a mind that abides in form, nor should they give rise to a mind that abides in sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects. They should give rise to a mind that abides nowhere." "Subhuti, suppose there were a person whose body was as great as Mount Sumeru. What do you think — would that body be great?" Subhuti said: "Very great, World-Honored One. Why? The Buddha has said it is not a body; that is what is called a great body."

passages.text: 「須菩提！如恆河中所有沙數，如是沙等恆河，於意云何？是諸恆河沙，寧為多不？」須菩提言：「甚多，世尊！但諸恆河，尚多無數，何況其沙。」「須菩提！我今實言告汝：若有善男子、善女人，以七寶滿爾所恆河沙數三千大千世界，以用布施，得福多不？」須菩提言：「甚多，世尊！」佛告須菩提：「若善男子、善女人，於此經中，乃至受持四句偈等，為他人說，而此福德，勝前福德。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, what do you think — would the grains of sand in all those Ganges Rivers be many?" Subhuti said: "Very many, World-Honored One. The Ganges Rivers alone would already be countless, how much more so the sand in them all." "Subhuti, I now tell you truly: if a good man or good woman filled as many three-thousand-fold great-thousand worlds as there are grains of sand in all those Ganges Rivers with the seven precious treasures and used them for giving, would the merit obtained be great?" Subhuti said: "Very great, World-Honored One." The Buddha told Subhuti: "If a good man or good woman receives and upholds from this sutra even as few as four lines of verse and explains them to others, this merit surpasses the former."

passages.text: 「復次，須菩提！隨說是經，乃至四句偈等，當知此處，一切世間，天、人、阿修羅，皆應供養，如佛塔廟。何況有人，盡能受持讀誦。須菩提！當知是人成就最上第一希有之法，若是經典所在之處，即為有佛，若尊重弟子。」
passages.translation_en: "Furthermore, Subhuti, wherever this sutra is spoken, even as few as four lines of verse, know that that place should be revered by all the world — by gods, humans, and asuras — as if it were a shrine of the Buddha. How much more so for one who can fully receive, uphold, read, and recite it. Subhuti, know that such a person achieves the supreme, foremost, and rarest of dharmas. Wherever this sutra is found, there the Buddha is present, and it should be honored as one would honor his revered disciples."

passages.text: 爾時，須菩提白佛言：「世尊！當何名此經？我等云何奉持？」佛告須菩提：「是經名為金剛般若波羅蜜，以是名字，汝當奉持。所以者何？須菩提！佛說般若波羅蜜，即非般若波羅蜜。是名般若波羅蜜。須菩提！於意云何？如來有所說法不？」須菩提白佛言：「世尊！如來無所說。」「須菩提！於意云何？三千大千世界所有微塵，是為多不？」須菩提言：「甚多，世尊！」「須菩提！諸微塵，如來說非微塵，是名微塵。
passages.translation_en: At that time, Subhuti addressed the Buddha: "World-Honored One, what should this sutra be called? How should we receive and uphold it?" The Buddha told Subhuti: "This sutra is called the Diamond Prajna Paramita. By this name you should receive and uphold it. Why? Subhuti, the Buddha has taught that Prajna Paramita is not Prajna Paramita; it is called Prajna Paramita. Subhuti, what do you think? Has the Tathagata spoken any Dharma?" Subhuti addressed the Buddha: "World-Honored One, the Tathagata has spoken nothing." "Subhuti, what do you think? Are the motes of dust in the three-thousand-fold great-thousand world many?" Subhuti said: "Very many, World-Honored One." "Subhuti, the Tathagata has taught that these motes of dust are not motes of dust; they are called motes of dust."

passages.text: 如來說：世界，非世界，是名世界。須菩提！於意云何？可以三十二相見如來不？」「不也，世尊！不可以三十二相得見如來。何以故？如來說：三十二相，即是非相，是名三十二相。」「須菩提！若有善男子、善女人，以恆河沙等身命布施；若復有人，於此經中，乃至受持四句偈等，為他人說，其福甚多！」。
passages.translation_en: The Tathagata says: a world is not a world, and is therefore called a world. Subhuti, what do you think? Can one perceive the Tathagata through the thirty-two physical marks? No, World-Honored One! One cannot perceive the Tathagata through the thirty-two marks. Why? Because what the Tathagata calls the thirty-two marks are not marks, and are therefore called the thirty-two marks. Subhuti, if a good man or good woman were to sacrifice as many lives as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, and another person were to receive and uphold even just four lines of verse from this sutra and explain them to others, the merit of the latter would be far greater.

passages.text: 爾時，須菩提聞說是經，深解義趣，涕淚悲泣，而白佛言：「希有世尊！佛說如是甚深經典，我從昔來所得慧眼，未曾得聞如是之經。世尊！若復有人，得聞是經，信心清淨，則生實相，當知是人，成就第一希有功德。世尊！是實相者，則是非相，是故如來說名實相。世尊！我今得聞如是經典，信解受持，不足為難；若當來世，後五百歲，其有眾生，得聞是經，信解受持，是人則為第一希有。何以故？此人無我相、無人相、無眾生相、無壽者相。
passages.translation_en: At that time, Subhuti, having heard the teaching of this sutra, deeply understood its meaning and purport. Moved to tears, he addressed the Buddha: How rare, World-Honored One! The Buddha has spoken such a profoundly deep sutra. Since I first attained the wisdom eye, I have never heard such a sutra as this. World-Honored One, if someone hears this sutra and gives rise to pure faith, that person will realize true reality. Know that such a person will achieve the most rare and foremost merit. World-Honored One, this true reality is not reality, and therefore the Tathagata calls it true reality. World-Honored One, it is not difficult for me now to hear this sutra, to believe, understand, receive, and uphold it. But in the future, in the last five hundred years, if there are beings who hear this sutra, believe, understand, receive, and uphold it, such persons will be most rare indeed. Why? Because they will be free of the mark of self, the mark of person, the mark of sentient being, and the mark of life span.

passages.text: 所以者何？我相，即是非相；人相、眾生相、壽者相，即是非相。何以故？離一切諸相，則名諸佛。」佛告須菩提：「如是，如是！若復有人，得聞是經，不驚、不怖、不畏，當知是人，甚為希有。何以故？須菩提！如來說：第一波羅蜜，即非第一波羅蜜，是名第一波羅蜜。須菩提！忍辱波羅蜜，如來說非忍辱波羅蜜。是名忍辱波羅密。何以故？須菩提！如我昔為歌利王割截身體，我於爾時，無我相、無人相、無眾生相、無壽者相。
passages.translation_en: Why is this? The mark of self is not a mark; the marks of person, sentient being, and life span are not marks. Why? Because to be free of all marks is to be called a buddha. The Buddha told Subhuti: So it is, so it is! If someone hears this sutra and is not alarmed, not frightened, not afraid, know that such a person is most rare. Why? Subhuti, what the Tathagata calls the first paramita is not the first paramita, and is therefore called the first paramita. Subhuti, the paramita of patience, the Tathagata says, is not the paramita of patience, and is therefore called the paramita of patience. Why? Subhuti, in the past, when King Kalinga cut my body to pieces, at that time I had no mark of self, no mark of person, no mark of sentient being, and no mark of life span.

passages.text: 何以故？我於往昔，節節支解時，若有我相、人相、眾生相、壽者相，應生瞋恨。須菩提！又念過去，於五百世，作忍辱仙人，於爾所世，無我相、無人相、無眾生相、無壽者相。是故須菩提！菩薩應離一切相，發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心。不應住色生心，不應住聲、香、味、觸、法生心，應生無所住心。若心有住，則為非住。」「是故佛說：菩薩心不應住色布施。須菩提！菩薩為利益一切眾生故，應如是布施。如來說：一切諸相，即是非相。
passages.translation_en: Why? In the past, when my body was being dismembered limb by limb, if I had held the marks of self, person, sentient being, or life span, I would have given rise to anger and hatred. Subhuti, I also recall that in the past, for five hundred lifetimes, I was the ascetic known as the Patient One. During all those lifetimes, I was free of the mark of self, the mark of person, the mark of sentient being, and the mark of life span. Therefore, Subhuti, a bodhisattva should leave behind all marks and give rise to the aspiration for anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. One should not give rise to a mind that dwells on form, nor should one give rise to a mind that dwells on sound, smell, taste, touch, or dharmas. One should give rise to a mind that dwells on nothing. If the mind dwells on anything, it does not truly dwell. Therefore the Buddha says: a bodhisattva's mind should not dwell on form when practicing generosity. Subhuti, a bodhisattva, for the benefit of all sentient beings, should practice generosity in this way. The Tathagata says: all marks are not marks.

passages.text: 又說：一切眾生，即非眾生。須菩提！如來是真語者、實語者、如語者、不誑語者、不異語者。」「須菩提！如來所得法，此法無實無虛。須菩提！若菩薩心住於法而行布施，如人入闇，則無所見；若菩薩心不住法而行布施，如人有目，日光明照，見種種色。」「須菩提！當來之世，若有善男子、善女人，能於此經，受持讀誦，則為如來，以佛智慧，悉知是人，悉見是人，皆得成就無量無邊功德。」。
passages.translation_en: And further says: all sentient beings are not sentient beings. Subhuti, the Tathagata is one who speaks truth, speaks reality, speaks things as they are, does not speak deceptively, and does not speak inconsistently. Subhuti, the dharma the Tathagata has attained is neither real nor unreal. Subhuti, if a bodhisattva practices generosity while the mind dwells on dharmas, it is like a person entering darkness — they cannot see anything. If a bodhisattva practices generosity while the mind does not dwell on dharmas, it is like a person with eyes in bright sunlight — they can see all manner of forms. Subhuti, in ages to come, if a good man or good woman is able to receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, the Tathagata, with his buddha-wisdom, will fully know and fully see that such a person will achieve immeasurable and boundless merit.

passages.text: 「須菩提！若有善男子、善女人，初日分以恆河沙等身布施，中日分復以恆河沙等身布施，後日分亦以恆河沙等身布施，如是無量百千萬億劫，以身布施；若復有人，聞此經典，信心不逆，其福勝彼，何況書寫、受持、讀誦、為人解說。」「須菩提！以要言之，是經有不可思議、不可稱量、無邊功德。如來為發大乘者說，為發最上乘者說。若有人能受持讀誦，廣為人說，如來悉知是人，悉見是人，皆得成就不可量、不可稱、無有邊、不可思議功德。
passages.translation_en: Subhuti, if a good man or good woman were to give away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges in the morning, give away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges at midday, and give away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges in the evening, and continued such bodily sacrifice for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas — yet if another person, upon hearing this sutra, gave rise to faith without opposition, that person's merit would surpass the former's, to say nothing of one who copies, receives, upholds, reads, recites, and explains it to others. Subhuti, to put it simply, this sutra possesses inconceivable, immeasurable, and boundless merit. The Tathagata has spoken it for those who have set out on the Great Vehicle, for those who have set out on the Supreme Vehicle. If there are those who can receive, uphold, read, and recite it, and widely explain it to others, the Tathagata will fully know and fully see that such persons will achieve immeasurable, incalculable, boundless, and inconceivable merit.

passages.text: 」「如是人等，則為荷擔如來阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。何以故？須菩提！若樂小法者，著我見、人見、眾生見、壽者見，則於此經不能聽受、讀誦，為人解說。」「須菩提！在在處處，若有此經，一切世間，天、人、阿修羅，所應供養；當知此處，則為是塔，皆應恭敬，作禮圍遶，以諸華香而散其處。」。
passages.translation_en: Such persons will bear the Tathagata's anuttara-samyak-sambodhi upon their shoulders. Why? Subhuti, those who delight in lesser teachings and cling to the view of self, the view of person, the view of sentient being, and the view of life span — such people cannot listen to, receive, read, or recite this sutra, nor explain it to others. Subhuti, wherever this sutra is found, all worlds of devas, humans, and asuras should make offerings there. Know that such a place is a sacred shrine. All should pay reverence, bow, and circumambulate it, and scatter flowers and incense upon it.

passages.text: 「復次，須菩提！善男子、善女人，受持讀誦此經，若為人輕賤，是人先世罪業，應墮惡道，以今世人輕賤故，先世罪業則為消滅，當得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。」「須菩提！我念過去無量阿僧祇劫，於燃燈佛前，得值八百四千萬億那由他諸佛，悉皆供養承事，無空過者；若復有人，於後末世，能受持讀誦此經，所得功德，於我所供養諸佛功德，百分不及一，千萬億分、乃至算數譬喻所不能及。」「須菩提！若善男子，善女人，於後末世，有受持讀誦此經，所得功德，我若具說者，或有人聞，心則狂亂，狐疑不信。須菩提！當知是經義不可思議，果報亦不可思議！」
passages.translation_en: Furthermore, Subhuti, if a good man or good woman receives, upholds, reads, and recites this sutra, yet is scorned and looked down upon by others, know that this person's karmic offenses from previous lives, which would have led to rebirth in evil realms, are being dissolved through the contempt suffered in this present life, and that person will attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, I recall that in the immeasurable asamkhyeya kalpas of the past, before the time of Dipankara Buddha, I encountered and made offerings to eighty-four billion nayutas of buddhas, serving each one without exception. Yet if someone in the final age can receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, the merit obtained will be a hundred times — a thousand, ten thousand, a billion times — greater than the merit of my offerings to all those buddhas, so great that no number, no calculation, no analogy can approach it. Subhuti, if I were to fully describe the merit that such a good man or good woman in the final age would obtain by receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting this sutra, there are those who, upon hearing it, would become bewildered, filled with doubt and disbelief. Subhuti, know that the meaning of this sutra is inconceivable, and its fruition is equally inconceivable!

passages.text: 爾時，須菩提白佛言：「世尊！善男子、善女人，發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心，云何應住？云何降伏其心？」佛告須菩提：「善男子、善女人，發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心者，當生如是心：我應滅度一切眾生。滅度一切眾生已，而無有一眾生實滅度者。何以故？須菩提！若菩薩有我相、人相、眾生相、壽者相，則非菩薩。所以者何？須菩提！實無有法，發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心者。
passages.translation_en: At that time, Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, if a good man or good woman gives rise to the aspiration for anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, how should they abide? How should they subdue their mind? The Buddha told Subhuti: A good man or good woman who gives rise to the aspiration for anuttara-samyak-sambodhi should give rise to this thought: I should bring all sentient beings to final nirvana. Yet when all sentient beings have been brought to final nirvana, in truth not a single sentient being has been brought to final nirvana. Why? Subhuti, if a bodhisattva holds the mark of self, the mark of person, the mark of sentient being, or the mark of life span, then that one is not a bodhisattva. Why is this? Subhuti, there is in reality no dharma called 'giving rise to the aspiration for anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.'

passages.text: 」「須菩提！於意云何？如來於燃燈佛所，有法得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提不？」「不也，世尊！如我解佛所說義，佛於燃燈佛所，無有法得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。」佛言：「如是，如是！須菩提！實無有法，如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。須菩提！若有法，如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提者，燃燈佛則不與我授記：『汝於來世，當得作佛，號釋迦牟尼。』以實無有法得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提，是故燃燈佛與我授記，作是言：『汝於來世，當得作佛，號釋迦牟尼。
passages.translation_en: Subhuti, what do you think? When the Tathagata was with Dipankara Buddha, was there any dharma through which he attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi? No, World-Honored One! As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has said, when the Buddha was with Dipankara Buddha, there was no dharma through which he attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. The Buddha said: So it is, so it is! Subhuti, there is in reality no dharma through which the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, if there were any dharma through which the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, then Dipankara Buddha would not have given me the prediction: 'In a future life, you shall become a buddha named Shakyamuni.' It is precisely because there is no dharma through which one attains anuttara-samyak-sambodhi that Dipankara Buddha gave me the prediction, saying: 'In a future life, you shall become a buddha named Shakyamuni.'

passages.text: 』何以故？如來者，即諸法如義。」「若有人言：如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。須菩提！實無有法，佛得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。須菩提！如來所得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提，於是中無實無虛。是故如來說：一切法皆是佛法。須菩提！所言一切法者，即非一切法，是故名一切法。」「須菩提！譬如人身長大。」須菩提言：「世尊！如來說：人身長大，則為非大身，是名大身。」「須菩提！菩薩亦如是。若作是言：我當滅度無量眾生，則不名菩薩。
passages.translation_en: Why is this? 'Tathagata' means the suchness of all dharmas. If someone says that the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi — Subhuti, in reality there is no dharma through which the Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, the anuttara-samyak-sambodhi that the Tathagata attained is, in this, neither real nor unreal. Therefore the Tathagata says: all dharmas are buddha-dharma. Subhuti, what are called 'all dharmas' are not all dharmas, and are therefore called all dharmas. Subhuti, it is like a person with a great body. Subhuti said: World-Honored One, what the Tathagata calls a great body is not a great body, and is therefore called a great body. Subhuti, it is the same for a bodhisattva. If a bodhisattva says, 'I shall bring immeasurable sentient beings to final nirvana,' then that one is not a bodhisattva.

passages.text: 何以故？須菩提！實無有法名為菩薩。是故佛說一切法，無我、無人、無眾生、無壽者。」「須菩提！若菩薩作是言：『我當莊嚴佛土』，是不名菩薩。何以故？如來說：莊嚴佛土者，即非莊嚴，是名莊嚴。」「須菩提！若菩薩通達無我、法者，如來說名真是菩薩。」。
passages.translation_en: Why? Subhuti, there is in reality no dharma called 'bodhisattva.' Therefore the Buddha says that all dharmas are without self, without person, without sentient being, without life span. Subhuti, if a bodhisattva says, 'I shall adorn buddha-lands,' that one is not a bodhisattva. Why? What the Tathagata calls adorning buddha-lands is not adorning, and is therefore called adorning. Subhuti, if a bodhisattva thoroughly comprehends the selflessness of self and dharmas, the Tathagata calls that one a true bodhisattva.

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？如來有肉眼不？」「如是，世尊！如來有肉眼。」「須菩提！於意云何？如來有天眼不？」「如是，世尊！如來有天眼。」「須菩提！於意云何？如來有慧眼不？」「如是，世尊！如來有慧眼。」「須菩提！於意云何？如來有法眼不？」「如是，世尊！如來有法眼。」「須菩提！於意云何？如來有佛眼不？」「如是，世尊！如來有佛眼。」「須菩提！於意云何？如恆河中所有沙，佛說是沙不？」「如是，世尊！如來說是沙。
passages.translation_en: Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the fleshly eye? Yes, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the fleshly eye. Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the divine eye? Yes, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the divine eye. Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the wisdom eye? Yes, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the wisdom eye. Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the dharma eye? Yes, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the dharma eye. Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the buddha eye? Yes, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the buddha eye. Subhuti, what do you think? Has the Buddha said that the grains of sand in the Ganges River are sand? Yes, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has said they are sand.

passages.text: 」「須菩提！於意云何？如一恆河中所有沙，有如是沙等恆河，是諸恆河所有沙數，佛世界如是，寧為多不？」「甚多，世尊。」佛告須菩提：「爾所國土中，所有眾生，若干種心，如來悉知。何以故？如來說：諸心皆為非心，是名為心。所以者何？須菩提！過去心不可得，現在心不可得，未來心不可得。」。
passages.translation_en: Subhuti, what do you think? If there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, and the buddha-worlds were as numerous as all the grains of sand in all those Ganges Rivers, would that be many? Very many, World-Honored One. The Buddha told Subhuti: Within all those lands, every mind of every sentient being, in all its variety, is fully known to the Tathagata. Why? What the Tathagata calls minds are not minds, and are therefore called minds. Why is this? Subhuti, the past mind cannot be grasped, the present mind cannot be grasped, and the future mind cannot be grasped.

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？若有人滿三千大千世界七寶，以用布施，是人以是因緣，得福多不？」「如是，世尊！此人以是因緣，得福甚多。」「須菩提！若福德有實，如來不說得福德多；以福德無故，如來說得福德多。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? If someone filled the three thousand great thousand worlds with the seven treasures and used them for giving, would that person gain much merit from this cause?" "Indeed so, World-Honored One! This person would gain very much merit from this cause." "Subhuti, if merit were something real, the Tathagata would not say that much merit is gained. It is because merit is without substance that the Tathagata says much merit is gained."

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？佛可以具足色身見不？」「不也，世尊！如來不應以具足色身見。何以故？如來說：具足色身，即非具足色身，是名具足色身。」「須菩提！於意云何？如來可以具足諸相見不？」「不也，世尊！如來不應以具足諸相見。何以故？如來說：諸相具足，即非具足。是名諸相具足。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Buddha be seen through his complete physical form?" "No, World-Honored One! The Tathagata should not be seen through his complete physical form. Why? Because what the Tathagata calls the complete physical form is not the complete physical form — it is merely called the complete physical form." "Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be seen through the perfection of all marks?" "No, World-Honored One! The Tathagata should not be seen through the perfection of all marks. Why? Because what the Tathagata calls the perfection of all marks is not truly perfection — it is merely called the perfection of all marks."

passages.text: 「須菩提！汝勿謂如來作是念：『我當有所說法。』莫作是念。何以故？若人言：如來有所說法，即為謗佛，不能解我所說故。須菩提！說法者，無法可說，是名說法。」爾時，慧命須菩提白佛言：「世尊！頗有眾生，於未來世，聞說是法，生信心不？」佛言：「須菩提！彼非眾生，非不眾生。何以故？須菩提！眾生眾生者，如來說非眾生，是名眾生。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, do not say that the Tathagata has this thought: 'I have something to teach.' Do not think this way. Why? If someone says the Tathagata has something to teach, that person slanders the Buddha and cannot understand what I have said. Subhuti, teaching the Dharma means there is no Dharma to teach — this is called teaching the Dharma." At that time, the wise Subhuti addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One! Will there be beings in the future who, hearing this teaching, give rise to faith?" The Buddha said: "Subhuti, they are neither beings nor non-beings. Why? Subhuti, what is called 'beings' — the Tathagata says they are not beings; they are merely called beings."

passages.text: 須菩提白佛言：「世尊！佛得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。為無所得耶？」佛言：「如是，如是。須菩提！我於阿耨多羅三藐三菩提乃至無有少法可得，是名阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。」
passages.translation_en: Subhuti addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One! When the Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, was there truly nothing attained?" The Buddha said: "Just so, just so. Subhuti, with regard to anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, there is not even the slightest dharma to be attained. This is what is called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi."

passages.text: 「復次，須菩提！是法平等，無有高下，是名『阿耨多羅三藐三菩提』；以無我、無人、無眾生、無壽者，修一切善法，則得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。須菩提！所言善法者，如來說即非善法，是名善法。」
passages.translation_en: "Furthermore, Subhuti, this Dharma is equal and without high or low. This is what is called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. By cultivating all wholesome dharmas with no self, no person, no being, and no one who lives a lifespan, one attains anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, what are called wholesome dharmas — the Tathagata says they are not wholesome dharmas; they are merely called wholesome dharmas."

passages.text: 「須菩提！若三千大千世界中，所有諸須彌山王，如是等七寶聚，有人持用布施；若人以此《般若波羅蜜經》，乃至四句偈等，受持讀誦，為他人說，於前福德百分不及一，百千萬億分、乃至算數譬喻所不能及。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if someone gathered together heaps of the seven treasures equal in number to all the Mount Sumerus in the three thousand great thousand worlds and used them for giving; and if another person received, upheld, read, and recited even as few as four lines of verse from this Prajnaparamita Sutra and explained it to others — the merit of the former would not equal even one hundredth, one billionth, nor any fraction reachable by calculation or analogy of the latter."

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？汝等勿謂如來作是念：『我當度眾生。』須菩提！莫作是念。何以故？實無有眾生如來度者。若有眾生如來度者，如來則有我、人、眾生、壽者。須菩提！如來說：『有我者，則非有我，而凡夫之人以為有我。』須菩提！凡夫者，如來說則非凡夫，是名凡夫。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? You should not say that the Tathagata has this thought: 'I shall deliver sentient beings.' Subhuti, do not think this way. Why? There are in truth no sentient beings for the Tathagata to deliver. If there were sentient beings for the Tathagata to deliver, then the Tathagata would have a self, a person, a being, and one who lives a lifespan. Subhuti, when the Tathagata speaks of 'having a self,' it is not truly having a self, yet ordinary people take it as having a self. Subhuti, as for ordinary people — the Tathagata says they are not ordinary people; they are merely called ordinary people."

passages.text: 「須菩提！於意云何？可以三十二相觀如來不？」須菩提言：「如是！如是！以三十二相觀如來。」佛言：「須菩提！若以三十二相觀如來者，轉輪聖王則是如來。」須菩提白佛言：「世尊！如我解佛所說義。不應以三十二相觀如來。」爾時，世尊而說偈言：「若以色見我，以音聲求我，是人行邪道，不能見如來。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be perceived through the thirty-two marks?" Subhuti said: "Yes! Yes! The Tathagata can be perceived through the thirty-two marks." The Buddha said: "Subhuti, if the Tathagata could be perceived through the thirty-two marks, then a wheel-turning sage king would be a Tathagata." Subhuti addressed the Buddha: "World-Honored One! As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has said, one should not perceive the Tathagata through the thirty-two marks." At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this verse: "If one seeks me through form, or seeks me through sound, this person walks a misguided path and cannot see the Tathagata."

passages.text: 「須菩提！汝若作是念：『如來不以具足相故，得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。』須菩提！莫作是念：『如來不以具足相故，得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。』」「須菩提！汝若作是念，發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心者，說諸法斷滅。莫作是念！何以故？發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心者。於法不說斷滅相。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if you have this thought: 'The Tathagata did not attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi by means of the perfection of marks' — Subhuti, do not think this way: 'The Tathagata did not attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi by means of the perfection of marks.'" "Subhuti, if you have this thought, then one who aspires to anuttara-samyak-sambodhi would be declaring all dharmas to be annihilated. Do not think this way! Why? One who aspires to anuttara-samyak-sambodhi does not declare the mark of annihilation regarding any dharma."

passages.text: 「須菩提！若菩薩以滿恆河沙等世界七寶持用布施；若復有人，知一切法無我，得成於忍，此菩薩勝前菩薩所得功德。何以故？須菩提！以諸菩薩不受福德故。」須菩提白佛言：「世尊！云何菩薩不受福德？」「須菩提！菩薩所作福德，不應貪著。是故說不受福德。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if a bodhisattva used the seven treasures filling worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges for giving; and if another person, knowing that all dharmas are without self, perfected patience — this bodhisattva's merit would surpass that of the former. Why? Subhuti, because bodhisattvas do not cling to merit." Subhuti addressed the Buddha: "World-Honored One, how is it that bodhisattvas do not cling to merit?" "Subhuti, a bodhisattva should not be attached to the merit they create. Therefore it is said they do not cling to merit."

passages.text: 「須菩提！若有人言：如來若來若去，若坐若臥，是人不解我所說義。何以故？如來者，無所從來，亦無所去，故名如來。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if someone says that the Tathagata comes or goes, sits or lies down, this person does not understand the meaning of what I have said. Why? The Tathagata has nowhere from which he comes and nowhere to which he goes. Therefore he is called the Tathagata."

passages.text: 「須菩提！若善男子、善女人，以三千大千世界碎為微塵，於意云何？是微塵眾寧為多不？」須菩提言「甚多，世尊！何以故？若是微塵眾實有者，佛則不說是微塵眾。所以者何？佛說微塵眾，則非微塵眾，是名微塵眾。」「世尊！如來所說三千大千世界，則非世界，是名世界。何以故？若世界實有者，則是一合相。如來說一合相，則非一合相，是名一合相。」「須菩提！一合相者，則是不可說；但凡夫之人貪著其事。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if a good man or good woman were to grind the three thousand great thousand worlds into fine dust, what do you think — would that mass of fine dust be great?" Subhuti said: "Very great, World-Honored One! Why? If that mass of fine dust were truly real, the Buddha would not call it a mass of fine dust. Why is this? What the Buddha calls a mass of fine dust is not a mass of fine dust — it is merely called a mass of fine dust." "World-Honored One! What the Tathagata calls the three thousand great thousand worlds is not a world — it is merely called a world. Why? If a world were truly real, it would be a composite unity. What the Tathagata calls a composite unity is not a composite unity — it is merely called a composite unity." "Subhuti, a composite unity is something that cannot be spoken of; yet ordinary people are greedily attached to such things."

passages.text: 「須菩提！若人言：佛說我見、人見、眾生見、壽者見。須菩提！於意云何？是人解我所說義不？」「不也，世尊！是人不解如來所說義。何以故？世尊說我見、人見、眾生見、壽者見，即非我見、人見、眾生見、壽者見，是名我見、人見、眾生見、壽者見。」「須菩提！發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心者，於一切法，應如是知，如是見，如是信解，不生法相。須菩提！所言法相者，如來說即非法相，是名法相。」
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if someone says the Buddha teaches the view of self, the view of person, the view of being, and the view of one who lives a lifespan — Subhuti, what do you think? Does this person understand the meaning of what I have said?" "No, World-Honored One! This person does not understand the meaning of what the Tathagata has said. Why? The World-Honored One's teaching of the view of self, the view of person, the view of being, and the view of one who lives a lifespan — these are not the view of self, the view of person, the view of being, and the view of one who lives a lifespan. They are merely called the view of self, the view of person, the view of being, and the view of one who lives a lifespan." "Subhuti, one who aspires to anuttara-samyak-sambodhi should know all dharmas thus, see them thus, understand and believe them thus, without giving rise to the mark of dharmas. Subhuti, what is called the mark of dharmas — the Tathagata says it is not the mark of dharmas; it is merely called the mark of dharmas."

passages.text: 「須菩提！若有人以滿無量阿僧祇世界七寶，持用布施；若有善男子、善女人，發菩提心者，持於此經，乃至四句偈等，受持讀誦，為人演說，其福勝彼。云何為人演說，不取於相，如如不動。何以故？」「一切有為法，如夢幻泡影，如露亦如電，應作如是觀。」佛說是經已，長老須菩提及諸比丘、比丘尼、優婆塞、優婆夷、一切世間天、人、阿修羅，聞佛所說，皆大歡喜，信受奉行。
passages.translation_en: "Subhuti, if someone used the seven treasures filling immeasurable asamkhya worlds for giving; and if a good man or good woman who has aspired to the bodhi mind upheld even as few as four lines of verse from this sutra, received, upheld, read, and recited it, and explained it to others — the merit of the latter would surpass the former. How should one explain it to others? By not grasping at appearances, remaining in thusness, unmoving. Why?" "All conditioned phenomena are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows; like dew and like lightning — one should contemplate them thus." When the Buddha finished speaking this sutra, the elder Subhuti, along with all the monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, and all the beings of the world — devas, humans, and asuras — having heard what the Buddha taught, all rejoiced greatly, and faithfully received and practiced it.

時，大師至寶林。韶州韋刺史（名璩）與官僚入山請師，出於城中大梵寺講堂，為眾開緣說法。師陞座次，刺史官僚三十餘人，儒宗學士三十餘人，僧尼道俗一千餘人，同時作禮，願聞法要。
大師告眾曰：「善知識！菩提自性，本來清淨，但用此心，直了成佛。善知識！且聽惠能行由，得法事意。惠能嚴父，本貫范陽，左降流于嶺南，作新州百姓。此身不幸，父又早亡。老母孤遺，移來南海，艱辛貧乏，於市賣柴。
passages.translation_en:
At that time, the Great Master arrived at Baolin Monastery. Magistrate Wei of Shaozhou (given name Qu) and his officials entered the mountain to invite the Master. They went to the lecture hall of Dafan Temple in the city, where the Master would expound the Dharma for the assembly. When the Master ascended the seat, over thirty officials, over thirty Confucian scholars and literati, and over a thousand monks, nuns, Taoists, and laypeople all bowed together, wishing to hear the essentials of the Dharma.
The Great Master addressed the assembly: 'Good friends! The bodhi-nature is originally pure in itself. Simply use this mind, and you can directly realize Buddhahood. Good friends, listen now to how Huineng came to the Dharma. My late father was originally from Fanyang. He was demoted and banished to Lingnan, becoming a commoner of Xinzhou. My life was unfortunate — my father died early. My widowed mother and I, left alone, moved to Nanhai, where we endured hardship and poverty, and I sold firewood at the market.'

passages.text: 時，有一客買柴，使令送至客店；客收去，惠能得錢，却出門外，見一客誦經。惠能一聞經語，心即開悟，遂問：『客誦何經？』客曰：『《金剛經》。』復問：『從何所來，持此經典？』客云：『我從蘄州黃梅縣東禪寺來。其寺是五祖忍大師在彼主化，門人一千有餘；我到彼中禮拜，聽受此經。大師常勸僧俗，但持《金剛經》，即自見性，直了成佛。』惠能聞說，宿昔有緣，乃蒙一客，取銀十兩與惠能，令充老母衣糧，教便往黃梅參禮五祖。
passages.translation_en: At that time, a customer bought firewood and had me deliver it to his lodging. After the customer took the firewood and I received my payment, I went out the door and encountered another man reciting a sutra. The moment I heard the words of the sutra, my mind was opened to awakening. I asked, 'What sutra are you reciting?' The man said, 'The Diamond Sutra.' I asked further, 'Where have you come from, carrying this scripture?' He replied, 'I come from Dongchan Monastery in Huangmei County, Qizhou. The Fifth Patriarch, Great Master Hongren, presides there, with over a thousand disciples. I went there to pay my respects and received this sutra. The Master constantly urges both monks and laypeople to simply uphold the Diamond Sutra, and they will see their own nature and directly realize Buddhahood.' Hearing this, I felt a karmic connection from past lives. Then a patron gave me ten taels of silver for my mother's clothing and provisions, and told me to go to Huangmei to pay respects to the Fifth Patriarch.

passages.text: 「惠能安置母畢，即便辭違。不經三十餘日，便至黃梅，禮拜五祖。祖問曰：『汝何方人？欲求何物？』惠能對曰：『弟子是嶺南新州百姓，遠來禮師，惟求作佛，不求餘物。』祖言：『汝是嶺南人，又是獵獠，若為堪作佛？』惠能曰：『人雖有南北，佛性本無南北；獵獠身與和尚不同，佛性有何差別？』五祖更欲與語，且見徒眾總在左右，乃令隨眾作務。惠能曰：『惠能啟和尚，弟子自心，常生智慧，不離自性，即是福田。
passages.translation_en: After Huineng had settled his mother, he immediately set out. In less than thirty-some days, he arrived at Huangmei and paid respects to the Fifth Patriarch. The Patriarch asked, 'Where are you from? What do you seek?' Huineng replied, 'Your disciple is a commoner from Xinzhou in Lingnan. I have come from afar to pay respects to the Master. I seek only to become a Buddha — nothing else.' The Patriarch said, 'You are from Lingnan, and a barbarian besides. How could you possibly become a Buddha?' Huineng said, 'Although people are from the south or north, the Buddha-nature fundamentally has no south or north. The body of a barbarian and that of a monk may differ, but what difference is there in the Buddha-nature?' The Fifth Patriarch wished to continue the conversation, but seeing that his followers were all standing nearby, he ordered Huineng to join the group and work. Huineng said, 'May I say to the Master: my own mind constantly gives rise to wisdom. To never depart from one's own nature — that itself is the field of merit.

passages.text: 末審和尚教作何務？』祖云：『這獦獠根性大利！汝更勿言，著槽廠去。』惠能退至後院，有一行者，差惠能破柴踏碓。經八月餘，祖一日忽見惠能曰：『吾思汝之見可用，恐有惡人害汝，遂不與汝言。汝知之否？』惠能曰：『弟子亦知師意，不敢行至堂前，令人不覺。
passages.translation_en: May I ask what work the Master would have me do?' The Patriarch said, 'This barbarian has sharp roots indeed! Say no more — go to the threshing floor.' Huineng withdrew to the rear yard, where a lay worker assigned him to split firewood and pound rice. After more than eight months, the Patriarch came upon Huineng one day and said, 'I have thought that your understanding could be of use, but I feared that evil people might harm you, so I did not speak with you. Did you know this?' Huineng said, 'Your disciple understood the Master's intention, and so dared not walk to the front hall, lest anyone take notice.'

「祖一日喚諸門人總來：『吾向汝說，世人生死事大，汝等終日只求福田，不求出離生死苦海；自性若迷，福何可救？汝等各去，自看智慧，取自本心般若之性，各作一偈，來呈吾看。若悟大意，付汝衣法，為第六代祖。火急速去，不得遲滯，思量即不中用；見性之人，言下須見。若如此者，輪刀上陣，亦得見之。』眾得處分，退而遞相謂曰：『我等眾人，不須澄心用意作偈，將呈和尚，有何所益？神秀上座，現為教授師，必是他得。
passages.translation_en: One day the Patriarch summoned all his disciples and said, 'Let me tell you: the matter of birth and death is the great concern of worldly beings. Yet all day long you only seek the field of merit and do not seek to escape the bitter sea of birth and death. If your own nature is deluded, how can merit save you? Each of you, go and look into your own wisdom. Take the prajna-nature of your original mind and each compose a verse. Bring it to me. If one of you awakens to the great meaning, I will transmit the robe and Dharma to you, making you the Sixth Patriarch. Go quickly! Do not delay! Deliberation is useless in this matter. One who sees their nature must see it the instant the words are spoken. One who can do this could see it even while wielding a sword in battle.' The assembly, having received these instructions, withdrew and said to one another, 'We in the assembly need not bother calming our minds to compose a verse and present it to the Master — what good would it do? Senior monk Shenxiu is currently the head instructor. It must surely be he who will receive it.

passages.translation_en:
It would be presumptuous of us to compose verses — a waste of effort.' The rest, hearing this, all gave up the idea and said, 'From now on we will simply follow Master Shenxiu. Why trouble ourselves composing verses?' Shenxiu thought to himself, 'The others are not submitting verses because I am their instructor. I must compose a verse and present it to the Master. If I do not, how will the Master know the depth of my understanding? My intention in presenting a verse — if it is to seek the Dharma, that is good; if it is to claim the patriarchship, that is wrong, no different from a worldly mind grasping at a holy position. But if I do not present a verse, I will never receive the Dharma. How difficult! How difficult!'
In front of the Fifth Patriarch's hall there was a corridor of three bays. The Patriarch had planned to commission the court artist Lu Zhen to paint scenes from the Lankavatara Sutra and a lineage chart of the five patriarchs, to be displayed for veneration.
