神秀作偈成已，數度欲呈，行至堂前，心中恍惚，遍身汗流，擬呈不得；前後經四日，一十三度呈偈不得。秀乃思惟：『不如向廊下書著，從他和尚看見，忽若道好，即出禮拜，云是秀作；若道不堪，枉向山中數年，受人禮拜，更修何道？』是夜三更，不使人知，自執燈，書偈於南廊壁間，呈心所見。偈曰：
身是菩提樹，心如明鏡臺，時時勤拂拭，勿使惹塵埃。
「秀書偈了，便却歸房，人總不知。
passages.translation_en:
After Shenxiu finished composing his verse, he tried to present it several times. Each time he walked to the hall, his mind became dazed, his whole body broke out in sweat, and he could not bring himself to submit it. Over four days, he attempted thirteen times without success. Then Shenxiu thought, 'It would be better to write it on the corridor wall and let the Master see it for himself. If he says it is good, I will come forward, bow, and say that I, Shenxiu, wrote it. If he says it is no good, then I have wasted years in these mountains receiving people's reverence for nothing — and what further cultivation should I pursue?' That night, at the third watch, telling no one, he took a lamp and wrote his verse on the wall of the south corridor, expressing what his mind had seen. The verse said:
The body is the bodhi tree, / The mind is like a bright mirror's stand. / At all times diligently polish it — / Do not let it gather dust.
After writing the verse, Shenxiu returned to his room, and no one knew.

passages.text:
秀復思惟：『五祖明日見偈歡喜，即我與法有緣；若言不堪，自是我迷，宿業障重，不合得法。』聖意難測，房中思想，坐臥不安，直至五更。祖已知神秀入門未得，不見自性。
「天明，祖喚盧供奉來，向南廊壁間，繪畫圖相，忽見其偈，報言：『供奉却不用畫，勞爾遠來。經云：「凡所有相，皆是虛妄。」但留此偈，與人誦持。依此偈修，免墮惡道；依此偈修，有大利益。』令門人炷香禮敬，盡誦此偈，即得見性。門人誦偈，皆歎善哉。
passages.translation_en:
Shenxiu thought further: 'If the Fifth Patriarch sees the verse tomorrow and is pleased, then I have an affinity with the Dharma. If he says it is no good, then I am deluded, my past karma is heavy, and I am not fit to receive the Dharma.' The sage's intention was hard to fathom. In his room, Shenxiu turned the matter over in his mind, sitting and lying in unease, all the way until the fifth watch. The Patriarch already knew that Shenxiu had not yet entered the gate and had not seen his own nature.
At dawn, the Patriarch called for the artist Lu and went to the south corridor wall to have the murals painted. Suddenly he saw the verse. He said to Lu, 'There is no need to paint after all. I am sorry you have come so far. The scripture says: "All that has form is illusory." Let us keep this verse instead, for people to recite and uphold. Those who practice according to this verse will avoid falling into evil destinies; those who practice according to this verse will gain great benefit.' He ordered the community to light incense, pay respect, and recite the verse, so that they might see their own nature. The disciples recited the verse and all exclaimed, 'Excellent!'

passages.text: 「祖，三更喚秀入堂，問曰：『偈是汝作否？』秀言：『實是秀作，不敢妄求祖位，望和尚慈悲，看弟子有少智慧否？』祖曰：『汝作此偈，未見本性，只到門外，未入門內。如此見解，覓無上菩提，了不可得；無上菩提，須得言下識自本心，見自本性不生不滅；於一切時中，念念自見萬法無滯，一真一切真，萬境自如如。如如之心，即是真實。若如是見，即是無上菩薩之自性也。
passages.translation_en: At the third watch, the Patriarch summoned Shenxiu into the hall and asked, 'Did you write that verse?' Shenxiu said, 'It was indeed written by Shenxiu. I dare not presume to seek the patriarchship. I only hope the Master, in his compassion, will judge whether your disciple has some small wisdom.' The Patriarch said, 'This verse of yours shows that you have not yet seen your original nature. You have reached the gate but have not entered it. With such understanding, you cannot attain supreme bodhi. Supreme bodhi requires that in the very moment of hearing the words, you recognize your original mind and see your original nature — which is neither born nor destroyed. At all times, in every thought, you see for yourself that the myriad dharmas are unobstructed. The one truth is all truth, and all things are just as they are. The mind of suchness — that is the real. If you see in this way, that is the self-nature of supreme bodhi.

passages.text:
汝且去，一兩日思惟，更作一偈，將來吾看；汝偈若入得門，付汝衣法。』神秀作禮而出。又經數日，作偈不成，心中恍惚，神思不安，猶如夢中，行坐不樂。
「復兩日，有一童子於碓坊過，唱誦其偈；惠能一聞，便知此偈未見本性，雖未蒙教授，早識大意。遂問童子曰：『誦者何偈？』童子曰：『爾這獵獠不知，大師言：「世人生死事大，欲得傳付衣法，令門人作偈來看。若悟大意，即付衣法為第六祖。
passages.translation_en:
Go now, and think for a day or two. Compose another verse and bring it to me. If your verse shows that you have entered the gate, I will transmit the robe and Dharma to you.' Shenxiu bowed and left. Several more days passed, but he could not compose a verse. His mind was dazed, his spirit unsettled, as if in a dream — whether walking or sitting, he found no peace.
Two days later, a young attendant passed through the rice-pounding room, chanting Shenxiu's verse. The moment Huineng heard it, he knew this verse had not penetrated to the original nature. Although he had received no formal instruction, he already grasped the essential meaning. He asked the boy, 'What verse is that you are chanting?' The boy said, 'You barbarian, you know nothing! The Great Master said that birth and death is the great matter of life. Wishing to transmit the robe and Dharma, he ordered his disciples to compose verses. If one awakens to the great meaning, the robe and Dharma will be transmitted, making that person the Sixth Patriarch.

passages.text: 」神秀上座，於南廊壁上，書無相偈，大師令人皆誦，依此偈修，免墮惡道；依此偈修，有大利益。』惠能曰：『上人！我此踏碓，八箇餘月，未曾行到堂前。望上人引至偈前禮拜。』童子引至偈前禮拜，惠能曰：『惠能不識字，請上人為讀。』時，有江州別駕，姓張名日用，便高聲讀。惠能聞已，遂言：『亦有一偈，望別駕為書。』別駕言：『汝亦作偈？其事希有。』惠能向別駕言：『欲學無上菩提，不得輕於初學。
passages.translation_en: Senior monk Shenxiu wrote this formless verse on the south corridor wall. The Great Master ordered everyone to recite it, saying that those who practice according to this verse will avoid evil destinies, and those who practice according to it will gain great benefit.' Huineng said, 'Sir, I have been pounding rice here for over eight months and have never once gone to the front hall. I beg you to lead me to the verse so I may pay my respects.' The boy led him to the verse, where Huineng bowed. Huineng said, 'I cannot read. Would you please read it for me?' At that time, there was a vice-prefect from Jiangzhou, surnamed Zhang, given name Riyong, who read it aloud. After hearing it, Huineng said, 'I also have a verse. Would the vice-prefect write it down for me?' The vice-prefect said, 'You — composing a verse? That would be extraordinary indeed!' Huineng said to the vice-prefect, 'If you wish to attain supreme bodhi, do not look down on a beginner.

passages.text:
下下人有上上智，上上人有沒意智。若輕人，即有無量無邊罪。』別駕言：『汝但誦偈，吾為汝書。汝若得法，先須度吾。勿忘此言。』惠能偈曰：
菩提本無樹，明鏡亦非臺；本來無一物，何處惹塵埃？
「書此偈已，徒眾總驚，無不嗟訝，各相謂言：『奇哉！不得以貌取人，何得多時，使他肉身菩薩。』祖見眾人驚怪，恐人損害，遂將鞋擦了偈，曰：『亦未見性。』眾以為然。
passages.translation_en:
The lowest of people may have the highest wisdom, and the highest of people may lack all discernment. If you look down on others, you incur boundless, immeasurable transgression.' The vice-prefect said, 'Just recite your verse and I will write it for you. If you attain the Dharma, you must liberate me first. Do not forget these words.' Huineng's verse said:
Bodhi is originally no tree, / Nor is the bright mirror a stand. / Originally there is not a single thing — / Where could dust alight?
When this verse was written, the entire assembly was astounded. They marveled to one another, 'How extraordinary! One cannot judge a person by appearance. How is it that in so short a time, he has become a living bodhisattva?' The Patriarch, seeing the assembly's shock and fearing someone might harm Huineng, wiped the verse away with his shoe and said, 'This too has not yet seen the nature.' The assembly accepted this.

passages.text: 「次日，祖潛至碓坊，見能腰石舂米，語曰：『求道之人，為法忘軀，當如是乎！』乃問曰：『米熟也未？』惠能曰：『米熟久矣，猶欠篩在。』祖以杖擊碓三下而去。惠能即會祖意，三鼓入室；祖以袈裟遮圍，不令人見，為說《金剛經》。至『應無所住而生其心』，惠能言下大悟，一切萬法，不離自性。遂啟祖言：『何期自性，本自清淨；何期自性，本不生滅；何期自性，本自具足；何期自性，本無動搖；何期自性，能生萬法。
passages.translation_en: The next day, the Patriarch came secretly to the rice-pounding room and saw Huineng with a stone tied to his waist, pounding rice. He said, 'A seeker of the Way, forgetting his body for the Dharma — should it not be just so!' Then he asked, 'Is the rice ready yet?' Huineng replied, 'The rice has been ready for a long time — it still needs sifting.' The Patriarch tapped the mortar three times with his staff and left. Huineng immediately understood the Patriarch's meaning. At the third watch, he entered the Patriarch's chamber. The Patriarch used his kashaya robe as a screen so that no one could see, and expounded the Diamond Sutra. When he reached the passage 'Give rise to a mind that abides nowhere,' Huineng was instantly and completely awakened: all the myriad dharmas are inseparable from one's own nature. He said to the Patriarch: 'Who would have thought that the self-nature is originally pure! Who would have thought that the self-nature is originally neither born nor destroyed! Who would have thought that the self-nature is originally complete in itself! Who would have thought that the self-nature is originally without agitation! Who would have thought that the self-nature can give rise to all dharmas!'

passages.text:
』祖知悟本性，謂惠能曰：『不識本心，學法無益；若識自本心，見自本性，即名丈夫、天人師、佛。』三更受法，人盡不知，便傳頓教及衣鉢，云：『汝為第六代祖，善自護念，廣度有情，流布將來，無令斷絕。聽吾偈曰：
有情來下種，因地果還生，無情既無種，無性亦無生。
「祖復曰：『昔達磨大師，初來此土，人未之信，故傳此衣，以為信體，代代相承；法則以心傳心，皆令自悟自解。
passages.translation_en:
The Patriarch, knowing that Huineng had awakened to the original nature, said to him, 'If you do not recognize your original mind, studying the Dharma is of no benefit. If you recognize your original mind and see your original nature, then you are called a great person, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha.' At the third watch the Dharma was transmitted, and no one knew. The Patriarch also passed on the Sudden Teaching, along with the robe and bowl, saying, 'You are now the Sixth Patriarch. Guard your thoughts well, liberate sentient beings far and wide, and spread the teaching into the future so that it will not be cut off. Listen to my verse:
With sentient beings, a seed is sown; / From this ground, the fruit is born. / Without sentience there is no seed; / Without a nature, there is no birth.'
The Patriarch also said, 'Long ago, when the Great Master Bodhidharma first came to this land, people did not yet trust him. Therefore this robe was transmitted as a token of faith, passed down from generation to generation. But the Dharma is transmitted mind to mind, each person arriving at their own awakening and understanding.

passages.text: 自古，佛佛惟傳本體，師師密付本心；衣為爭端，止汝勿傳。若傳此衣，命如懸絲。汝須速去，恐人害汝。』惠能啟曰：『向甚處去？』祖云：『逢懷則止，遇會則藏。』惠能三更領得衣鉢，云：『能本是南中人，素不知此山路，如何出得江口？』五祖言：『汝不須憂，吾自送汝。』祖相送，直至九江驛。祖令上船，五祖把艣自搖。惠能言：『請和尚坐。弟子合搖艣。』祖云：『合是吾渡汝。』惠能云：『迷時師度，悟了自度；度名雖一，用處不同。
passages.translation_en: Since ancient times, Buddha has only transmitted the original essence, and master has only secretly entrusted the original mind. The robe has become a source of contention — let it stop with you; do not transmit it further. If you pass on this robe, your life will hang by a thread. You must leave quickly, for I fear someone may harm you.' Huineng asked, 'Where should I go?' The Patriarch said, 'Stop when you reach Huai; hide when you encounter Hui.' Huineng received the robe and bowl at the third watch and said, 'I am originally a southerner and do not know these mountain paths. How do I reach the river crossing?' The Fifth Patriarch said, 'Do not worry — I will escort you myself.' The Patriarch accompanied him all the way to the Jiujiang courier station and told him to board a boat. The Fifth Patriarch took the oar and began rowing. Huineng said, 'Please sit, Master. It is proper for the disciple to row.' The Patriarch said, 'It is fitting that I ferry you across.' Huineng said, 'When one is deluded, the teacher ferries; when one is awakened, one ferries oneself. The word "ferry" is the same, but its application differs.

passages.text:
惠能生在邊方，語音不正，蒙師傳法，今已得悟，只合自性自度。』祖云：『如是，如是！以後佛法，由汝大行。汝去三年，吾方逝世。汝今好去，努力向南。不宜速說，佛法難起。』
「惠能辭違祖已，發足南行。兩月中間，至大廋嶺。逐後數百人來，欲奪衣鉢。一僧俗姓陳，名惠明，先是四品將軍，性行麁慥，極意參尋。為眾人先，趁及惠能。惠能擲下衣鉢於石上，云：『此衣表信，可力爭耶？』能隱草莽中。
passages.translation_en:
Huineng was born in a remote region and speaks with an imperfect accent. Yet having received the Dharma from the Master, I am now awakened. It is only fitting that I ferry myself with my own nature.' The Patriarch said, 'Just so, just so! Hereafter, the Buddha-Dharma will spread widely through you. Three years after you leave, I will depart this world. Go well now, and strive toward the south. But do not begin teaching too soon — the Buddha-Dharma is difficult to establish.'
After Huineng took leave of the Patriarch, he set out southward on foot. Within two months, he reached the Dayu Mountain Range. Several hundred people were pursuing him from behind, intent on seizing the robe and bowl. One monk, surnamed Chen in lay life and named Huiming, had formerly been a general of the fourth rank. He was rough in temperament and the most determined of the pursuers, outrunning all the rest to catch up with Huineng. Huineng set the robe and bowl down on a rock and said, 'This robe is a symbol of faith. Should it be fought over by force?' Then he hid himself in the undergrowth.

passages.text: 惠明至，提掇不動，乃喚云：『行者！行者！我為法來，不為衣來。』惠能遂出，坐盤石上。惠明作禮云：『望行者為我說法。』惠能云：『汝既為法而來，可屏息諸緣，勿生一念。吾為汝說。』明良久。惠能云：『不思善，不思惡，正與麼時，那箇是明上座本來面目？』惠明言下大悟。復問云：『上來密語密意外，還更有密意否？』惠能云：『與汝說者，即非密也。汝若返照，密在汝邊。』明曰：『惠明雖在黃梅，實未省自己面目。
passages.translation_en: When Huiming arrived and tried to pick up the robe and bowl, he could not move them. He called out, 'Lay brother! Lay brother! I have come for the Dharma, not for the robe.' Huineng came out and sat upon the rock. Huiming bowed and said, 'I beg the lay brother to expound the Dharma for me.' Huineng said, 'Since you have come for the Dharma, put aside all external conditions and do not give rise to a single thought. I will explain it to you.' After Huiming stood in silence for a long while, Huineng said, 'Without thinking of good, without thinking of evil — at just this moment, what is your original face, Venerable Ming?' At these words, Huiming was greatly awakened. He then asked, 'Beyond the secret words and secret meaning just spoken, is there anything further?' Huineng said, 'What I have told you is not secret. If you turn your light inward, the secret is right where you are.' Huiming said, 'Although I was at Huangmei, I had never truly realized my own original face.

passages.text:
今蒙指示，如人飲水，冷暖自知。今行者即惠明師也。』惠能曰：『汝若如是，吾與汝同師黃梅，善自護持。』明又問：『惠明今後向甚處去？』惠能曰：『逢袁則止，遇蒙則居。』明禮辭。
「惠能後至曹溪，又被惡人尋逐。乃於四會，避難獵人隊中，凡經一十五載，時與獵人隨宜說法。獵人常令守網，每見生命，盡放之。每至飯時，以菜寄煮肉鍋。或問，則對曰：『但喫肉邊菜。』
「一日思惟：『時當弘法，不可終遯。
passages.translation_en:
Now, receiving your guidance, I am like a person drinking water who knows for himself whether it is cold or warm. Now you, lay brother, are my teacher.' Huineng said, 'If that is so, then you and I share the same teacher in Huangmei. Protect and uphold the Dharma well.' Huiming asked again, 'Where should I go from here?' Huineng said, 'Stop when you reach Yuan; settle when you encounter Meng.' Huiming bowed and departed.
Later, Huineng reached Caoxi, but was again pursued by those who wished him harm. He took refuge among a band of hunters in Sihui, living with them for fifteen years, and teaching them the Dharma as occasion allowed. The hunters often had him watch the nets; whenever he saw a living creature caught, he would release it. At mealtimes, he would cook vegetables in the same pot with the hunters' meat. If anyone asked, he would say, 'I only eat the vegetables from beside the meat.'
One day he reflected, 'The time has come to spread the Dharma. I cannot remain in hiding forever.'

passages.text: 』遂出至廣州法性寺，值印宗法師講《涅槃經》。時有風吹旛動，一僧曰：『風動。』一僧曰：『旛動。』議論不已。惠能進曰：『不是風動，不是旛動，仁者心動。』一眾駭然。印宗延至上席，徵詰奧義。見惠能言簡理當，不由文字，宗云：『行者定非常人。久聞黃梅衣法南來，莫是行者否？』惠能曰：『不敢。』宗於是作禮，告請傳來衣鉢出示大眾。宗復問曰：『黃梅付囑，如何指授？』惠能曰：『指授即無；惟論見性，不論禪定解脫。
passages.translation_en: He then went to Faxing Temple in Guangzhou, where the monk Yinzong was lecturing on the Nirvana Sutra. At that time, the wind was blowing a banner, and one monk said, 'The wind is moving.' Another monk said, 'The banner is moving.' They argued back and forth without end. Huineng stepped forward and said, 'It is not the wind that moves, nor the banner that moves — it is your minds that move.' The entire assembly was astonished. Yinzong invited Huineng to the seat of honor and questioned him on the profound meaning of the teaching. Seeing that Huineng's words were simple yet perfectly apt, and not dependent on written texts, Yinzong said, 'You are certainly no ordinary person. I have long heard that the robe and Dharma of Huangmei came south — could it be you?' Huineng said, 'I would not presume to claim so.' Yinzong then bowed and asked Huineng to show the robe and bowl to the assembly. Yinzong asked further, 'How did the master at Huangmei instruct you when he transmitted the teaching?' Huineng said, 'There was no special instruction. We only discussed seeing one's own nature — not meditation or liberation.'

passages.text: 』宗曰：『何不論禪定解脫？』能曰：『為是二法，不是佛法。佛法是不二之法。』宗又問：『如何是佛法不二之法？』惠能曰：『法師講《涅槃經》，明佛性，是佛法不二之法。如高貴德王菩薩白佛言：「犯四重禁、作五逆罪，及一闡提等，當斷善根佛性否？」佛言：「善根有二：一者常，二者無常，佛性非常非無常，是故不斷，名為不二。一者善，二者不善，佛性非善非不善，是名不二。
passages.translation_en: Yinzong asked, 'Why not discuss meditation and liberation?' Huineng said, 'Because those are dualistic practices, and the Buddha-Dharma is the teaching of non-duality.' Yinzong asked again, 'What is the non-dual teaching of the Buddha-Dharma?' Huineng said, 'In your lecture on the Nirvana Sutra, you explain that Buddha-nature is the non-dual teaching of the Buddha-Dharma. As the noble Bodhisattva King of High Virtue said to the Buddha: "Do those who have violated the four grave precepts, committed the five heinous crimes, or who are icchantikas — have they cut off their good roots and Buddha-nature?" The Buddha said: "Good roots are of two kinds: one is permanent, the other impermanent. But Buddha-nature is neither permanent nor impermanent, and therefore is not cut off — this is called non-duality. One kind is good, the other is not good. But Buddha-nature is neither good nor not good — this is called non-duality.

passages.text:
蘊之與界，凡夫見二，智者了達其性無二，無二之性即是佛性。」』印宗聞說，歡喜合掌，言：『某甲講經，猶如瓦礫；仁者論義，猶如真金。』於是為惠能剃髮，願事為師。惠能遂於菩提樹下，開東山法門。
「惠能於東山得法，辛苦受盡，命似懸絲。今日得與使君、官僚、僧尼、道俗同此一會，莫非累劫之緣，亦是過去生中供養諸佛，同種善根，方始得聞如上頓教得法之因。教是先聖所傳，不是惠能自智。
passages.translation_en:
The aggregates and the elements — ordinary people see them as two, but the wise understand that their nature is not two. This non-dual nature is itself the Buddha-nature."' Hearing this, Yinzong was delighted. Pressing his palms together, he said, 'My own lecturing on the sutra is like broken tiles, while your discourse on its meaning is like pure gold.' Thereupon he shaved Huineng's head and asked to become his disciple. Huineng then began teaching the East Mountain Dharma Gate beneath the bodhi tree.
Huineng said, 'Since receiving the Dharma at East Mountain, I endured every hardship, my life hanging by a thread. That today I am able to share this gathering with you — the magistrate, officials, monks, nuns, Taoists, and laypeople — is surely due to the karmic connections of countless past lives, and to the good roots we have planted together through making offerings to the Buddhas in former existences. Only through this could you now hear the causes and conditions of receiving the Sudden Teaching. This teaching was transmitted by the ancient sages — it is not Huineng's own wisdom.

passages.text:
願聞先聖教者，各令淨心，聞了各自除疑，如先代聖人無別。」
一眾聞法，歡喜作禮而退。
passages.translation_en:
Those who wish to hear the teaching of the ancient sages, let each of you purify your mind. Having heard it, let each of you cast away your doubts and be no different from the sages of the past.'
The entire assembly, having heard the Dharma, rejoiced, bowed, and withdrew.

passages.text: 次日，韋使君請益。師陞座，告大眾曰：「總淨心念摩訶般若波羅蜜多。」復云：「善知識！菩提般若之智，世人本自有之；只緣心迷，不能自悟，須假大善知識，示導見性。當知愚人智人，佛性本無差別，只緣迷悟不同，所以有愚有智。吾今為說摩訶般若波羅蜜法，使汝等各得智慧。志心諦聽！吾為汝說。善知識！世人終日口念般若，不識自性般若，猶如說食不飽。口但說空，萬劫不得見性，終無有益。
passages.translation_en: The next day, Magistrate Wei requested further teaching. The Master ascended the platform and addressed the assembly: 'All of you, purify your minds and recite Mahaprajnaparamita.' He continued: 'Good friends, the wisdom of bodhi-prajna is something all people inherently possess. It is only because the mind is deluded that one cannot awaken to it oneself, and must rely on a great good teacher to show the way and reveal one's true nature. You should understand that the buddha-nature of the foolish and the wise is fundamentally no different. It is only because delusion and awakening differ that some are foolish and some are wise. I will now teach you the Mahaprajnaparamita Dharma, so that each of you may attain wisdom. Listen carefully with sincere minds, and I will explain it for you. Good friends, people in the world recite "prajna" all day long, yet do not recognize the prajna of their own nature. This is like talking about food but never being full. If your mouth merely speaks of emptiness, you will not see your true nature even in ten thousand kalpas — in the end it brings no benefit.'

passages.text: 善知識！摩訶般若波羅蜜是梵語，此言大智慧到彼岸。此須心行，不在口念。口念心不行，如幻、如化、如露、如電；口念心行，則心口相應，本性是佛，離性無別佛。何名摩訶？摩訶是大。心量廣大，猶如虛空，無有邊畔，亦無方圓大小，亦非青黃赤白，亦無上下長短，亦無瞋無喜，無是無非，無善無惡，無有頭尾。諸佛剎土，盡同虛空。世人妙性本空，無有一法可得。自性真空，亦復如是。善知識！莫聞吾說空，便即著空。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends, Mahaprajnaparamita is a Sanskrit term meaning "great wisdom that reaches the other shore." This must be practiced with the mind, not merely recited with the mouth. If the mouth recites but the mind does not practice, it is like an illusion, a phantom, dewdrops, or a lightning flash. If the mouth recites and the mind also practices, then mind and mouth correspond, and one's original nature is itself Buddha — apart from this nature there is no other Buddha. What does "maha" mean? Maha means "great." The capacity of the mind is vast and great, like empty space, without boundaries. It is neither square nor round, neither great nor small. It is not blue, yellow, red, or white. It has no above or below, no long or short. It has no anger or joy, no right or wrong, no good or evil, no head or tail. All buddha-lands are ultimately like empty space. The wondrous nature of worldly people is originally empty — there is not a single dharma that can be grasped. The true emptiness of self-nature is also like this. Good friends, do not hear me speak of emptiness and then become attached to emptiness.'

passages.text: 第一莫著空，若空心靜坐，即著無記空。善知識！世界虛空，能含萬物色像，日月星宿，山河大地，泉源谿澗，草木叢林，惡人善人，惡法善法，天堂地獄，一切大海，須彌諸山，總在空中。世人性空，亦復如是。善知識！自性能含萬法是大，萬法在諸人性中。若見一切人、惡之與善，盡皆不取不捨亦不染著，心如虛空，名之為大，故曰摩訶。善知識！迷人口說，智者心行。又有迷人，空心靜坐，百無所思，自稱為大。
passages.translation_en: 'Above all, do not cling to emptiness. If you sit in meditation with a blank mind, you fall into the emptiness of blankness. Good friends, the emptiness of the universe can contain all things and forms — the sun, moon, and stars; mountains, rivers, and the great earth; springs, streams, and valleys; grass, trees, and forests; bad people and good people; bad dharmas and good dharmas; heavens and hells; all the great oceans; and all the Sumeru mountains — all are contained within space. The emptiness of people's nature is also like this. Good friends, our self-nature can contain the ten thousand dharmas — this is what "great" means. The ten thousand dharmas are within the nature of all people. If you see all people — whether evil or good — and neither grasp nor reject any of them, and are not stained by attachment, then the mind is like empty space, and this is called "great" — hence the term "maha." Good friends, the deluded merely talk about it; the wise practice it in their minds. There are also deluded people who sit in meditation with blank minds, thinking of nothing whatsoever, and call themselves great.'

passages.text:
此一輩人，不可與語，為邪見故。善知識！心量廣大，遍周法界，用即了了分明，應用便知一切。一切即一，一即一切。去來自由，心體無滯，即是般若。善知識！一切般若智，皆從自性而生，不從外入。莫錯用意，名為真性自用，一真一切真。心量大事，不行小道。口莫終日說空，心中不修此行，恰似凡人自稱國王，終不可得，非吾弟子。
「善知識！何名般若？般若者，唐言智慧也。一切處所，一切時中，念念不愚，常行智慧，即是般若行。
passages.translation_en: 'This kind of person is not worth speaking with, because they hold wrong views. Good friends, the capacity of the mind is vast and great, pervading the entire dharma-realm. When it functions, it is clear and distinct in every detail; in application it knows all things. All is one, and one is all. Coming and going freely, with the mind-substance unobstructed — this is prajna. Good friends, all prajna-wisdom arises from one's own nature, not from outside. Do not misuse your intention — this is called the authentic functioning of true nature. One truth, and all is true. The mind's capacity is a great matter — do not walk small paths. Do not spend all day talking about emptiness while your mind does not cultivate this practice; this is like a commoner calling himself a king — it can never be realized. Such a person is not my disciple.' 'Good friends, what is prajna? Prajna means "wisdom" in Chinese. In every place and at every moment, thought after thought, never falling into ignorance, always acting with wisdom — this is the practice of prajna.'

passages.text: 一念愚即般若絕，一念智即般若生。世人愚迷，不見般若，口說般若，心中常愚。常自言：『我修般若。』念念說空，不識真空。般若無形相，智慧心即是。若作如是解，即名般若智。何名波羅蜜？此是西國語，唐言到彼岸，解義離生滅。著境生滅起，如水有波浪，即名為此岸；離境無生滅，如水常通流，即名為彼岸，故號波羅蜜。善知識！迷人口念，當念之時，有妄有非。念念若行，是名真性。悟此法者，是般若法；修此行者，是般若行。
passages.translation_en: 'One thought of ignorance and prajna is cut off; one thought of wisdom and prajna arises. Worldly people are ignorant and deluded, unable to see prajna. They speak of prajna with their mouths, yet in their minds they remain ignorant. They constantly say, "I cultivate prajna," and speak of emptiness thought after thought, yet do not recognize true emptiness. Prajna has no form or appearance — the wisdom-mind itself is prajna. If you understand it this way, this is called prajna-wisdom. What does "paramita" mean? It is a Western Indian term meaning "arriving at the other shore" in Chinese. Its meaning is: understanding that transcends birth and extinction. When you cling to sense-objects, birth and extinction arise — this is like water with waves, and is called "this shore." When you are free from sense-objects, there is no birth or extinction — this is like water flowing freely and unobstructed, and is called "the other shore." Hence the term "paramita." Good friends, deluded people recite with their mouths, but at the very moment of recitation there are both false and wrong thoughts. If you practice it thought after thought, this is called true nature. One who awakens to this dharma has awakened to the prajna-dharma; one who cultivates this practice cultivates the prajna-practice.'

passages.text:
不修即凡；一念修行，自身等佛。善知識！凡夫即佛，煩惱即菩提。前念迷即凡夫，後念悟即佛。前念著境即煩惱，後念離境即菩提。
「善知識！摩訶般若波羅蜜，最尊最上最第一，無住無往亦無來，三世諸佛從中出。當用大智慧，打破五蘊煩惱塵勞。如此修行，定成佛道，變三毒為戒定慧。善知識！我此法門，從一般若生八萬四千智慧。何以故？為世人有八萬四千塵勞。若無塵勞，智慧常現，不離自性。
passages.translation_en: 'Those who do not cultivate remain ordinary beings; with a single thought of cultivation, one is equal to the Buddha. Good friends, ordinary beings are themselves Buddha; afflictions are themselves bodhi. The previous thought, if deluded, is that of an ordinary being; the next thought, if awakened, is that of a Buddha. The previous thought, if attached to sense-objects, is affliction; the next thought, if free from sense-objects, is bodhi.' 'Good friends, Mahaprajnaparamita is the most honored, the most supreme, the foremost. It neither abides, nor goes, nor comes. All buddhas of the three times emerge from it. One should use great wisdom to shatter the afflictions and defilements of the five aggregates. Practicing in this way, one will certainly attain buddhahood, transforming the three poisons into morality, concentration, and wisdom. Good friends, in my Dharma-gate, from one prajna, eighty-four thousand wisdoms are born. Why? Because worldly people have eighty-four thousand defilements. If there were no defilements, wisdom would always be manifest, never separate from one's own nature.'

passages.text: 悟此法者，即是無念，無憶無著，不起誑妄。用自真如性，以智慧觀照，於一切法不取不捨，即是見性成佛道。善知識！若欲入甚深法界及般若三昧者，須修般若行，持誦《金剛般若經》，即得見性。當知此經功德無量無邊，經中分明讚歎，莫能具說。此法門是最上乘，為大智人說，為上根人說。小根小智人聞，心生不信。何以故？譬如大龍下雨於閻浮提，城邑聚落，悉皆漂流如漂棗葉。若雨大海，不增不減。
passages.translation_en: 'One who awakens to this dharma is without thought, without memory, without attachment, and does not give rise to falsehood and delusion. Using the true suchness of one's own nature, and contemplating with wisdom, one neither grasps nor rejects any dharma — this is seeing one's nature and attaining the Buddha-way. Good friends, if you wish to enter the most profound dharma-realm and the prajna-samadhi, you must cultivate the prajna-practice and recite and uphold the Diamond Prajna Sutra, and then you will see your nature. You should know that this sutra's merit is immeasurable and boundless. The sutra clearly praises it, and its virtues cannot be fully described. This Dharma-gate is the Supreme Vehicle, taught for people of great wisdom and superior capacity. When those of lesser capacity and lesser wisdom hear it, their minds give rise to disbelief. Why? It is like a great dragon sending down rain over Jambudvipa — cities, towns, and villages are all swept away like drifting jujube leaves. But if the rain falls upon the great ocean, it neither increases nor decreases.'

passages.text: 若大乘人，若最上乘人，聞說《金剛經》，心開悟解。故知本性自有般若之智，自用智慧，常觀照故，不假文字。譬如雨水，不從天有，元是龍能興致，令一切眾生、一切草木、有情無情，悉皆蒙潤。百川眾流，却入大海，合為一體。眾生本性般若之智，亦復如是。善知識！小根之人，聞此頓教，猶如草木根性小者，若被大雨，悉皆自倒，不能增長。小根之人，亦復如是。
passages.translation_en: 'If those of the Great Vehicle or the Supreme Vehicle hear the Diamond Sutra explained, their minds open in awakening and understanding. Therefore we know that one's original nature inherently possesses prajna-wisdom. Through the constant use of this wisdom in contemplation, one does not depend on written words. It is like the rain: it does not come from heaven, but is actually brought forth by the dragons, causing all living beings, all grasses and trees, all sentient and insentient things to be nourished. The hundred rivers and countless streams all flow back into the great ocean, merging into one body. The prajna-wisdom of beings' original nature is also like this. Good friends, those of lesser capacity who hear this sudden teaching are like grasses and trees with shallow roots — if drenched by a great rain, they all topple over and cannot grow. Those of lesser capacity are also like this.'

passages.text:
元有般若之智，與大智人更無差別，因何聞法不自開悟？緣邪見障重、煩惱根深。猶如大雲覆蓋於日，不得風吹，日光不現。般若之智亦無大小，為一切眾生自心迷悟不同，迷心外見，修行覓佛；未悟自性，即是小根。若開悟頓教，不能外修，但於自心常起正見，煩惱塵勞常不能染，即是見性。善知識！內外不住，去來自由，能除執心，通達無礙。能修此行，與般若經本無差別。
「善知識！一切修多羅及諸文字，大小二乘，十二部經，皆因人置。
passages.translation_en: 'They originally possess prajna-wisdom no different from that of people of great wisdom. So why, upon hearing the Dharma, do they not awaken by themselves? It is because the obstacles of wrong views are heavy and the roots of affliction run deep. It is like when great clouds cover the sun: without wind to blow them away, the sunlight cannot appear. Prajna-wisdom is itself neither great nor small. It is because all beings' own minds are deluded or awakened differently. Those whose deluded minds look outward and seek the Buddha through external cultivation — these have not yet awakened to their own nature, and are called people of lesser capacity. If one awakens to the sudden teaching, one does not pursue external cultivation, but constantly gives rise to right views within one's own mind, so that afflictions and defilements can never stain it — this is seeing one's nature. Good friends, neither dwelling within nor without, coming and going freely, able to remove the clinging mind, penetrating without obstruction — one who can cultivate this practice is fundamentally no different from the Prajna Sutra.' 'Good friends, all sutras and written texts, both the Lesser and Greater Vehicles, and the twelve divisions of the canon, were all established because of people.'

passages.text: 因智慧性，方能建立。若無世人，一切萬法本自不有，故知萬法本自人興。一切經書，因人說有。緣其人中有愚有智，愚為小人，智為大人。愚者問於智人，智者與愚人說法。愚人忽然悟解心開，即與智人無別。善知識！不悟即佛是眾生，一念悟時眾生是佛，故知萬法盡在自心。何不從自心中，頓見真如本性？《菩薩戒經》云：『我本元自性清淨，若識自心見性，皆成佛道。』《淨名經》云：『即時豁然，還得本心。
passages.translation_en: 'It is because of the nature of wisdom that they could be established. If there were no people in the world, the ten thousand dharmas would not exist of themselves. Therefore we know that the ten thousand dharmas originally arise because of people. All scriptures exist because people expound them. Among people, some are foolish and some are wise. The foolish are called small-minded; the wise are called great-minded. The foolish ask the wise, and the wise teach the Dharma to the foolish. When the foolish suddenly awaken and their minds open, they become no different from the wise. Good friends, without awakening, even a buddha is a sentient being; with a single thought of awakening, a sentient being is a buddha. Therefore we know that the ten thousand dharmas are all within our own mind. Why not, from within your own mind, directly see the true suchness of your original nature? The Bodhisattva Precepts Sutra says: "My fundamental original nature is inherently pure. If one recognizes one's own mind and sees one's nature, one will attain the Buddha-way." The Vimalakirti Sutra says: "In an instant, there is sudden clarity, and one recovers one's original mind."'

passages.text: 』善知識！我於忍和尚處，一聞言下便悟，頓見真如本性。是以將此教法流行，令學道者頓悟菩提。各自觀心，自見本性。若自不悟，須覓大善知識、解最上乘法者，直示正路。是善知識有大因緣，所謂化導令得見性。一切善法，因善知識能發起故。三世諸佛、十二部經，在人性中本自具有。不能自悟，須求善知識指示方見；若自悟者，不假外求。若一向執謂須他善知識方得解脫者，無有是處。何以故？自心內有知識自悟。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends, when I was with the Fifth Patriarch, upon hearing a single phrase I immediately awakened and directly saw the true suchness of my original nature. This is why I am spreading this teaching, so that students of the Way may suddenly awaken to bodhi. Each of you, look into your own mind and see your own nature. If you cannot awaken by yourself, you must seek out a great good teacher — one who understands the Supreme Vehicle Dharma — to point you directly to the right path. Such a good teacher has great karmic affinity, which is to say: guiding and teaching others so they may see their nature. All wholesome dharmas can arise because of a good teacher. The buddhas of the three times and the twelve divisions of the canon are inherently complete within human nature. If you cannot awaken by yourself, you must seek a good teacher's guidance to see it. But if you are one who awakens on your own, do not seek outside. If you stubbornly insist that only through another good teacher can you attain liberation, that is impossible. Why? Within your own mind there is already a knowing awareness that awakens of itself.'

passages.text: 若起邪迷、妄念顛倒，外善知識雖有教授，救不可得。若起正真般若觀照，一剎那間，妄念俱滅。若識自性，一悟即至佛地。善知識！智慧觀照，內外明徹，識自本心。若識本心，即本解脫。若得解脫，即是般若三昧，即是無念。何名無念？若見一切法，心不染著，是為無念。用即遍一切處，亦不著一切處。但淨本心，使六識出六門，於六塵中無染無雜，來去自由，通用無滯，即是般若三昧、自在解脫，名無念行。
passages.translation_en: 'If you give rise to deviant confusion, false thoughts, and inverted views, then even though an external good teacher offers instruction, you cannot be saved. But if you give rise to true and correct prajna-contemplation, in a single instant all false thoughts are extinguished. If you recognize your own nature, with one awakening you arrive directly at the ground of buddhahood. Good friends, when wisdom illuminates, inside and outside become thoroughly clear, and you recognize your own original mind. If you recognize your original mind, you are fundamentally liberated. If you attain liberation, this is prajna-samadhi, which is no-thought. What is no-thought? If you see all dharmas yet the mind is not stained or attached — this is no-thought. Its function reaches everywhere, yet it is not attached anywhere. Simply purify your original mind, letting the six consciousnesses go out through the six gates, and amid the six sense-objects remain undefiled and unmixed, coming and going freely, functioning without obstruction — this is prajna-samadhi, freedom and liberation, and is called the practice of no-thought.'

passages.text:
若百物不思，當令念絕，即是法縛，即名邊見。善知識！悟無念法者，萬法盡通；悟無念法者，見諸佛境界；悟無念法者，至佛地位。
「善知識！後代得吾法者，將此頓教法門，於同見同行，發願受持。如事佛故，終身而不退者，定入聖位。然須傳授從上以來默傳分付，不得匿其正法。若不同見同行，在別法中，不得傳付。損彼前人，究竟無益。恐愚人不解，謗此法門，百劫千生，斷佛種性。
passages.translation_en: 'But if you think of nothing whatsoever and completely cut off all thought, this is bondage to dharma, and is called a one-sided view. Good friends, one who awakens to the dharma of no-thought penetrates all dharmas. One who awakens to the dharma of no-thought sees the realm of all buddhas. One who awakens to the dharma of no-thought attains the stage of buddhahood.' 'Good friends, those in future generations who receive my teaching should take this Sudden Teaching Dharma-gate and, together with those of the same understanding and same practice, vow to receive and uphold it. Serve it as you would serve the Buddha, and never retreat throughout your life — you will surely enter the holy stage. However, this must be transmitted and entrusted quietly, following the tradition from the beginning; do not conceal the true Dharma. If someone does not share the same understanding and same practice, being in a different lineage, do not transmit it to them. It will harm those who came before and ultimately bring no benefit. I fear that deluded people may fail to understand and slander this Dharma-gate, thereby cutting off the buddha-seed for hundreds of kalpas and thousands of lifetimes.'

passages.text:
善知識！吾有一無相頌，各須誦取，在家出家，但依此修。若不自修，惟記吾言，亦無有益。聽吾頌曰：
說通及心通，如日處虛空，惟傳見性法，出世破邪宗。法即無頓漸，迷悟有遲疾，只此見性門，愚人不可悉。說即雖萬般，合理還歸一，煩惱暗宅中，常須生慧日。邪來煩惱至，正來煩惱除，邪正俱不用，清淨至無餘。菩提本自性，起心即是妄，淨心在妄中，但正無三障。世人若修道，一切盡不妨，常自見己過，與道即相當。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends, I have a formless verse that each of you must recite and remember. Whether you have left home or remain a householder, just practice according to it. If you do not practice it yourselves and merely memorize my words, it will be of no benefit. Listen to my verse:' 'Mastery in speech and mastery in mind are like the sun dwelling in empty space. Transmit only the Dharma of seeing one's nature — this appears in the world to shatter wrong teachings. The Dharma itself has neither sudden nor gradual; it is delusion and awakening that are slow or fast. This gate of seeing one's nature cannot be fathomed by the foolish. Though explanations may be given in ten thousand ways, when they accord with principle they return to one. In the dark house of afflictions, one must constantly give birth to the sun of wisdom. When wrong views come, afflictions arise; when right views come, afflictions are removed. When neither wrong nor right is employed, purity reaches its completest extent. Bodhi is originally one's own nature; to give rise to mental activity is itself delusion. The pure mind exists within delusion; simply correct it and the three obstructions vanish. If worldly people cultivate the Way, nothing whatsoever is an obstacle. Always see your own faults — this accords with the Way.'

passages.text: 色類自有道，各不相妨惱，離道別覓道，終身不見道。波波度一生，到頭還自懊，欲得見真道，行正即是道。自若無道心，暗行不見道，若真修道人，不見世間過。若見他人非，自非却是左，他非我不非，我非自有過。但自却非心，打除煩惱破，憎愛不關心，長伸兩腳臥。欲擬化他人，自須有方便，勿令彼有疑，即是自性現。佛法在世間，不離世間覺，離世覓菩提，恰如求兔角。正見名出世，邪見名世間，邪正盡打却，菩提性宛然。
passages.translation_en: 'Each form and kind has its own path, none obstructing or troubling the others. If you leave the Way to seek the Way elsewhere, you will never see the Way in your entire life. Rushing busily through this one life, in the end you will only regret it. If you wish to see the true Way, right action is itself the Way. If you yourself lack the mind of the Way, you walk in darkness and cannot see it. If you are a person who truly cultivates the Way, you do not see the faults of the world. If you see the wrongs of others, your own finding of fault is itself wrong. Others' wrongs are not my wrong; my own faults are my own transgressions. Simply rid yourself of the fault-finding mind, and shatter afflictions completely. When neither hate nor love concerns the mind, stretch out both legs and lie down at ease. If you wish to guide and transform others, you must have skillful means. Do not cause them to have doubts — that is when self-nature manifests. The Buddha-dharma is in the world, and is never apart from worldly awakening. To leave the world seeking bodhi is like looking for rabbit horns. Right views are called transcending the world; wrong views are called worldly. When both wrong and right are completely cast away, the bodhi-nature is perfectly revealed.'

此頌是頓教，亦名大法船，迷聞經累劫，悟則剎那間。」
師復曰：「今於大梵寺說此頓教，普願法界眾生言下見性成佛。」時，韋使君與官僚道俗，聞師所說，無不省悟，一時作禮，皆歎善哉。
passages.translation_en: 'This verse is the sudden teaching, also called the great Dharma-ship. Those who hear it in delusion take kalpas upon kalpas; those who awaken do so in a single instant.' The Master further said: 'Now here at Dafan Temple I have taught this sudden teaching. I sincerely wish that all beings throughout the dharma-realm may, upon hearing these words, see their nature and attain buddhahood.' At that time, Magistrate Wei and the officials, monks, and laypeople who heard the Master's teaching all without exception attained insight. Together they bowed in respect and exclaimed with admiration: 'Excellent! How wonderful!'

passages.text:
一日，韋刺史為師設大會齋。齋訖，刺史請師陞座，同官僚士庶肅容再拜，問曰：「弟子聞和尚說法，實不可思議。今有少疑，願大慈悲，特為解說。」
師曰：「有疑即問，吾當為說。」
韋公曰：「和尚所說，可不是達磨大師宗旨乎？」
師曰：「是。」
公曰：「弟子聞：達磨初化梁武帝，帝問云：『朕一生造寺度僧、布施設齋，有何功德？』達磨言：『實無功德。』弟子未達此理，願和尚為說。」
師曰：「實無功德，勿疑先聖之言。
passages.translation_en: One day, Prefect Wei arranged a great vegetarian feast for the Master. When the meal was finished, the Prefect invited the Master to ascend the teaching seat. Together with his officials and lay followers, they composed themselves and bowed twice, then asked: 'Your disciple has heard the Master's Dharma talks, and they are truly inconceivable. Now I have a few doubts. Would the Master, in his great compassion, kindly resolve them for me?' The Master said: 'If you have doubts, then ask. I will explain.' Prefect Wei said: 'Is what the Master teaches not the essential doctrine of the Great Master Bodhidharma?' The Master said: 'It is.' The Prefect said: 'Your disciple has heard that when Bodhidharma first taught Emperor Wu of Liang, the Emperor asked: "Throughout my life I have built temples, ordained monks, given alms, and provided vegetarian feasts. What merit have I gained?" Bodhidharma said: "In truth, no merit at all." Your disciple does not yet understand this principle. Would the Master please explain it?' The Master said: 'There truly was no merit. Do not doubt the words of the ancient sage.'

passages.text: 武帝心邪，不知正法。造寺度僧、布施設齋，名為求福，不可將福便為功德。功德在法身中，不在修福。」師又曰：「見性是功，平等是德。念念無滯，常見本性，真實妙用，名為功德。內心謙下是功，外行於禮是德。自性建立萬法是功，心體離念是德。不離自性是功，應用無染是德。若覓功德法身，但依此作，是真功德。若修功德之人，心即不輕，常行普敬。心常輕人，吾我不斷，即自無功；自性虛妄不實，即自無德。為吾我自大，常輕一切故。
passages.translation_en: Emperor Wu's mind was misguided; he did not understand the true Dharma. Building temples, ordaining monks, giving alms, and providing feasts — this is called seeking blessings. Blessings should not be confused with merit. Merit resides in the Dharma-body, not in the cultivation of blessings.' The Master continued: 'Seeing one's own nature is merit; equanimity is virtue. When thought after thought flows without obstruction, and one constantly sees one's true nature in its genuine and wondrous function — this is called merit and virtue. Inward humility of mind is merit; outward practice of propriety is virtue. Establishing all dharmas from one's own nature is merit; the mind-essence being free from thought is virtue. Not departing from one's own nature is merit; responding to situations without defilement is virtue. If you seek the merit and virtue of the Dharma-body, simply act according to this — that is true merit and virtue. Those who cultivate merit and virtue do not look down on others in their minds, but always practice universal respect. If the mind constantly looks down on others and the sense of self never ceases, then one has no merit. If one's own nature is false and unreal, then one has no virtue — because the inflated ego constantly belittles everything else.'

passages.text:
善知識！念念無間是功，心行平直是德。自修性是功，自修身是德。善知識！功德須自性內見，不是布施供養之所求也。是以福德與功德別。武帝不識真理，非我祖師有過。」
刺史又問曰：「弟子常見僧俗念阿彌陀佛，願生西方。請和尚說，得生彼否？願為破疑。」
師言：「使君善聽，惠能與說。世尊在舍衛城中，說西方引化。經文分明，去此不遠。若論相說，里數有十萬八千，即身中十惡八邪，便是說遠。說遠為其下根，說近為其上智。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends! Thought after thought without interruption is merit; the mind acting with fairness and uprightness is virtue. Cultivating one's own nature is merit; cultivating one's own conduct is virtue. Good friends! Merit and virtue must be seen within one's own nature — they cannot be sought through charitable giving and offerings. This is why blessings and merit are different. Emperor Wu did not recognize the true principle; the error was not with our Patriarch.' The Prefect asked again: 'Your disciple often sees monks and laypeople reciting the name of Amitabha Buddha, vowing to be reborn in the Western Pure Land. Would the Master please explain — can they actually be reborn there? Please resolve this doubt for me.' The Master said: 'Listen well, Prefect, and Huineng will explain. The World-Honored One, while in the city of Shravasti, spoke of the Western Pure Land as a skillful teaching. As the sutra clearly states, it is not far from here. If we speak in terms of physical distance, it is 108,000 li away — but this number corresponds to the ten evils and eight wrong practices within our own being. That is what makes it seem far. Calling it far is for those of lesser capacity; calling it near is for those of higher wisdom.'

passages.text: 人有兩種，法無兩般。迷悟有殊，見有遲疾。迷人念佛求生於彼，悟人自淨其心。所以佛言：『隨其心淨即佛土淨。』使君東方人，但心淨即無罪。雖西方人，心不淨亦有愆。東方人造罪，念佛求生西方。西方人造罪，念佛求生何國？凡愚不了自性，不識身中淨土，願東願西。悟人在處一般，所以佛言：『隨所住處恒安樂。』使君心地但無不善，西方去此不遙。若懷不善之心，念佛往生難到。今勸善知識，先除十惡即行十萬，後除八邪乃過八千。
passages.translation_en: 'People are of two kinds, but the Dharma is not of two kinds. Delusion and awakening differ, and understanding may come slowly or quickly. The deluded recite the Buddha's name seeking rebirth in that land; the awakened purify their own minds. Therefore the Buddha said: "As the mind is purified, so is the Buddha-land purified." Prefect, you are a person of the East — just purify your mind and you are without transgression. Even a person of the West, if their mind is impure, still has faults. An Easterner who commits transgressions recites the Buddha's name seeking rebirth in the West. But when a Westerner commits transgressions, which land do they recite the Buddha's name to be reborn in? Ordinary fools do not understand their own nature and do not recognize the Pure Land within their own being, so they wish for the East or wish for the West. But for the awakened, any place is the same. Therefore the Buddha said: "Wherever one dwells, there is constant peace and joy." Prefect, if your mind is simply free from unwholesomeness, the West is not far from here. But if you harbor unwholesome thoughts in your mind, reciting the Buddha's name for rebirth will be hard to reach. Now I urge all good friends: first remove the ten evils, and you have traveled the 100,000 li; then remove the eight wrong practices, and you have crossed the 8,000 li.'

passages.text:
念念見性，常行平直，到如彈指，便覩彌陀。使君但行十善，何須更願往生？不斷十惡之心，何佛即來迎請？若悟無生頓法，見西方只在剎那。不悟念佛求生，路遙如何得達。惠能與諸人，移西方於剎那間，目前便見。各願見否？」
眾皆頂禮云：「若此處見，何須更願往生？願和尚慈悲，便現西方，普令得見。」
師言：「大眾！世人自色身是城，眼耳鼻舌是門，外有五門，內有意門。心是地，性是王。王居心地上，性在王在，性去王無。
passages.translation_en: 'In thought after thought, see your own nature; always act with fairness and directness — and arrival comes in a finger-snap, and you will see Amitabha. Prefect, just practice the ten virtues — what need is there to vow for rebirth? If you do not sever the mind of the ten evils, what Buddha would come to welcome you? If you awaken to the sudden teaching of the unborn, you see the West in an instant. Without awakening, reciting the Buddha's name and seeking rebirth — the road is so long, how could you ever arrive? Huineng will now, for all of you, move the Western Pure Land here in an instant, so you can see it right before your eyes. Does everyone wish to see it?' The assembly all prostrated and said: 'If we can see it right here, what need is there to vow for rebirth elsewhere? We beg the Master, in his compassion, to manifest the West so that all may see it.' The Master said: 'Great assembly! The worldly person's own physical body is the city. The eyes, ears, nose, and tongue are the gates. There are five gates on the outside and one gate of mind-consciousness within. The mind is the ground; the nature is the sovereign. The sovereign dwells upon the ground of the mind. When the nature is present, the sovereign is present; when the nature departs, the sovereign is gone.'

passages.text: 性在身心存，性去身壞。佛向性中作，莫向身外求。自性迷即是眾生，自性覺即是佛。慈悲即是觀音，喜捨名為勢至，能淨即釋迦，平直即彌陀；人我是須彌，貪欲是海水，煩惱是波浪，毒害是惡龍，虛妄是鬼神，塵勞是魚鱉。貪瞋是地獄，愚癡是畜生。善知識！常行十善，天堂便至。除人我，須彌倒；去貪欲，海水竭；煩惱無，波浪滅；毒害除，魚龍絕。
passages.translation_en: 'When the nature is present, body and mind endure; when the nature departs, the body disintegrates. The Buddha is made within the nature — do not seek outside the body. When one's own nature is deluded, one is a sentient being; when one's own nature is awakened, one is a Buddha. Compassion is Avalokiteshvara; joyful giving is Mahasthamaprapta; the ability to purify is Shakyamuni; equanimity and directness are Amitabha. Self-and-other discrimination is Mount Sumeru; greed and desire are the ocean waters; afflictions are the waves; malice is the evil dragons; falsehood is the ghosts and spirits; worldly defilements are the fish and turtles. Greed and anger are the hells; ignorance is the animal realm. Good friends! Always practice the ten virtues and heaven is right here. Remove self-and-other discrimination, and Mount Sumeru topples. Eliminate greed and desire, and the ocean waters dry up. When afflictions are gone, the waves are stilled. When malice is removed, the fish and dragons vanish.'

passages.text:
自心地上覺性，如來放大光明；外照六門清淨，能破六欲諸天；自性內照，三毒即除；地獄等罪一時銷滅，內外明徹不異西方。不作此修，如何到彼？」
大眾聞說，了然見性，悉皆禮拜，俱歎善哉。唱言：「普願法界眾生，聞者一時悟解。」
師言：「善知識！若欲修行，在家亦得，不由在寺。在家能行，如東方人心善；在寺不修，如西方人心惡。但心清淨，即是自性西方。」
韋公又問：「在家如何修行？願為教授。
passages.translation_en: 'Upon the ground of your own mind, the awakened nature — the Tathagata — radiates great light. Outwardly it illuminates the six gates, purifying them and shattering the six desire-heavens. When one's own nature shines inward, the three poisons are instantly removed. All karmic offenses such as those deserving of hell are dissolved at once. When inner and outer are bright and clear, this is no different from the Western Pure Land. If you do not cultivate in this way, how will you ever get there?' The great assembly, hearing this teaching, clearly saw their own nature. They all prostrated in reverence, exclaiming in unison: 'Excellent!' They proclaimed: 'May all sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm, upon hearing this, awaken and understand at once.' The Master said: 'Good friends! If you wish to practice, you can do so at home — you need not be in a monastery. Practicing at home is like an Easterner whose mind is virtuous; not practicing in a monastery is like a Westerner whose mind is unwholesome. Just purify the mind, and that itself is the Western Pure Land of your own nature.' Prefect Wei asked again: 'How should one practice at home? Please instruct us.'

師言：「吾與大眾說無相頌。但依此修，常與吾同處無別；若不依此修，剃髮出家於道何益？頌曰：
心平何勞持戒，行直何用修禪！恩則孝養父母，義則上下相憐，讓則尊卑和睦，忍則眾惡無諠，若能鑽木出火，淤泥定生紅蓮。苦口的是良藥，逆耳必是忠言，改過必生智慧，護短心內非賢。日用常行饒益，成道非由施錢，菩提只向心覓，何勞向外求玄。聽說依此修行，西方只在目前。
passages.translation_en: The Master said: 'I will give the assembly a formless verse. Simply practice according to it, and you will always be with me, no different from being together. But if you do not practice according to it, then even shaving your head and leaving home — what good does it do for the Way?' The verse says: 'When the mind is level, what need is there to uphold precepts? When conduct is straight, what use is practicing meditation? In kindness, care for your parents with filial devotion. In righteousness, let those above and below feel mutual compassion. In yielding, those of high and low station live in harmony. In patience, the host of evils makes no disturbance. If you can drill wood and produce fire, then from the muddy pond the red lotus will surely bloom. Bitter medicine is truly good medicine; words harsh to the ear are surely loyal counsel. Correcting faults gives birth to wisdom; defending shortcomings reveals an unworthy heart. In daily life, always practice generosity and benefit others — the Way is not achieved merely by giving money. Bodhi is to be sought only within your own mind — why labor to seek mysteries outside? If you listen to this teaching and practice accordingly, the Western Pure Land is right before your eyes.'
