師復曰：「善知識！總須依偈修行，見取自性，直成佛道。時不相待，眾人且散，吾歸曹溪。眾若有疑，却來相問。」
時，刺史官僚、在會善男信女，各得開悟，信受奉行。
passages.translation_en: The Master continued: 'Good friends! You must all practice according to this verse, see and grasp your own nature, and proceed directly to Buddhahood. Time waits for no one. The assembly should now disperse, and I will return to Caoxi. If any of you have doubts, come and ask me there.' At that time, the Prefect and his officials, together with all the good men and faithful women in the assembly, each attained awakening. They received the teaching with faith and put it into practice.

passages.text: 師示眾云：「善知識！我此法門，以定慧為本。大眾！勿迷，言定慧別。定慧一體，不是二。定是慧體，慧是定用。即慧之時定在慧，即定之時慧在定。若識此義，即是定慧等學。諸學道人，莫言先定發慧、先慧發定各別。作此見者，法有二相。口說善語，心中不善。空有定慧，定慧不等。若心口俱善、內外一如，定慧即等。自悟修行，不在於諍。若諍先後，即同迷人，不斷勝負，却增我法，不離四相。善知識！定慧猶如何等？猶如燈光。
passages.translation_en: The Master addressed the assembly: 'Good friends! This Dharma teaching of mine takes samadhi and prajna as its foundation. Great assembly, do not be confused into thinking that samadhi and prajna are separate. Samadhi and prajna are one substance, not two. Samadhi is the substance of prajna; prajna is the function of samadhi. At the very moment of prajna, samadhi is within prajna. At the very moment of samadhi, prajna is within samadhi. If you understand this principle, then you understand the equal cultivation of samadhi and prajna. All you students of the Way, do not say that samadhi comes first and gives rise to prajna, or that prajna comes first and gives rise to samadhi, as if they were separate. Holding such a view implies that the Dharma has a dual nature. If the mouth speaks good words but the mind within is not good, then samadhi and prajna are empty — they are not equal. If mind and mouth are both good, inner and outer are unified as one, then samadhi and prajna are equal. Self-awakening and self-practice — that is what matters, not disputation. If you argue about which comes first or last, you are like a deluded person, never settling the contest of winning and losing, only increasing attachment to self and dharmas, never departing from the four marks. Good friends! What is samadhi-prajna like? It is like the lamp and its light.'

passages.text:
有燈即光，無燈即闇。燈是光之體，光是燈之用；名雖有二，體本同一。此定慧法，亦復如是。」
師示眾云：「善知識！一行三昧者，於一切處行住坐臥，常行一直心是也。《淨名》云：『直心是道場，直心是淨土。』莫心行諂曲，口但說直；口說一行三昧，不行直心。但行直心，於一切法勿有執著。迷人著法相、執一行三昧，直言：『常坐不動，妄不起心，即是一行三昧。』作此解者，即同無情，却是障道因緣。
passages.translation_en: 'When there is a lamp, there is light; without a lamp, there is darkness. The lamp is the substance of light; the light is the function of the lamp. Their names are two, but their substance is fundamentally one. The Dharma of samadhi and prajna is exactly like this.' The Master addressed the assembly: 'Good friends! The single-practice samadhi means that in all places — whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down — one always acts with a straightforward mind. The Vimalakirti Sutra says: "The straightforward mind is the place of awakening; the straightforward mind is the Pure Land." Do not let your mind engage in crookedness and flattery while your mouth merely speaks of straightforwardness. Do not speak of the single-practice samadhi while failing to act with a straightforward mind. Simply practice the straightforward mind, and do not cling to any dharma whatsoever. The deluded cling to the characteristics of dharmas, fixate on the single-practice samadhi, and declare: "Just sitting still and not moving, not giving rise to false thoughts in the mind — that is the single-practice samadhi." Those who interpret it this way are no different from insentient things, and they actually create an obstruction to the Way.'

passages.text:
善知識！道須通流，何以却滯？心不住法，道即通流；心若住法，名為自縛。若言常坐不動是，只如舍利弗宴坐林中，却被維摩詰訶。善知識！又有人教坐，看心觀靜，不動不起，從此置功。迷人不會，便執成顛。如此者眾，如是相教，故知大錯。」
師示眾云：「善知識！本來正教，無有頓漸，人性自有利鈍。迷人漸修，悟人頓契。自識本心，自見本性，即無差別，所以立頓漸之假名。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends! The Way must flow freely — why would you cause it to stagnate? When the mind does not dwell on dharmas, the Way flows freely. When the mind dwells on dharmas, that is called binding yourself. If you say that constantly sitting without moving is correct, consider that Shariputra was sitting quietly in the forest and was scolded by Vimalakirti. Good friends! There are also those who teach sitting meditation by watching the mind and contemplating stillness, remaining motionless and unmoving, and devoting their efforts to this. Deluded people who do not understand latch on to this and become confused and unbalanced. There are many such people. Those who instruct others in this way are, one should know, gravely in error.' The Master addressed the assembly: 'Good friends! Originally the true teaching has no distinction of sudden and gradual — it is human nature that has sharpness and dullness. The deluded cultivate gradually; the awakened achieve sudden realization. When you recognize your own original mind and see your own original nature, then there is no difference. Therefore the labels "sudden" and "gradual" are merely provisional designations.'

passages.text: 善知識！我此法門，從上以來，先立無念為宗，無相為體，無住為本。無相者，於相而離相。無念者，於念而無念。無住者，人之本性。於世間善惡好醜，乃至冤之與親，言語觸刺欺爭之時，並將為空，不思酬害，念念之中不思前境。若前念今念後念，念念相續不斷，名為繫縛。於諸法上念念不住，即無縛也。此是以無住為本。善知識！外離一切相，名為無相。能離於相，即法體清淨。此是以無相為體。善知識！於諸境上，心不染，曰無念。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends! This Dharma teaching of mine, from the patriarchs onward, has first established no-thought as its doctrine, formlessness as its substance, and non-abiding as its foundation. Formlessness means to be amid forms yet free from forms. No-thought means to be amid thoughts yet free from thoughts. Non-abiding is the fundamental nature of human beings. In the midst of all worldly things — good and evil, attractive and ugly, even when facing hostility or friendship, provocative words, deception, and conflict — regard it all as empty. Do not contemplate retaliation or harm. In thought after thought, do not dwell on past objects. If previous thoughts, present thoughts, and future thoughts follow one upon another without ceasing, this is called bondage. But in regard to all dharmas, if thought after thought does not abide, then there is no bondage. This is what is meant by taking non-abiding as the foundation. Good friends! Being free from all outward forms is called formlessness. When you can be free from forms, then the Dharma-substance is pure. This is what is meant by taking formlessness as the substance. Good friends! When the mind is not stained by any object encountered, this is called no-thought.'

passages.text: 於自念上，常離諸境，不於境上生心。若只百物不思，念盡除却，一念絕即死，別處受生，是為大錯。學道者思之。若不識法意，自錯猶可，更誤他人；自迷不見，又謗佛經，所以立無念為宗。善知識！云何立無念為宗？只緣口說見性，迷人於境上有念，念上便起邪見，一切塵勞妄想從此而生。自性本無一法可得，若有所得，妄說禍福，即是塵勞邪見，故此法門立無念為宗。善知識！無者無何事？念者念何物？無者無二相，無諸塵勞之心。
passages.translation_en: 'In your own thoughts, always remain free from all objects; do not give rise to mental activity in response to objects. If you merely try to think of nothing at all, eliminating all thoughts completely, then the moment thought ceases entirely you die and are reborn elsewhere — this is a grave error. Students of the Way, reflect on this carefully. If you do not understand the meaning of this Dharma, you will go wrong yourself, which is one thing — but worse, you will mislead others. Unable to see because of your own delusion, you will even slander the Buddhist sutras. Therefore no-thought is established as the doctrine. Good friends! Why is no-thought established as the doctrine? Simply because those who speak of seeing their own nature are still, when encountering objects, caught up in thoughts, and upon those thoughts, wrong views arise. All the dust and defilements and deluded thinking spring from this. In its own nature, there is originally not a single dharma that can be grasped. If there is anything grasped, then one falsely speaks of fortune and misfortune — and that itself is dust, defilement, and wrong views. Therefore this Dharma teaching establishes no-thought as its doctrine. Good friends! "No" — no what? "Thought" — thought of what? "No" means free from duality, free from all the minds of dust and defilement.'

passages.text: 念者念真如本性。真如即是念之體，念即是真如之用。真如自性起念，非眼耳鼻舌能念。真如有性，所以起念；真如若無，眼耳色聲當時即壞。善知識！真如自性起念，六根雖有見聞覺知，不染萬境，而真性常自在。故經云：『能善分別諸法相，於第一義而不動。』」。
passages.translation_en: '"Thought" means thought of Suchness, of one's true original nature. Suchness is the substance of thought; thought is the function of Suchness. It is the Suchness of one's own nature that gives rise to thought — not the eyes, ears, nose, or tongue that can think. Suchness possesses this nature, and therefore thought arises. If Suchness were absent, then eyes, ears, forms, and sounds would instantly disintegrate. Good friends! When the Suchness of one's own nature gives rise to thought, the six sense faculties may see, hear, perceive, and know, yet they are not stained by the myriad objects, and the true nature is always free and autonomous. Therefore the sutra says: "One who can skillfully distinguish all dharma-characteristics remains unmoved in the ultimate, first meaning."'

passages.text: 師示眾云：「此門坐禪，元不著心，亦不著淨，亦不是不動。若言著心，心元是妄，知心如幻，故無所著也。若言著淨，人性本淨，由妄念故，蓋覆真如。但無妄想，性自清淨；起心著淨，却生淨妄。妄無處所，著者是妄。淨無形相，却立淨相，言是工夫。作此見者，障自本性，却被淨縛。善知識！若修不動者，但見一切人時，不見人之是非善惡過患，即是自性不動。善知識！迷人身雖不動，開口便說他人是非長短好惡，與道違背。
passages.translation_en: The Master addressed the assembly: 'In this school, sitting meditation fundamentally does not focus on the mind, nor does it focus on purity, nor is it about being motionless. If one speaks of focusing on the mind—the mind is fundamentally illusory. Knowing the mind is like a phantom, there is nothing to focus on. If one speaks of focusing on purity—people's nature is originally pure. It is due to deluded thoughts that true suchness is obscured. Simply be free of deluded thoughts and the nature is pure of itself. If you arouse the mind to focus on purity, you instead produce the delusion of purity. Delusion has no fixed location; the one who fixates is deluded. Purity has no form, yet you set up the form of purity and call it spiritual practice. Those who hold this view obstruct their own original nature and become bound by purity. Good friends! Those who cultivate stillness should simply, when seeing all people, not perceive their right and wrong, good and evil, faults and afflictions—that is the stillness of one's own nature. Good friends! A deluded person may sit with the body unmoving, yet the moment they open their mouth they speak of others' right and wrong, strengths and weaknesses, good and bad—this goes against the Way.'

passages.text:
若著心著淨，即障道也。」
師示眾云：「善知識！何名坐禪？此法門中，無障無礙，外於一切善惡境界，心念不起，名為坐；內見自性不動，名為禪。善知識！何名禪定？外離相為禪，內不亂為定。外若著相，內心即亂；外若離相，心即不亂。本性自淨自定，只為見境，思境即亂。若見諸境心不亂者，是真定也。善知識！外離相即禪，內不亂即定。外禪內定，是為禪定。《菩薩戒經》云：『我本元自性清淨。
passages.translation_en: 'If you fixate on mind or fixate on purity, this obstructs the Way.' The Master addressed the assembly: 'Good friends! What is meant by sitting meditation? In this Dharma gate, there are no obstructions and no hindrances. Externally, when confronting all conditions of good and evil, not a single thought arises in the mind—this is called sitting. Inwardly, seeing one's own nature without being moved—this is called meditation. Good friends! What is meant by meditative concentration? Externally, being free from forms is meditation; inwardly, being undisturbed is concentration. If you attach to external forms, the inner mind becomes disturbed. If you are free from external forms, the mind is undisturbed. The original nature is inherently pure and inherently settled. It is only because of perceiving sense objects and thinking about them that disturbance arises. If one can see all conditions and the mind remains undisturbed, this is true concentration. Good friends! Being free from forms externally is meditation; being undisturbed internally is concentration. External meditation and internal concentration—this is meditative concentration. The Bodhisattva Precepts Sutra says: "Our original self-nature is inherently pure."'

passages.text: 』善知識！於念念中，自見本性清淨，自修自行，自成佛道。」。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends! In each successive thought, see for yourselves that your original nature is pure. Cultivate and practice by yourselves, and accomplish the Buddha Way by yourselves.'

passages.text: 時，大師見廣韶洎四方士庶，駢集山中聽法，於是陞座，告眾曰：「來，諸善知識！此事須從自事中起，於一切時，念念自淨其心。自修自行，見自己法身，見自心佛，自度自戒，始得不假到此。既從遠來，一會于此，皆共有緣。今可各各胡跪，先為傳自性五分法身香，次授無相懺悔。」眾胡跪。師曰：「一、戒香。即自心中無非無惡、無嫉妬、無貪瞋、無劫害，名戒香。二、定香。即覩諸善惡境相，自心不亂，名定香。三、慧香。
passages.translation_en: At that time, the Great Master saw that scholars and commoners from Guangzhou, Shaozhou, and all four directions had gathered in the mountains to hear the Dharma. He ascended the platform and addressed the assembly: 'Come, good friends! This matter must arise from within yourselves. At all times, in every thought-moment, purify your own minds. Cultivate and practice by yourselves, see your own Dharma-body, see the Buddha of your own mind, and deliver and discipline yourselves — only then will you not have come here in vain. Since you have come from afar and we are gathered here together, we all share a karmic connection. Now let each of you kneel. I will first transmit the five-fold Dharma-body incense of your own self-nature, and then confer the formless repentance.' The assembly knelt. The Master said: 'First, the incense of moral discipline — that is, within your own mind there is no wrong, no evil, no jealousy, no greed or anger, and no intention to harm. This is called the incense of discipline. Second, the incense of concentration — that is, when encountering all conditions of good and evil, your own mind is not disturbed. This is called the incense of concentration. Third, the incense of wisdom —

passages.text:
自心無礙，常以智慧觀照自性，不造諸惡；雖修眾善，心不執著，敬上念下，矜恤孤貧，名慧香。四、解脫香。即自心無所攀緣，不思善、不思惡，自在無礙，名解脫香。五、解脫知見香。自心既無所攀緣善惡，不可沈空守寂，即須廣學多聞，識自本心，達諸佛理，和光接物，無我無人，直至菩提，真性不易，名解脫知見香。善知識！此香各自內熏，莫向外覓。
「今與汝等授無相懺悔，滅三世罪，令得三業清淨。
passages.translation_en: your own mind is unobstructed, and you constantly use wisdom to contemplate your own nature. You do not commit any evil; though you practice many good deeds, your mind does not cling to them. You respect those above and care for those below, and show compassion for the orphaned and the poor. This is called the incense of wisdom. Fourth, the incense of liberation — that is, your own mind does not grasp at conditions, does not think of good or evil, and is free and unobstructed. This is called the incense of liberation. Fifth, the incense of the knowledge and insight of liberation — when your own mind neither grasps at good or evil nor sinks into emptiness or clings to stillness, you must study broadly and learn widely, recognize your original mind, comprehend the principles of all Buddhas, harmonize with others in a gentle light, be free of self and other, and go straight to bodhi. Your true nature never changes. This is called the incense of the knowledge and insight of liberation. Good friends! This incense each person must burn inwardly — do not seek it outside. Now I will confer upon you the formless repentance, to eliminate the offenses of the three times and purify the three karmas of body, speech, and mind.'

passages.text: 善知識！各隨我語，一時道：『弟子等，從前念今念及後念，念念不被愚迷染。從前所有惡業愚迷等罪，悉皆懺悔，願一時銷滅，永不復起。弟子等，從前念今念及後念，念念不被憍誑染。從前所有惡業憍誑等罪，悉皆懺悔，願一時銷滅，永不復起。弟子等，從前念今念及後念，念念不被嫉妬染。從前所有惡業嫉妬等罪，悉皆懺悔，願一時銷滅，永不復起。』善知識！已上是為無相懺悔。
passages.translation_en: 'Good friends! Each of you repeat after me, saying together: We disciples — in past thoughts, present thoughts, and future thoughts, thought after thought — vow never to be tainted by delusion and ignorance. We fully repent all past evil karma born of ignorance and delusion. May it all be eliminated at once and never arise again. We disciples — in past thoughts, present thoughts, and future thoughts, thought after thought — vow never to be tainted by arrogance and deceit. We fully repent all past evil karma born of arrogance and deceit. May it all be eliminated at once and never arise again. We disciples — in past thoughts, present thoughts, and future thoughts, thought after thought — vow never to be tainted by jealousy and envy. We fully repent all past evil karma born of jealousy and envy. May it all be eliminated at once and never arise again.' Good friends! The above is the formless repentance.

passages.text:
云何名懺？云何名悔？懺者，懺其前愆，從前所有惡業，愚迷憍誑嫉妬等罪，悉皆盡懺，永不復起，是名為懺。悔者，悔其後過，從今以後，所有惡業，愚迷憍誑嫉妬等罪，今已覺悟，悉皆永斷，更不復作，是名為悔。故稱懺悔。凡夫愚迷，只知懺其前愆，不知悔其後過。以不悔故，前愆不滅，後過又生。前愆既不滅，後過復又生，何名懺悔？
「善知識！既懺悔已，與善知識發四弘誓願，各須用心正聽。
passages.translation_en: What is meant by 'repentance' (chan) and what is meant by 'reform' (hui)? 'Repentance' means to repent of past transgressions — all previous evil karma born of ignorance, arrogance, deceit, jealousy, and envy is entirely repented, never to arise again. This is called repentance. 'Reform' means to reform future conduct — from this moment forward, all evil karma born of ignorance, arrogance, deceit, jealousy, and envy, now that one has awakened, is entirely and forever cut off, never to be committed again. This is called reform. Therefore it is called 'repentance and reform.' Ordinary people in their delusion only know how to repent past transgressions but do not know how to reform future conduct. Because they do not reform, past transgressions are not eliminated and future offenses continue to arise. If past transgressions are not eliminated and future offenses continue to arise, how can this be called repentance and reform? Good friends! Now that the repentance is complete, I will make the Four Great Vows together with you. Each of you must listen attentively with a sincere mind.

passages.text: 自心眾生無邊誓願度，自心煩惱無邊誓願斷，自性法門無盡誓願學，自性無上佛道誓願成。善知識！大家豈不道，眾生無邊誓願度。恁麼道，且不是惠能度。善知識！心中眾生，所謂邪迷心、誑妄心、不善心、嫉妬心、惡毒心，如是等心，盡是眾生。各須自性自度，是名真度。何名自性自度？即自心中邪見煩惱愚癡眾生，將正見度。既有正見，使般若智打破愚癡迷妄眾生，各各自度。邪來正度，迷來悟度，愚來智度，惡來善度；如是度者，名為真度。
passages.translation_en: 'Sentient beings of my own mind, limitless in number, I vow to deliver. Afflictions of my own mind, inexhaustible in number, I vow to cut off. Dharma teachings of my own nature, boundless in number, I vow to study. The supreme Buddha Way of my own nature, I vow to attain.' Good friends! Do we not all say, 'Sentient beings, limitless in number, I vow to deliver'? But saying this does not mean that Huineng delivers them. Good friends! The 'sentient beings' within the mind are deviant thoughts, deluded thoughts, unwholesome thoughts, jealous thoughts, and malicious thoughts — minds such as these are all sentient beings. Each person must deliver them with their own self-nature. This is called true deliverance. What does it mean to deliver them with one's own self-nature? It means to use right views to deliver the sentient beings of wrong views, afflictions, and ignorance within your own mind. Once you have right views, use prajna wisdom to shatter the sentient beings of ignorance and delusion. Each delivers themselves. When deviance comes, correct it through right views; when confusion comes, dissolve it through awakening; when ignorance comes, counter it with wisdom; when evil comes, transform it with goodness. Deliverance such as this is called true deliverance.

passages.text:
又煩惱無邊誓願斷，將自性般若智，除却虛妄思想心是也。又法門無盡誓願學，須自見性，常行正法，是名真學。又無上佛道誓願成，既常能下心，行於真正，離迷離覺，常生般若。除真除妄，即見佛性，即言下佛道成。常念修行，是願力法。
「善知識！今發四弘願了，更與善知識授無相三歸依戒。善知識！歸依覺，兩足尊。歸依正，離欲尊。歸依淨，眾中尊。
passages.translation_en: Furthermore, 'Afflictions, inexhaustible in number, I vow to cut off' means to use the prajna wisdom of your own nature to eliminate false and deluded thoughts. Furthermore, 'Dharma teachings, boundless in number, I vow to study' means that you must see your own nature and always practice the true Dharma. This is called true study. Furthermore, 'The supreme Buddha Way, I vow to attain' means that once you can constantly humble your mind and practice what is true and correct, departing from both delusion and enlightenment, constantly giving rise to prajna, and setting aside both the true and the false — then you see the Buddha-nature, and in that very moment the Buddha Way is attained. Always be mindful of cultivation and practice — this is the power of the vows. Good friends! Now that we have made the Four Great Vows, I will further confer upon you the formless threefold refuge precepts. Good friends! Take refuge in enlightenment, the most honored among those replete in both blessings and wisdom. Take refuge in the true Dharma, the most honored among those free from desire. Take refuge in purity, the most honored among communities.

passages.text: 從今日去，稱覺為師，更不歸依邪魔外道，以自性三寶常自證明，勸善知識歸依自性三寶。佛者，覺也。法者，正也。僧者，淨也。自心歸依覺，邪迷不生，少欲知足，能離財色，名兩足尊。自心歸依正，念念無邪見，以無邪見故，即無人我貢高，貪愛執著，名離欲尊。自心歸依淨，一切塵勞愛欲境界，自性皆不染著，名眾中尊。若修此行，是自歸依。凡夫不會，從日至夜受三歸戒。若言歸依佛，佛在何處？若不見佛，憑何所歸，言却成妄。
passages.translation_en: From this day forward, take awakening as your teacher and never again take refuge in deviant demons or non-Buddhist paths. Constantly verify this through the Three Treasures of your own self-nature. I urge you, good friends, to take refuge in the Three Treasures of your own nature. 'Buddha' means awakening. 'Dharma' means what is right and true. 'Sangha' means purity. When your own mind takes refuge in awakening, deviance and delusion do not arise. With few desires and contentment, able to be free from wealth and sensuality — this is called 'the most honored, replete in both blessings and wisdom.' When your own mind takes refuge in what is right, thought after thought free from wrong views, and because there are no wrong views there is no self-importance, no arrogance, no greed, no attachment — this is called 'the most honored, free from desire.' When your own mind takes refuge in purity, all dusty toil and realms of desire cannot stain your own nature — this is called 'the most honored among communities.' To practice in this way is to take refuge in oneself. Ordinary people do not understand this. Day after day they take the threefold refuge precepts. If they say they take refuge in the Buddha, where is the Buddha? If they do not see the Buddha, on what basis do they take refuge? Their words become falsehood.

passages.text:
善知識！各自觀察，莫錯用心。經文分明言自歸依佛，不言歸依他佛。自佛不歸，無所依處。今既自悟，各須歸依自心三寶，內調心性，外敬他人，是自歸依也。
「善知識！既歸依自三寶竟，各各志心，吾與說一體三身自性佛，令汝等見三身了然，自悟自性。總隨我道：『於自色身，歸依清淨法身佛。於自色身，歸依圓滿報身佛。於自色身，歸依千百億化身佛。』善知識！色身是舍宅，不可言歸。
passages.translation_en: Good friends! Each of you, examine yourselves and do not misuse your minds. The sutra text clearly says to take refuge in one's own Buddha, not in some other Buddha. If you do not take refuge in your own Buddha, there is nothing to rely upon. Now that you have awakened for yourselves, each of you must take refuge in the Three Treasures of your own mind: inwardly regulate your mind-nature, outwardly show respect to all people. This is self-refuge. Good friends! Now that you have taken refuge in the Three Treasures of your own nature, each of you focus your minds. I will explain for you the single-substance, three-body, self-nature Buddha, so that you may clearly see the three bodies and awaken to your own nature for yourselves. Repeat after me together: 'In this very physical body, I take refuge in the pure Dharma-body Buddha. In this very physical body, I take refuge in the perfect Reward-body Buddha. In this very physical body, I take refuge in the myriad Transformation-body Buddha.' Good friends! The physical body is a dwelling place; it cannot be spoken of as a refuge.

passages.text: 向者三身佛，在自性中，世人總有；為自心迷，不見內性。外覓三身如來，不見自身中有三身佛。汝等聽說，令汝等於自身中，見自性有三身佛。此三身佛，從自性生，不從外得。何名清淨法身佛？世人性本清淨，萬法從自性生。思量一切惡事，即生惡行；思量一切善事，即生善行。如是諸法在自性中，如天常清，日月常明，為浮雲蓋覆，上明下暗。忽遇風吹雲散，上下俱明，萬象皆現。世人性常浮游，如彼天雲。
passages.translation_en: The three-body Buddha mentioned above is within your own self-nature. Everyone in the world possesses it, but because their own minds are deluded, they do not see their inner nature. They seek the three-body Tathagata outside themselves and do not see that the three-body Buddha is within their own bodies. Listen to my explanation, which will enable you to see within your own bodies that your self-nature possesses the three-body Buddha. These three-body Buddhas arise from self-nature, not from external seeking. What is meant by the pure Dharma-body Buddha? The nature of all people in this world is originally pure, and the myriad dharmas are born from self-nature. Thinking about all manner of evil gives rise to evil conduct; thinking about all manner of good gives rise to good conduct. Thus all dharmas exist within self-nature, like the sky that is always clear and the sun and moon that always shine. When floating clouds cover them, it is bright above and dark below. But when a wind suddenly blows the clouds away, above and below are both bright and the myriad forms all appear. The nature of people in this world constantly drifts and floats, like those clouds in the sky.

passages.text: 善知識！智如日，慧如月，智慧常明。於外著境，被妄念浮雲蓋覆自性，不得明朗。若遇善知識，聞真正法，自除迷妄，內外明徹，於自性中萬法皆現。見性之人，亦復如是。此名清淨法身佛。善知識！自心歸依自性，是歸依真佛。自歸依者，除却自性中不善心、嫉妬心、諂曲心、吾我心、誑妄心、輕人心、慢他心、邪見心、貢高心，及一切時中不善之行，常自見己過，不說他人好惡，是自歸依。
passages.translation_en: Good friends! Knowledge is like the sun and wisdom is like the moon; knowledge and wisdom are always shining. But when you attach to external objects, the floating clouds of deluded thoughts cover your self-nature so that it cannot be clear and bright. If you encounter a good spiritual teacher and hear the true and correct Dharma, you will remove delusion for yourselves, and inside and outside will become bright and penetrating. Within your self-nature, the myriad dharmas all appear. Those who see their own nature are also like this. This is called the pure Dharma-body Buddha. Good friends! When your own mind takes refuge in your own nature, that is taking refuge in the true Buddha. Self-refuge means removing from your self-nature all unwholesome thoughts, jealous thoughts, flattering thoughts, egotistic thoughts, deceitful thoughts, thoughts of contempt for others, thoughts of arrogance, wrong views, conceit, and all unwholesome conduct at all times. Always see your own faults and do not speak of the good and evil of others. This is self-refuge.

passages.text: 常須下心，普行恭敬，即是見性通達，更無滯礙，是自歸依。何名圓滿報身？譬如一燈能除千年闇，一智能滅萬年愚。莫思向前，己過不可得；常思於後，念念圓明，自見本性。善惡雖殊，本性無二，無二之性，名為實性。於實性中，不染善惡，此名圓滿報身佛。自性起一念惡，滅萬劫善因；自性起一念善，得恒沙惡盡。直至無上菩提，念念自見，不失本念，名為報身。何名千百億化身？若不思萬法，性本如空，一念思量，名為變化。
passages.translation_en: You must always humble your mind and practice universal reverence. This is seeing your nature, penetrating and free of all obstruction. This is self-refuge. What is meant by the perfect Reward-body? It is like a single lamp that can dispel a thousand years of darkness; a single insight can eliminate ten thousand years of ignorance. Do not think about the past — what is done cannot be undone. Always reflect on the future, and in thought after thought be perfectly bright; see your own original nature for yourself. Though good and evil are different, the original nature is non-dual. This non-dual nature is called the true nature. Within the true nature, neither good nor evil can stain it. This is called the perfect Reward-body Buddha. If from self-nature a single thought of evil arises, it destroys ten thousand kalpas of wholesome causes. If from self-nature a single thought of good arises, evil as numerous as the sands of the Ganges is entirely eliminated. Straight through to unsurpassed bodhi, see it for yourself in each thought-moment, never losing sight of the original mind. This is called the Reward-body. What is meant by the myriad Transformation-bodies? If you do not think about the myriad dharmas, your nature is originally like empty space. One thought of deliberation is called transformation.

passages.text: 思量惡事，化為地獄；思量善事，化為天堂。毒害化為龍蛇，慈悲化為菩薩，智慧化為上界，愚癡化為下方。自性變化甚多，迷人不能省覺，念念起惡，常行惡道。迴一念善，智慧即生，此名自性化身佛。善知識！法身本具，念念自性自見，即是報身佛。從報身思量，即是化身佛。自悟自修自性功德，是真歸依。皮肉是色身，色身是舍宅，不言歸依也。但悟自性三身，即識自性佛。吾有一無相頌，若能持誦，言下令汝積劫迷罪一時銷滅。
passages.translation_en: When you think of evil things, it transforms into hell. When you think of good things, it transforms into heaven. Malice and harm transform into dragons and serpents. Compassion and kindness transform into bodhisattvas. Wisdom transforms into the higher realms. Ignorance transforms into the lower realms. The transformations of self-nature are very many. Deluded people, unable to awaken and reflect, thought after thought give rise to evil and constantly walk the path of evil. But if they turn around with a single thought of goodness, wisdom is immediately born. This is called the Transformation-body Buddha of one's own nature. Good friends! The Dharma-body is originally complete in everyone. Seeing your own nature for yourself in each thought-moment — that is the Reward-body Buddha. When from the Reward-body there arises deliberation — that is the Transformation-body Buddha. Awakening, cultivating, and developing the merit and virtue of your own nature for yourself: this is true refuge. The skin and flesh are the physical body; the physical body is a dwelling — it is not spoken of as a refuge. Simply awaken to the three bodies of your own nature, and you will recognize the self-nature Buddha. I have a verse without characteristics. If you can recite and uphold it, it will instantly eliminate the accumulated offenses of kalpas upon kalpas of delusion.

頌曰：
迷人修福不修道，只言修福便是道，布施供養福無邊，心中三惡元來造。擬將修福欲滅罪，後世得福罪還在，但向心中除罪緣，名自性中真懺悔。忽悟大乘真懺悔，除邪行正即無罪，學道常於自性觀，即與諸佛同一類。吾祖惟傳此頓法，普願見性同一體，若欲當來覓法身，離諸法相心中洗。努力自見莫悠悠，後念忽絕一世休，若悟大乘得見性，虔恭合掌至心求。」
師言：「善知識！總須誦取，依此修行，言下見性。
passages.translation_en: The verse says: Deluded people cultivate blessings but not the Way, / Saying that cultivating blessings itself is the Way. / Though the blessings of giving and offerings are boundless, / The three evils in the mind were there all along. / If you try to use cultivated blessings to eliminate offenses, / In future lives you gain blessings but the offenses remain. / Simply remove the causes of offenses within your mind — / This is true repentance within your own self-nature. / Suddenly awakening to the Great Vehicle's true repentance, / Remove the deviant, practice the right, and there are no offenses. / Studying the Way, always contemplate your own nature — / Then you are of the same kind as all Buddhas. / Our patriarchs only transmitted this sudden teaching, / Universally wishing that all who see their nature share one substance. / If in the future you wish to find the Dharma-body, / Wash away attachment to dharma-characteristics within your mind. / Strive to see it yourselves, do not be idle, / For if in the next thought-moment life is suddenly cut off, all is lost. / If you awaken to the Great Vehicle and see your nature, / Join your palms with sincerity and seek it wholeheartedly.' The Master said: 'Good friends! All of you must recite this and practice accordingly. Seeing your nature will happen the moment these words are spoken.

passages.text:
雖去吾千里，如常在吾邊。於此言下不悟，即對面千里，何勤遠來。珍重！好去。」
一眾聞法，靡不開悟，歡喜奉行。
passages.translation_en: Even if you are a thousand miles from me, it will be as though you are constantly at my side. But if you cannot awaken at these very words, then even face to face you are a thousand miles away — so why bother making the long journey here? Take care of yourselves! Farewell and go well.' The entire assembly, upon hearing the Dharma, was without exception awakened. They accepted it with joy and put it into practice.

passages.text: 師自黃梅得法，回至韶州曹侯村，人無知者。有儒士劉志略，禮遇甚厚。志略有姑為尼，名無盡藏，常誦《大涅槃經》。師暫聽，即知妙義，遂為解說。尼乃執卷問字，師曰：「字即不識，義即請問。」尼曰：「字尚不識，焉能會義？」師曰：「諸佛妙理，非關文字。」尼驚異之，遍告里中耆德云：「此是有道之士，宜請供養。」有魏武侯玄孫曹叔良及居民，競來瞻禮。時，寶林古寺，自隋末兵火已廢，遂於故基重建梵宇，延師居之。
passages.translation_en: After the Master received the Dharma at Huangmei, he returned to Caohou Village in Shaozhou. No one there knew of him. There was a Confucian scholar named Liu Zhilue who treated him with great courtesy and respect. Zhilue had an aunt who was a nun named Wujinzang ('Inexhaustible Treasury'). She constantly recited the Mahaparinirvana Sutra. After listening briefly, the Master immediately understood its subtle meaning and proceeded to explain it to her. The nun then held up the text and asked about specific characters. The Master said: 'I cannot read the characters, but please ask me about the meaning.' The nun said: 'If you cannot even read the characters, how can you understand the meaning?' The Master said: 'The wondrous principle of all Buddhas has nothing to do with written words.' The nun was astonished, and she told all the village elders: 'This is a man who has attained the Way. We should invite him to stay and make offerings to him.' A descendant of Marquis Cao of the Wei — Cao Shuliang — along with local residents came eagerly to pay respects and bow. At that time the ancient Baolin Monastery, which had been destroyed by fire during the wars at the end of the Sui dynasty, was rebuilt on its old foundations, and the Master was invited to reside there.

passages.text:
俄成寶坊，師住九月餘日，又為惡黨尋逐，師乃遯于前山。被其縱火焚草木，師隱身挨入石中得免。石今有師趺坐膝痕，及衣布之紋，因名避難石。師憶五祖懷會止藏之囑，遂行隱于二邑焉。
僧法海，韶州曲江人也。初參祖師，問曰：「即心即佛，願垂指諭。」師曰：「前念不生即心，後念不滅即佛；成一切相即心，離一切相即佛。吾若具說，窮劫不盡。聽吾偈曰：即心名慧，即佛乃定，定慧等持，意中清淨。
passages.translation_en:
Soon the place became a precious sanctuary. After the Master had resided there for just over nine months, he was again pursued by hostile parties. The Master fled into the mountains ahead of them. When they set fire to the grass and trees, the Master hid by pressing himself into a rock crevice and was spared. The rock still bears the imprint of the Master's crossed knees and the texture of his robe's cloth, and so it is called the Refuge Rock. Remembering the Fifth Patriarch's instruction to 'stop and hide at Huai,' the Master went into hiding between the two districts.

The monk Fahai, a native of Qujiang in Shaozhou, first came to visit the Patriarch and asked: 'What is meant by "mind itself is Buddha"? I humbly request your instruction.' The Master said: 'When the preceding thought does not arise, that is mind. When the succeeding thought does not cease, that is Buddha. Giving rise to all forms is mind; being free from all forms is Buddha. If I were to explain this fully, I could not exhaust it even in an entire kalpa. Listen to my verse: Mind itself is called wisdom; Buddha itself is samadhi. When samadhi and wisdom are maintained equally, the mind becomes pure and clear.'

passages.text:
悟此法門，由汝習性，用本無生，雙修是正。」法海言下大悟，以偈讚曰：「即心元是佛，不悟而自屈，我知定慧因，雙修離諸物。」
僧法達，洪州人，七歲出家，常誦《法華經》。來禮祖師，頭不至地。師訶曰：「禮不投地，何如不禮？汝心中必有一物。蘊習何事耶？」曰：「念《法華經》已及三千部。」師曰：「汝若念至萬部，得其經意，不以為勝，則與吾偕行。汝今負此事業，都不知過。
passages.translation_en:
'Awakening to this Dharma gate depends on your own practice-nature. Applying the originally unborn, cultivating both equally — this is the correct path.' At these words, Fahai experienced great awakening and offered this verse of praise: 'Mind itself is originally Buddha — not to realize this is to wrong oneself. Now I know the cause of samadhi and wisdom: cultivating both, one is free from all things.'

The monk Fada, a native of Hongzhou, left home at age seven and constantly recited the Lotus Sutra. When he came to pay respects to the Patriarch, his head did not touch the ground. The Master rebuked him: 'If your bow does not reach the ground, what is the use of bowing at all? There must be something in your mind. What have you been practicing?' He replied: 'I have recited the Lotus Sutra nearly three thousand times.' The Master said: 'Even if you had recited it ten thousand times, if you grasped its meaning and did not consider it a superior achievement, you could walk alongside me. But now you carry this accomplishment as a burden and do not even recognize the error.'

passages.text: 聽吾偈曰：禮本折慢幢，頭奚不至地？有我罪即生，亡功禮無比。」師又曰：「汝名什麼？」曰：「法達。」師曰：「汝名法達，何曾達法？」復說偈曰：「汝今名法達，勤誦未休歇，空誦但循聲，明心號菩薩。汝今有緣故，吾今為汝說，但信佛無言，蓮華從口發。」達聞偈，悔謝曰：「而今而後，當謙恭一切。弟子誦《法華經》，未解經義，心常有疑。和尚智慧廣大，願略說經中義理。」師曰：「法達！法即甚達，汝心不達。經本無疑，汝心自疑。
passages.translation_en: 'Listen to my verse: Bowing is meant to topple the banner of pride — why then does your head not touch the ground? When there is a sense of self, offenses arise at once; forget all merit, and your bowing is beyond compare.' The Master then asked: 'What is your name?' He answered: 'Fada.' The Master said: 'Your name means "Dharma Penetrator" — yet when have you ever penetrated the Dharma?' He then spoke another verse: 'Your name is Fada, yet you tirelessly recite without rest. Chanting by rote merely follows the sound; one who illuminates the mind is called a bodhisattva. Because you have this karmic connection, I will now explain it for you. Simply trust that the Buddha speaks without words, and the lotus flower will blossom from your mouth.' Hearing the verse, Fada repented and apologized, saying: 'From this day forward, I shall be humble and respectful toward all. I have been reciting the Lotus Sutra but have not understood its meaning, and my mind has always been plagued by doubts. Master, your wisdom is vast — please briefly explain the essential principles of the sutra.' The Master said: 'Fada! The Dharma is quite penetrating — it is your own mind that has not penetrated it. The sutra itself holds no doubts; it is your own mind that creates doubt.'

passages.text: 汝念此經，以何為宗？」達曰：「學人根性闇鈍，從來但依文誦念，豈知宗趣？」師曰：「吾不識文字，汝試取經誦一遍，吾當為汝解說。」法達即高聲念經，至譬喻品，師曰：「止！此經元來以因緣出世為宗，縱說多種譬喻，亦無越於此。何者因緣？經云：『諸佛世尊，唯以一大事因緣出現於世。』一大事者，佛之知見也。世人外迷著相，內迷著空；若能於相離相、於空離空，即是內外不迷。若悟此法，一念心開，是為開佛知見。佛，猶覺也。
passages.translation_en: 'With what do you take as the essential theme when you recite this sutra?' Fada replied: 'This student's capacity is dull and dim. I have always just followed the text and recited aloud — how would I know its essential purport?' The Master said: 'I cannot read, but if you try reciting it once for me, I will explain it to you.' Fada then recited the sutra in a loud voice. When he reached the Parables chapter, the Master said: 'Stop! This sutra takes as its central theme the causes and conditions of the Buddha's appearance in the world. No matter how many parables are offered, none go beyond this. What are these causes and conditions? The sutra says: "All the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, appear in the world for the sake of one great matter of causes and conditions." This one great matter is the Buddha's knowledge and insight. Worldly people are outwardly deluded by attachment to forms, and inwardly deluded by attachment to emptiness. If one can be free from forms while among forms, and free from emptiness while in emptiness, then one is deluded neither inwardly nor outwardly. If you awaken to this Dharma, in a single thought the mind opens — this is called "opening the Buddha's knowledge and insight." Buddha simply means awakening.'

passages.text: 分為四門，開覺知見、示覺知見、悟覺知見、入覺知見。若聞開示，便能悟入，即覺知見，本來真性而得出現。汝慎勿錯解經意，見他道：『開示悟入，自是佛之知見。我輩無分。』若作此解，乃是謗經毀佛也。彼既是佛，已具知見，何用更開？汝今當信，佛知見者，只汝自心，更無別佛。蓋為一切眾生，自蔽光明，貪愛塵境，外緣內擾，甘受驅馳。便勞他世尊，從三昧起，種種苦口，勸令寢息，莫向外求，與佛無二。故云：『開佛知見。
passages.translation_en: 'It is divided into four aspects: opening awakened insight, revealing awakened insight, realizing awakened insight, and entering awakened insight. If upon hearing the opening and revealing, one can realize and enter, then awakened insight — one's original true nature — manifests. You must be careful not to misinterpret the sutra's meaning and think: "Opening, revealing, realizing, and entering belong only to the Buddha's knowledge and insight — we have no share in it." To hold such a view is to slander the sutra and defame the Buddha. Since the Buddha already possesses knowledge and insight, what need would there be to open it further? You should now have faith that the Buddha's knowledge and insight is nothing other than your own mind — there is no other Buddha. It is because all sentient beings veil their own luminosity, crave and cling to the sense-objects, and are disturbed from within by external conditions, that they willingly submit to being driven about. This is what compelled the World-Honored One to rise from samadhi and, with all manner of earnest exhortation, urge them to rest and be still, to stop seeking outside themselves, and to realize they are no different from the Buddha. Hence it is said: "Opening the Buddha's knowledge and insight."'

passages.text: 』吾亦勸一切人，於自心中，常開佛之知見。世人心邪，愚迷造罪，口善心惡，貪瞋嫉妬，諂佞我慢，侵人害物，自開眾生知見。若能正心，常生智慧，觀照自心，止惡行善，是自開佛之知見。汝須念念開佛知見，勿開眾生知見。開佛知見，即是出世；開眾生知見，即是世間。汝若但勞勞執念，以為功課者，何異犛牛愛尾。」達曰：「若然者，但得解義，不勞誦經耶？」師曰：「經有何過，豈障汝念？只為迷悟在人，損益由己。
passages.translation_en: 'I too urge all people to constantly open the Buddha's knowledge and insight within their own minds. The minds of worldly people are crooked — foolish, deluded, and creating offenses; their mouths speak of goodness while their hearts harbor evil; they are full of greed, anger, jealousy, flattery, deceit, and arrogance; they harm others and injure living things. This is to open the knowledge and insight of sentient beings. If one can rectify the mind, constantly give rise to wisdom, contemplate and illuminate one's own mind, and cease evil while practicing good — this is to open the Buddha's knowledge and insight for oneself. In every thought, you must open the Buddha's knowledge and insight; do not open the knowledge and insight of sentient beings. To open the Buddha's knowledge and insight is to be beyond the world; to open the knowledge and insight of sentient beings is to remain in the world. If you merely toil away clinging to recitation and consider it your spiritual practice, how are you different from a yak infatuated with its own tail?' Fada asked: 'If that is so, then one need only understand the meaning — there is no need to recite the sutra?' The Master said: 'What fault does the sutra have? How could it obstruct your recitation? Delusion and awakening lie in the person; loss and gain depend on oneself.'

passages.text: 口誦心行，即是轉經；口誦心不行，即是被經轉。聽吾偈曰：心迷法華轉，心悟轉法華，誦經久不明，與義作讎家。無念念即正，有念念成邪，有無俱不計，長御白牛車。」達聞偈，不覺悲泣，言下大悟，而告師曰：「法達從昔已來，實未曾轉法華，乃被法華轉。」再啟曰：「經云：『諸大聲聞乃至菩薩，皆盡思共度量，不能測佛智。』今令凡夫但悟自心，便名佛之知見。自非上根，未免疑謗。
passages.translation_en: 'When you recite with your mouth and practice with your mind, that is turning the sutra. When you recite with your mouth but do not practice with your mind, you are being turned by the sutra. Listen to my verse: When the mind is deluded, it is turned by the Lotus; when the mind is awakened, it turns the Lotus. Reciting for so long without understanding makes one an enemy of the teaching's meaning. Without thought-attachment, thought is correct; with thought-attachment, thought becomes deviant. When neither being nor non-being is calculated, one rides forever in the white ox cart.' Upon hearing the verse, Fada wept without realizing it and experienced great awakening. He said to the Master: 'From the very beginning until now, Fada has in truth never turned the Lotus Sutra — rather, the Lotus Sutra has been turning me.' He then asked further: 'The sutra says: "All the great shravakas and even the bodhisattvas, pooling all their thought, cannot fathom the Buddha's wisdom." Yet now you say that ordinary people need only awaken to their own mind and it is called the Buddha's knowledge and insight. Unless one is of the highest capacity, this will inevitably give rise to doubt and slander.'

passages.text: 又經說三車，羊鹿牛車與白牛之車，如何區別？願和尚再垂開示。」師曰：「經意分明，汝自迷背。諸三乘人，不能測佛智者，患在度量也。饒伊盡思共推，轉加懸遠。佛本為凡夫說，不為佛說。此理若不肯信者，從他退席。殊不知，坐却白牛車，更於門外覓三車。況經文明向汝道：『唯一佛乘，無有餘乘若二若三。』乃至無數方便，種種因緣譬喻言詞，是法皆為一佛乘故。汝何不省，三車是假，為昔時故；一乘是實，為今時故。
passages.translation_en: 'Furthermore, the sutra speaks of three carts — the goat cart, the deer cart, and the ox cart — and the white ox cart. How are these to be distinguished? I humbly ask the Master to explain once more.' The Master said: 'The sutra's meaning is perfectly clear; it is you yourself who turn away from it in confusion. The reason people of the Three Vehicles cannot fathom the Buddha's wisdom is that the problem lies in their calculating and measuring. The more they exhaust their thought and speculation, the further away they get. The Buddha originally taught for the sake of ordinary beings, not for those already enlightened. If people refuse to accept this principle, let them leave the assembly. What they fail to realize is that they are already sitting in the white ox cart, yet they go outside the gate looking for three other carts. Moreover, the sutra plainly tells you: "There is only the One Buddha Vehicle; there are no other vehicles, whether two or three." All the countless skillful means, all the various causes, conditions, parables, and expressions — all these are for the sake of the One Buddha Vehicle. Why can you not see? The three carts are provisional, established for the past; the One Vehicle is real, established for the present.'

passages.text:
只教汝去假歸實，歸實之後，實亦無名。應知所有珍財，盡屬於汝，由汝受用，更不作父想，亦不作子想，亦無用想。是名持法華經，從劫至劫，手不釋卷，從晝至夜，無不念時也。」達蒙啟發，踊躍歡喜，以偈讚曰：「經誦三千部，曹溪一句亡，未明出世旨，寧歇累生狂。羊鹿牛權設，初中後善揚，誰知火宅內，元是法中王。」師曰：「汝今後方可名念經僧也。」達從此領玄旨，亦不輟誦經。
僧智通，壽州安豐人。
passages.translation_en:
'The teaching is simply to have you abandon the provisional and return to the real. After returning to the real, even "real" has no name. You should know that all the precious treasures belong entirely to you, for you to use freely — without thinking of them as the father's, nor as the son's, nor needing any thought of using them at all. This is called truly upholding the Lotus Sutra — from kalpa to kalpa, the hand never lets go of the scroll; from dawn to night, there is not a moment without mindfulness of it.' Fada, having received this revelation, leapt with joy and offered this verse of praise: 'Three thousand times the sutra was recited, but one phrase at Caoxi swept it all away. Before the meaning of the Buddha's appearance was clear, how could the madness accumulated over lifetimes be put to rest? The goat, deer, and ox carts were provisionally established; the good of the beginning, middle, and end was thus proclaimed. Who would have known that within the burning house, one was all along the Dharma King?' The Master said: 'From now on, you may truly be called a sutra-reciting monk.' Fada, having grasped the profound meaning from that point on, also never ceased reciting the sutra.

The monk Zhitong was a native of Anfeng in Shouzhou.

passages.text: 初看《楞伽經》，約千餘遍，而不會三身四智。禮師求解其義，師曰：「三身者，清淨法身，汝之性也；圓滿報身，汝之智也；千百億化身，汝之行也。若離本性，別說三身，即名有身無智；若悟三身無有自性，即明四智菩提。聽吾偈曰：自性具三身，發明成四智，不離見聞緣，超然登佛地。吾今為汝說，諦信永無迷，莫學馳求者，終日說菩提。」通再啟曰：「四智之義，可得聞乎？」師曰：「既會三身，便明四智。
passages.translation_en: He had studied the Lankavatara Sutra roughly a thousand times but could not comprehend the Three Bodies and Four Wisdoms. He came to the Master seeking an explanation. The Master said: 'The Three Bodies are as follows: the pure Dharmakaya is your own nature; the perfect Sambhogakaya is your own wisdom; the myriad billions of Nirmanakayas are your own actions. If you speak of the Three Bodies as separate from your original nature, that is called having bodies without wisdom. If you realize that the Three Bodies have no independent self-nature, that is to illuminate the Four Wisdoms of bodhi. Listen to my verse: Your own nature is complete with the Three Bodies; when illuminated, they become the Four Wisdoms. Without departing from seeing and hearing, one transcends directly to the ground of Buddhahood. I now explain this for you — have sincere faith and you will never be confused. He said: "Your original nature is just like empty space — there is not a single thing to be seen, and this is called right view. There is not a single thing to be known, and this is called true knowledge. Had I not entered the Patriarch's chamber, I would have remained lost, chasing both extremes.' passages.translation_en: The monk Zhidao was a native of Nanhai in Guangzhou. He came to seek instruction, saying: ‘Since I left home to become a monk, I have studied the Nirvana Sutra for over ten years, yet I still do not understand its essential meaning. I humbly ask the Master to bestow his teaching.’ The Master said: ‘Where exactly do you not understand?’ He replied: ‘The passage that says: All conditioned phenomena are the dharma of arising and ceasing; when arising and ceasing are themselves extinguished, the quiescence of cessation is bliss. This is where my doubt lies.’

passages.translation_en: The Master said: ‘What exactly is your doubt?’ He replied: ‘All sentient beings have two bodies: the physical body and the Dharma body. The physical body is impermanent—it arises and perishes. The Dharma body is permanent, yet without knowing or perceiving. The sutra says: When arising and ceasing are themselves extinguished, the quiescence of cessation is bliss. But I am unsure—which body achieves quiescent cessation? Which body experiences bliss? If it is the physical body, then when the physical body perishes and the four great elements scatter, it is entirely suffering—suffering cannot be called bliss. If the Dharma body achieves quiescent cessation, it would be the same as grass, trees, tiles, and stones—who then experiences bliss? Furthermore, the Dharma-nature is the substance of arising and ceasing, and the five aggregates are the function of arising and ceasing. One substance with five functions—arising and ceasing are constant. When arising occurs, function emerges from substance; when ceasing occurs, function returns to substance. If rebirth is permitted, then sentient beings are neither cut off nor extinguished. If rebirth is not permitted, then all returns permanently to quiescent cessation, the same as insentient things.’

According to what you have said, there is a Dharma body separate from the physical body, and one must leave arising-and-ceasing to seek quiescent cessation. Furthermore, you infer that nirvana is permanent bliss and say there is a body that experiences it. This is clinging to birth-and-death and indulging in worldly pleasures. You should now understand: the Buddha taught this because all deluded people take the union of the five aggregates as their own self, distinguish all dharmas as external sense-objects, crave life and loathe death, drift from thought to thought, not knowing that all is like a dream or illusion, and vainly undergo the cycle of rebirth. They turn the permanent bliss of nirvana into a mark of suffering, and all day long they chase after things. Out of compassion for this, the Buddha revealed the true bliss of nirvana.’

One constantly responds through the sense faculties, yet gives rise to no thought of functioning; one discriminates all dharmas, yet gives rise to no thought of discrimination. Even when the fire at the end of the kalpa burns the ocean floor, and wind-driven mountains crash against each other, the true, permanent bliss of quiescent cessation—such is the nature of nirvana. But after that Buddha, anyone who claims self-awakening without a teacher is nothing but a naturalist heretic.’ Xuanjue said: ‘I ask you to serve as my witness.’ Xuance said: ‘My word carries little weight. At Caoxi, the Sixth Patriarch is there, and students gather from all directions—all of them recipients of the Dharma. If you wish to go, I will accompany you.’ Xuanjue then traveled with Xuance to call on the Master. He circumambulated the Master three times, struck his staff on the ground, and stood still. The Master said: ‘A monk is one who embodies the three thousand rules of deportment and eighty thousand fine practices.’

passages.text: 時，祖師居曹溪寶林，神秀大師在荊南玉泉寺。于時兩宗盛化，人皆稱南能北秀，故有南北二宗頓漸之分，而學者莫知宗趣。師謂眾曰：「法本一宗，人有南北。法即一種，見有遲疾。何名頓漸？法無頓漸，人有利鈍，故名頓漸。」然秀之徒眾，往往譏南宗祖師，不識一字，有何所長。秀曰：「他得無師之智，深悟上乘。吾不如也。且吾師五祖，親傳衣法。豈徒然哉！吾恨不能遠去親近，虛受國恩。汝等諸人，毋滯於此，可往曹溪參決。
passages.translation_en: At that time, the Sixth Patriarch was residing at Baolin Monastery in Caoxi, while Great Master Shenxiu was at Yuquan Temple in Jingnan. Both schools were flourishing, and people commonly referred to them as 'Huineng of the South' and 'Shenxiu of the North,' giving rise to the distinction between the Southern and Northern schools and their 'sudden' versus 'gradual' approaches. Yet students could not discern the true meaning of either school. The Master addressed the assembly: 'The Dharma is originally one school; it is people who come from south or north. The Dharma is of one kind; it is perception that is slow or fast. Why speak of sudden and gradual? The Dharma itself has no sudden or gradual — people are sharp or dull, hence the names sudden and gradual.' Meanwhile, Shenxiu's followers frequently disparaged the Patriarch of the Southern school, saying he could not read a single character and had nothing noteworthy about him. Shenxiu said: 'He has attained the wisdom that needs no teacher and has deeply awakened to the Supreme Vehicle. I am not his equal. Moreover, our teacher the Fifth Patriarch personally transmitted the robe and Dharma to him — how could that be without reason? I regret only that I cannot travel far to be near him, and that I receive imperial favor in vain. All of you should not linger here — go to Caoxi and seek the decisive teaching.'

passages.text: 」一日，命門人志誠曰：「汝聰明多智，可為吾到曹溪聽法。若有所聞，盡心記取，還為吾說。」志誠稟命至曹溪，隨眾參請，不言來處。時祖師告眾曰：「今有盜法之人，潛在此會。」志誠即出禮拜，具陳其事。師曰：「汝從玉泉來，應是細作。」對曰：「不是。」師曰：「何得不是？」對曰：「未說即是，說了不是。」師曰：「汝師若為示眾？」對曰：「常指誨大眾，住心觀靜，長坐不臥。
passages.translation_en: One day, Shenxiu instructed his disciple Zhicheng: 'You are clever and perceptive. Go to Caoxi on my behalf and listen to the teaching. If you hear anything, remember it thoroughly and relate it to me.' Zhicheng followed these instructions and went to Caoxi, joining the assembly without revealing where he had come from. At that time the Patriarch told the assembly: 'There is someone here today who has come to steal the Dharma, hiding in this gathering.' Zhicheng immediately came forward, bowed, and explained the whole matter. The Master said: 'You come from Yuquan — you must be a spy.' Zhicheng replied: 'No, I am not.' The Master said: 'How can you say you are not?' Zhicheng replied: 'Before I spoke, I was. Now that I have spoken, I am not.' The Master asked: 'How does your teacher instruct the assembly?' Zhicheng replied: 'He constantly teaches the great assembly to fix the mind and contemplate stillness, to sit for long periods without lying down.'

passages.text: 」師曰：「住心觀靜，是病非禪；長坐拘身，於理何益？聽吾偈曰：生來坐不臥，死去臥不坐，一具臭骨頭，何為立功課？」志誠再拜曰：「弟子在秀大師處學道九年，不得契悟。今聞和尚一說，便契本心。弟子生死事大，和尚大慈，更為教示。」師云：「吾聞汝師教示學人戒定慧法，未審汝師說戒定慧行相如何？與吾說看。」誠曰：「秀大師說，諸惡莫作名為戒，諸善奉行名為慧，自淨其意名為定。
passages.translation_en: The Master said: 'Fixing the mind and contemplating stillness — this is sickness, not Chan. Sitting for long periods merely confines the body — what benefit does it serve for understanding truth? Listen to my verse: In life, sitting and never lying down; in death, lying down and never sitting — in both cases, just a set of stinking bones. What basis is this for spiritual practice?' Zhicheng bowed again and said: 'I studied the Way under Great Master Shenxiu for nine years without attaining realization. Now, hearing the Master's single statement, it accords with my original mind. The matter of birth and death is of great urgency. I beg the Master, in great compassion, to teach me further.' The Master said: 'I have heard that your teacher instructs students in the method of precepts, concentration, and wisdom. I wonder how your teacher explains the characteristics of precepts, concentration, and wisdom? Tell me.' Zhicheng said: 'Great Master Shenxiu says: refraining from all evil is called precepts; practicing all good is called wisdom; purifying one's own mind is called concentration.'

passages.text: 彼說如此，未審和尚以何法誨人？」師曰：「吾若言有法與人，即為誑汝。但且隨方解縛，假名三昧。如汝師所說戒定慧，實不可思議。吾所見戒定慧又別。」志誠曰：「戒定慧只合一種，如何更別？」師曰：「汝師戒定慧接大乘人，吾戒定慧接最上乘人。悟解不同，見有遲疾。汝聽吾說，與彼同否？吾所說法，不離自性。離體說法，名為相說，自性常迷。須知一切萬法，皆從自性起用，是真戒定慧法。
passages.translation_en: 'That is what he teaches. I wonder what Dharma the Master uses to instruct people?' The Master said: 'If I claimed to have a teaching to give people, I would be deceiving you. I simply untie bonds according to circumstances, provisionally calling it samadhi. As for the precepts, concentration, and wisdom your teacher speaks of — they are truly inconceivable. But my understanding of precepts, concentration, and wisdom is different.' Zhicheng said: 'There should be only one kind of precepts, concentration, and wisdom. How can there be a difference?' The Master said: 'Your teacher's precepts, concentration, and wisdom are suited to those of the Mahayana. My precepts, concentration, and wisdom are suited to those of the Supreme Vehicle. Awakening and understanding differ; perception may be slow or fast. Listen to what I say and see whether it is the same as his or not. The Dharma I teach never departs from self-nature. To teach Dharma apart from the essence is called teaching through characteristics, and one's self-nature remains forever confused. You must know that all the myriad dharmas arise from the functioning of self-nature — this is the true teaching of precepts, concentration, and wisdom.'

passages.text: 聽吾偈曰：心地無非自性戒，心地無癡自性慧，心地無亂自性定，不增不減自金剛，身去身來本三昧。」誠聞偈，悔謝，乃呈一偈曰：「五蘊幻身，幻何究竟？迴趣真如，法還不淨。」師然之，復語誠曰：「汝師戒定慧，勸小根智人；吾戒定慧，勸大根智人。若悟自性，亦不立菩提涅槃，亦不立解脫知見。無一法可得，方能建立萬法。若解此意，亦名佛身，亦名菩提涅槃，亦名解脫知見。
passages.translation_en: 'Listen to my verse: When the ground of mind is free from wrong, that is the precept of self-nature. When the ground of mind is free from delusion, that is the wisdom of self-nature. When the ground of mind is free from disturbance, that is the concentration of self-nature. Neither increasing nor decreasing — that itself is diamond. The body comes and goes, yet fundamentally it is samadhi.' Hearing this verse, Zhicheng repented and expressed gratitude, then offered a verse of his own: 'The five aggregates are an illusory body — how could illusion be ultimate? Even turning toward True Suchness, the Dharma is still not pure.' The Master affirmed this and further told Zhicheng: 'Your teacher's precepts, concentration, and wisdom encourage those of lesser capacity and lesser wisdom. My precepts, concentration, and wisdom encourage those of greater capacity and greater wisdom. If one awakens to self-nature, one does not even establish bodhi and nirvana, nor does one establish liberation or knowledge and insight. When not a single dharma can be grasped, only then can one establish the myriad dharmas. If you understand this meaning, it is also called the Buddha-body, also called bodhi and nirvana, also called liberation and knowledge and insight.'

passages.text:
見性之人，立亦得、不立亦得，去來自由，無滯無礙，應用隨作，應語隨答，普見化身，不離自性，即得自在神通游戲三昧，是名見性。」志誠再啟師曰：「如何是不立義？」師曰：「自性無非、無癡無亂，念念般若觀照，常離法相，自由自在，縱橫盡得，有何可立？自性自悟，頓悟頓修，亦無漸次，所以不立一切法。諸法寂滅，有何次第？」志誠禮拜，願為執侍，朝夕不懈。
僧志徹，江西人，本姓張，名行昌，少任俠。
passages.translation_en: 'One who has seen their nature can establish or not establish — coming and going freely, without obstruction or hindrance. In action one responds spontaneously, in speech one answers spontaneously. Seeing transformation bodies everywhere, yet never departing from self-nature — this is to attain the samadhi of sovereign spiritual power and playful freedom. This is called seeing one's nature.' Zhicheng again addressed the Master: 'What is the meaning of not establishing?' The Master said: 'When self-nature is without wrong, without delusion, without disturbance, and every thought is illuminated by prajna, always transcending dharma-characteristics, free and at ease, penetrating everywhere without obstruction — what is there to establish? Self-nature is self-awakened; awakening is sudden, practice is sudden. There are no gradual stages, and therefore not a single dharma is established. All dharmas are quiescent — what stages could there be?' Zhicheng bowed in reverence and vowed to serve as the Master's attendant, diligent morning and evening without slackening.

passages.text: 自南北分化，二宗主雖亡彼我，而徒侶競起愛憎。時北宗門人，自立秀師為第六祖，而忌祖師傳衣為天下聞，乃囑行昌來刺師。師心通，預知其事，即置金十兩於座間。時夜暮，行昌入祖室，將欲加害。師舒頸就之，行昌揮刃者三，悉無所損。師曰：「正劍不邪，邪劍不正。只負汝金，不負汝命。」行昌驚仆，久而方蘇，求哀悔過，即願出家。師遂與金，言：「汝且去，恐徒眾翻害於汝。汝可他日易形而來，吾當攝受。」行昌稟旨宵遁。
passages.translation_en: The monk Zhiche, a native of Jiangxi, was originally surnamed Zhang with the given name Xingchang. In his youth he was a man of martial daring. Since the division into Southern and Northern schools, although the two founders themselves were free of rivalry, their followers increasingly gave rise to attachment and aversion. At that time the followers of the Northern school, having on their own authority established Master Shenxiu as the Sixth Patriarch, resented that the Patriarch's transmission of the robe was known throughout the land. So they dispatched Xingchang to assassinate the Master. The Master, whose mind was penetrating, foreknew this matter, and placed ten taels of gold beside his seat. That night, Xingchang entered the Patriarch's chamber intending to do harm. The Master extended his neck to receive the blade. Xingchang swung the sword three times, but caused no injury whatsoever. The Master said: 'A righteous sword does not cut crookedly; a crooked sword cannot cut rightly. I owe you gold, not my life.' Xingchang fell down in shock and lay unconscious for a long time before reviving. He begged for mercy and repented, vowing to leave home and become a monk. The Master gave him the gold and said: 'You should go now — I fear the assembly may turn and harm you. Come another day in a different guise, and I will accept you.' Xingchang followed these instructions and fled into the night.

passages.text: 後投僧出家，具戒精進。一日，憶師之言，遠來禮覲。師曰：「吾久念汝，汝來何晚？」曰：「昨蒙和尚捨罪，今雖出家苦行，終難報德，其惟傳法度生乎？弟子常覽《涅槃經》，未曉常無常義。乞和尚慈悲，略為解說。」師曰：「無常者，即佛性也。有常者，即一切善惡諸法分別心也。」曰：「和尚所說，大違經文。」師曰：「吾傳佛心印，安敢違於佛經？」曰：「經說佛性是常；和尚却言無常。善惡之法乃至菩提心，皆是無常；和尚却言是常。
passages.translation_en: Later he joined the sangha, was fully ordained, and practiced with diligence. One day, remembering the Master's words, he traveled from afar to pay his respects. The Master said: 'I have been thinking of you for a long time. Why have you come so late?' Xingchang said: 'Previously the Master pardoned my offense. Though I have now left home and practice austerities, I can never fully repay such virtue. Perhaps the only way is to transmit the Dharma and save sentient beings? I have been reading the Nirvana Sutra regularly, but I do not understand the meaning of permanence and impermanence. I humbly beg the Master to explain briefly out of compassion.' The Master said: 'Impermanence is itself Buddha-nature. Permanence is the discriminating mind that separates all dharmas into good and evil.' Xingchang said: 'What the Master says greatly contradicts the sutra text.' The Master said: 'I transmit the Buddha's mind-seal. How would I dare contradict the Buddha's sutras?' Xingchang said: 'The sutra says Buddha-nature is permanent, yet the Master says it is impermanent. It says good and evil dharmas, even the bodhi-mind, are all impermanent, yet the Master says they are permanent.'

passages.text: 此即相違，令學人轉加疑惑。」師曰：「《涅槃經》吾昔聽尼無盡藏讀誦一遍，便為講說，無一字一義不合經文。乃至為汝，終無二說。」曰：「學人識量淺昧，願和尚委曲開示。」師曰：「汝知否？佛性若常，更說什麼善惡諸法，乃至窮劫無有一人發菩提心者；故吾說無常，正是佛說真常之道也。又，一切諸法若無常者，即物物皆有自性，容受生死，而真常性有不遍之處。故吾說常者，正是佛說真無常義。
passages.translation_en: 'This is a direct contradiction that only deepens the student's doubt and confusion.' The Master said: 'Long ago I heard the nun Wujinzang recite the Nirvana Sutra once through, and I then expounded it for her. Not a single word or meaning was at odds with the sutra text. What I say to you now is no different.' Xingchang said: 'This student's understanding is shallow and dim. I beg the Master to explain in detail.' The Master said: 'Do you understand? If Buddha-nature were permanent, what more would there be to say about good and evil dharmas? To the end of all kalpas, not a single person would give rise to the bodhi-mind. Therefore, when I say impermanence, this is precisely the true permanence that the Buddha taught. Furthermore, if all dharmas were truly impermanent, then every single thing would possess an independent self-nature, capable of undergoing birth and death, and the truly permanent nature would fail to pervade everywhere. Therefore, when I say permanence, this is precisely the true impermanence that the Buddha meant.'

passages.text:
佛比為凡夫、外道執於邪常，諸二乘人於常計無常，共成八倒，故於《涅槃》了義教中，破彼偏見，而顯說真常、真樂、真我、真淨。汝今依言背義，以斷滅無常及確定死常，而錯解佛之圓妙最後微言。縱覽千遍，有何所益？」行昌忽然大悟，說偈曰：「因守無常心，佛說有常性，不知方便者，猶春池拾礫。我今不施功，佛性而現前，非師相授與，我亦無所得。」師曰：「汝今徹也，宜名志徹。」徹禮謝而退。
有一童子，名神會，襄陽高氏子。
passages.translation_en: 'It was because ordinary people and non-Buddhist practitioners cling to deviant permanence, and practitioners of the two vehicles mistake the permanent for impermanent, that together they form the eight inversions. Therefore in the definitive teaching of the Nirvana Sutra, the Buddha refuted their one-sided views and revealed true permanence, true joy, true self, and true purity. You now go against the meaning by following the words, interpreting the Buddha's most subtle final teaching through the lens of nihilistic impermanence and fixed, dead permanence. Even if you read the sutra a thousand times, what benefit would it bring?' Xingchang suddenly experienced a great awakening and spoke this verse: 'Because I clung to a mind of impermanence, the Buddha taught that there is a permanent nature. Not knowing this was a skillful means is like picking up pebbles from a spring pond. Now, without any effort on my part, Buddha-nature manifests before me. It is not that the teacher gave it to me, nor have I gained anything at all.' The Master said: 'Now you have thoroughly understood. You should be named Zhiche.' Zhiche bowed in gratitude and departed.

passages.text: 年十三，自玉泉來參禮。師曰：「知識遠來艱辛，還將得本來否？若有本則合識主。試說看。」會曰：「以無住為本，見即是主。」師曰：「這沙彌爭合取次語？」會乃問曰：「和尚坐禪，還見不見？」師以柱杖打三下，云：「吾打汝痛不痛？」對曰：「亦痛亦不痛。」師曰：「吾亦見亦不見。」神會問：「如何是亦見亦不見？」師云：「吾之所見，常見自心過愆，不見他人是非好惡，是以亦見亦不見。汝言：『亦痛亦不痛。
passages.translation_en: There was a young boy named Shenhui, a son of the Gao family of Xiangyang. At the age of thirteen, he came from Yuquan Temple to pay his respects. The Master said: 'Friend, you have come a long way through hardship. Have you brought the fundamental with you? If you possess the fundamental, you should know its master. Try to speak.' Shenhui said: 'I take non-abiding as the fundamental, and seeing as the master.' The Master said: 'This little novice — how dare you speak so glibly?' Shenhui then asked: 'When the Master sits in meditation, does he see or not see?' The Master struck him three times with his staff and said: 'When I strike you, does it hurt or not hurt?' Shenhui replied: 'It both hurts and doesn't hurt.' The Master said: 'I also both see and don't see.' Shenhui asked: 'What do you mean by both seeing and not seeing?' The Master said: 'What I see is that I constantly see the faults and errors of my own mind. I do not see the right and wrong, the good and bad, of others. This is why I say I both see and don't see. Now what about your saying it both hurts and doesn't hurt?'

passages.text: 』如何？汝若不痛，同其木石；若痛，則同凡夫，即起恚恨。汝向前見、不見是二邊，痛、不痛是生滅。汝自性且不見，敢爾弄人！」神會禮拜悔謝。師又曰：「汝若心迷不見，問善知識覓路。汝若心悟，即自見性依法修行。汝自迷不見自心，却來問吾見與不見。吾見自知，豈代汝迷？汝若自見，亦不代吾迷。何不自知自見，乃問吾見與不見？」神會再禮百餘拜，求謝過愆。服勤給侍，不離左右。
passages.translation_en: 'If it doesn't hurt, you are like wood or stone. If it does hurt, you are no different from an ordinary person and will give rise to anger and resentment. Your earlier answers of seeing and not-seeing are dualistic, and your hurt and not-hurt belong to arising and ceasing. You have not yet even seen your own nature, and yet you dare to come here and play games with people!' Shenhui bowed in repentance and gratitude. The Master continued: 'If your mind is confused and you cannot see, then ask a good spiritual friend to show you the way. If your mind is awakened, then see your own nature and practice in accord with the Dharma. You yourself are confused and cannot see your own mind, yet you come asking me whether I see or not. If I see, I know it for myself — how could that resolve your confusion? If you could see for yourself, that would equally not resolve my confusion. Why don't you know and see for yourself, instead of asking me whether I see or not?' Shenhui bowed more than a hundred times, begging forgiveness for his faults. He then served the Master diligently as an attendant, never leaving his side.

passages.text:
一日，師告眾曰：「吾有一物，無頭無尾，無名無字，無背無面。諸人還識否？」神會出曰：「是諸佛之本源，神會之佛性。」師曰：「向汝道：『無名無字』，汝便喚作本源佛性。汝向去有把茆蓋頭，也只成箇知解宗徒。」祖師滅後，會入京洛，大弘曹溪頓教，著《顯宗記》，盛行于世。
師見諸宗難問咸起惡心，多集座下愍而謂曰：「學道之人，一切善念惡念應當盡除。無名可名，名於自性，無二之性，是名實性。
passages.translation_en: One day, the Master addressed the assembly: 'I have one thing — it has no head and no tail, no name and no label, no back and no front. Do any of you recognize it?' Shenhui stepped forward and said: 'It is the original source of all Buddhas, and it is Shenhui's Buddha-nature.' The Master said: 'I just told you it has no name and no label, and you immediately call it the original source and Buddha-nature. Even if you go on to have a thatched hut over your head someday, you will be nothing more than a follower of intellectual understanding.' After the Patriarch's passing, Shenhui went to the capital region of Luoyang, where he widely propagated the sudden teaching of Caoxi. He wrote the Xianzong Ji (Record of Revealing the True Teaching), which became widely known throughout the land.

passages.text: 於實性上建立一切教門，言下便須自見。」諸人聞說，總皆作禮，請事為師。
passages.translation_en: The Master, seeing that followers of various schools were raising questions with hostile intent and gathering in large numbers at his seat, spoke to them with compassion: 'Students of the Way should eliminate all thoughts of good and evil. That which cannot be named, yet is named — call it self-nature. This non-dual nature is what is called true nature. Upon this true nature, all teachings are established. At these words, you should see it directly for yourselves.' Upon hearing this, all present bowed in reverence and requested to serve him as their teacher.

passages.text: 神龍元年上元日，則天、中宗詔云：「朕請安、秀二師宮中供養。萬機之暇，每究一乘。二師推讓云：『南方有能禪師，密授忍大師衣法，傳佛心印，可請彼問。』今遣內侍薛簡，馳詔迎請，願師慈念，速赴上京。」師上表辭疾，願終林麓。薛簡曰：「京城禪德皆云：『欲得會道，必須坐禪習定。若不因禪定而得解脫者，未之有也。』未審師所說法如何？」師曰：「道由心悟，豈在坐也。經云：『若言如來若坐若臥，是行邪道。
passages.translation_en: On the day of the Lantern Festival in the first year of the Shenlong era, Empress Wu Zetian and Emperor Zhongzong issued a decree: 'We have invited Masters Huian and Shenxiu to the palace for offerings. In our leisure from the myriad affairs of state, we often contemplate the One Vehicle. Both masters have deferred, saying: "In the south there is Chan Master Huineng, who secretly received the robe and Dharma from the great Master Hongren, transmitting the Buddha Mind Seal. You should invite him instead." We now dispatch the palace attendant Xue Jian with an urgent decree to welcome and invite you. We hope the Master will be compassionate and swiftly come to the capital.' The Master submitted a memorial declining due to illness, wishing to end his days in the forests. Xue Jian said: 'The Chan worthies in the capital all say: "To realize the Way, one must practice seated meditation and concentration. No one has ever attained liberation without dhyana concentration." I wonder what the Master's teaching is on this?' The Master said: 'The Way is realized through the mind — how could it depend on sitting? The sutra says: "If anyone says the Tathagata either sits or lies down, that person walks an errant path."'

passages.text: 』何故？無所從來，亦無所去。無生無滅，是如來清淨禪。諸法空寂，是如來清淨坐。究竟無證，豈況坐耶。」簡曰：「弟子回京，主上必問。願師慈悲，指示心要，傳奏兩宮及京城學道者。譬如一燈，然百千燈，冥者皆明，明明無盡。」師云：「道無明暗，明暗是代謝之義。明明無盡，亦是有盡，相待立名故。《淨名經》云：『法無有比，無相待故。』」簡曰：「明喻智慧，暗喻煩惱。
passages.translation_en: 'Why? Because there is nowhere the Tathagata comes from, and nowhere he goes. No arising and no ceasing — this is the Tathagata's pure dhyana. The emptiness and stillness of all dharmas — this is the Tathagata's pure sitting. Ultimately there is nothing to be verified, so how much less could it depend on sitting?' Xue Jian said: 'When I return to the capital, Their Majesties will certainly ask. I hope the Master will compassionately point out the essentials of mind, so I may convey them to both palaces and to those studying the Way in the capital. It is like one lamp lighting hundreds and thousands of lamps — all those in darkness become illumined, and the light is endless.' The Master said: 'The Way has neither light nor darkness. Light and darkness refer to alternation and succession. To say "the light is endless" — that too has an end, because the terms are established in mutual dependence. The Vimalakirti Sutra says: "The Dharma has no comparison, because it is not relative."' Xue Jian said: 'Light is a metaphor for wisdom; darkness is a metaphor for affliction.'

passages.text: 修道之人，倘不以智慧照破煩惱，無始生死憑何出離？」師曰：「煩惱即是菩提，無二無別。若以智慧照破煩惱者，此是二乘見解。羊鹿等機，上智大根，悉不如是。」簡曰：「如何是大乘見解？」師曰：「明與無明，凡夫見二；智者了達，其性無二。無二之性，即是實性。實性者，處凡愚而不減，在賢聖而不增，住煩惱而不亂，居禪定而不寂。不斷不常，不來不去，不在中間及其內外，不生不滅，性相如如，常住不遷，名之曰道。
passages.translation_en: 'If a practitioner does not use wisdom to break through affliction, how can one escape the beginningless cycle of birth and death?' The Master said: 'Affliction is itself bodhi — they are not two, not separate. To use wisdom to break through affliction is the understanding of the Two Vehicles. Those of the capacities symbolized by sheep and deer carts — people of superior wisdom and great spiritual roots do not see it this way.' Xue Jian asked: 'What then is the Mahayana understanding?' The Master said: 'Light and non-light — ordinary people see them as two. The wise penetrate to the truth that their nature is not two. This non-dual nature is the true nature. The true nature is not diminished in the foolish and ordinary, not increased in the worthy and sagely. It is not disturbed amid affliction, not stilled in meditation. It is neither cut off nor eternal, neither coming nor going, not in the middle nor inside nor outside, neither arising nor ceasing. Its nature and characteristics are thusness, permanently abiding and unchanging. This is called the Way.'

passages.text:
」簡曰：「師說不生不滅，何異外道？」師曰：「外道所說不生不滅者，將滅止生，以生顯滅，滅猶不滅，生說不生。我說不生不滅者，本自無生，今亦不滅，所以不同外道。汝若欲知心要，但一切善惡都莫思量，自然得入清淨心體，湛然常寂，妙用恒沙。」簡蒙指教，豁然大悟。禮辭歸闕，表奏師語。
其年九月三日，有詔獎諭師曰：「師辭老疾，為朕修道，國之福田。師若淨名托疾毘耶，闡揚大乘，傳諸佛心，談不二法。
passages.translation_en: Xue Jian said: 'The Master teaches neither arising nor ceasing — how does this differ from the non-Buddhists?' The Master said: 'What the non-Buddhists call "neither arising nor ceasing" uses ceasing to stop arising and uses arising to reveal ceasing — their ceasing is not truly ceasing, and their arising they merely claim is non-arising. What I call "neither arising nor ceasing" means there was originally no arising, and now there is also no ceasing. This is why it differs from the non-Buddhists. If you wish to know the essentials of mind, simply do not think about anything good or bad, and you will naturally enter the pure essence of mind — profoundly still and constantly serene, with wondrous functions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.' Xue Jian received this teaching and experienced a great, expansive awakening. He bowed, took his leave, and returned to the palace, where he submitted a memorial reporting the Master's words. In the ninth month, on the third day of that year, an imperial decree was issued commending the Master: 'The Master has declined due to age and illness, cultivating the Way on our behalf — he is a field of merit for the nation. The Master is like Vimalakirti feigning illness in Vaishali, expounding the Great Vehicle, transmitting the Buddha Mind, and teaching the Dharma of non-duality.'

passages.text: 薛簡傳師指授如來知見，朕積善餘慶，宿種善根，值師出世，頓悟上乘。感荷師恩，頂戴無已，并奉磨衲袈裟及水晶鉢，勅韶州剌史修飾寺宇，賜師舊居為國恩寺。」。
passages.translation_en: 'Xue Jian has conveyed the Master's teaching of the Tathagata's knowledge and vision. We have accumulated good fortune and blessings over past lives, planted wholesome roots, and have been fortunate to encounter the Master's appearance in the world, suddenly awakening to the Supreme Vehicle. Feeling deep gratitude for the Master's kindness, we reverently present a mona robe and kasaya along with a crystal bowl, and we command the prefect of Shaozhou to repair and adorn the monastery, bestowing the Master's former residence with the name "Guoen" — "Imperial Grace" — Temple.'

passages.text: 師一日喚門人法海、志誠、法達、神會、智常、智通、志徹、志道、法珍、法如等，曰：「汝等不同餘人，吾滅度後，各為一方師。吾今教汝說法，不失本宗：先須舉三科法門，動用三十六對，出沒即離兩邊。說一切法，莫離自性。忽有人問汝法，出語盡雙，皆取對法，來去相因。究竟二法盡除，更無去處。三科法門者，陰、界、入也。陰是五陰——色、受、想、行、識是也。
passages.translation_en: One day the Master summoned his disciples Fahai, Zhicheng, Fada, Shenhui, Zhichang, Zhitong, Zhiche, Zhidao, Fazhen, Faru, and others, and said: 'You are different from other people. After my passing, each of you will be a teacher in your own region. I will now teach you how to expound the Dharma without losing the essential teaching of our school. First you must raise the Three Categories of Dharma Teachings, employ the Thirty-Six Pairs of Opposites, and in all expression and activity, depart from both extremes. In teaching any dharma, do not depart from the self-nature. If someone suddenly asks you about the Dharma, speak always in pairs, each taking its opposite, cause and effect arising mutually. Ultimately, when both elements of each pair are eliminated, there is nowhere else to go. The Three Categories of Dharma Teachings are the aggregates, the sense-realms, and the sense-fields. The aggregates are the five aggregates: form, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.'

passages.text: 入是十二入——外六塵——色、聲、香、味、觸、法；內六門——眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意是也。界是十八界——六塵、六門、六識是也。自性能含萬法，名含藏識。若起思量，即是轉識。生六識，出六門，見六塵，如是一十八界，皆從自性起用。自性若邪，起十八邪；自性若正，起十八正。若惡用即眾生用，善用即佛用。用由何等？由自性有。對法外境，無情五對：天與地對，日與月對，明與暗對，陰與陽對，水與火對；此是五對也。
passages.translation_en: 'The sense-fields are the twelve sense-fields: the six external objects — form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental objects; and the six internal faculties — eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. The sense-realms are the eighteen realms: the six objects, the six faculties, and the six consciousnesses. The self-nature can contain all dharmas and is called the storehouse consciousness. If thinking arises, that is the transforming consciousness. It generates the six consciousnesses, which go out through the six faculties and perceive the six objects. Thus the eighteen realms all arise from the functioning of the self-nature. If the self-nature is deviant, it gives rise to eighteen deviations; if the self-nature is correct, it gives rise to eighteen correct functions. If used for evil, that is the functioning of a sentient being; if used for good, that is the functioning of a Buddha. What determines the use? The self-nature. For the pairs concerning external objects and non-sentient phenomena, there are five: heaven and earth, sun and moon, light and darkness, yin and yang, water and fire — these are the five pairs.'

passages.text: 法相語言十二對：語與法對，有與無對，有色與無色對，有相與無相對，有漏與無漏對，色與空對，動與靜對，清與濁對，凡與聖對，僧與俗對，老與少對，大與小對；此是十二對也。自性起用十九對：長與短對，邪與正對，癡與慧對，愚與智對，亂與定對，慈與毒對，戒與非對，直與曲對，實與虛對，險與平對，煩惱與菩提對，常與無常對，悲與害對，喜與瞋對，捨與慳對，進與退對，生與滅對，法身與色身對，化身與報身對；此是十九對也。
passages.translation_en: 'For dharma-characteristics and language there are twelve pairs: speech and dharma, existence and non-existence, form and formlessness, having characteristics and having no characteristics, conditioned and unconditioned, form and emptiness, movement and stillness, purity and turbidity, ordinary and sagely, monastic and lay, old and young, great and small — these are the twelve pairs. For self-nature's own functioning there are nineteen pairs: long and short, deviant and correct, delusion and wisdom, foolishness and intelligence, disorder and concentration, compassion and cruelty, morality and immorality, straightness and crookedness, truth and falsehood, danger and safety, affliction and bodhi, permanence and impermanence, pity and harm, joy and anger, renunciation and miserliness, advance and retreat, arising and ceasing, the Dharmakaya and the form body, the transformation body and the reward body — these are the nineteen pairs.'
