師言：「此三十六對法，若解用即道，貫一切經法，出入即離兩邊。自性動用，共人言語，外於相離相，內於空離空。若全著相，即長邪見；若全執空，即長無明。執空之人有謗經，直言不用文字。既云不用文字，人亦不合語言。只此語言，便是文字之相。又云：『直道不立文字。』即此不立兩字，亦是文字。見人所說，便即謗他言著文字。汝等須知，自迷猶可，又謗佛經。不要謗經，罪障無數。
passages.translation_en: The Master said: 'If you understand how to use these thirty-six pairs, you can thread your way through all the sutras and teachings, departing from both extremes in every expression and action. When the self-nature functions in conversation with others, outwardly be in the midst of forms yet detached from forms, and inwardly be in the midst of emptiness yet detached from emptiness. If you are entirely attached to forms, you will foster wrong views; if you entirely grasp at emptiness, you will foster ignorance. Those who cling to emptiness slander the sutras, declaring outright that written words are unnecessary. Since they claim written words are unnecessary, then people should not speak either — for speech itself is a form of written expression. Furthermore they say: "The direct Way is established without written words." But these very words "without written words" are themselves written words. Seeing others teach, they immediately slander them for being attached to words. You must understand: being deluded yourself is one thing, but slandering the Buddha's sutras is another. Do not slander the sutras — the karmic obstacles from doing so are beyond count.'

passages.text: 若著相於外，而作法求真；或廣立道場，說有無之過患。如是之人，累劫不得見性。但聽依法修行，又莫百物不思，而於道性窒礙。若聽說不修，令人反生邪念。但依法修行，無住相法施。汝等若悟，依此說、依此用、依此行、依此作，即不失本宗。若有人問汝義，問有將無對，問無將有對，問凡以聖對，問聖以凡對。二道相因，生中道義。如一問一對，餘問一依此作，即不失理也。設有人問：『何名為闇？』答云：『明是因，闇是緣，明沒即闇。
passages.translation_en: 'If you attach to forms externally and devise practices to seek the truth, or if you extensively establish places of practice and debate the faults of existence and non-existence — people like this, even after countless eons, will never see their true nature. Simply listen and practice according to the Dharma, and do not think about nothing at all, for that would obstruct the nature of the Way. If you only listen to teachings without practicing, it will cause people to develop wrong thoughts. Simply practice according to the Dharma — bestow the Dharma without attachment to any form. If you all awaken, then teach according to this, practice according to this, act according to this, and function according to this, and you will not lose the essential teaching of our school. If someone asks you about meaning, when asked about existence, respond with non-existence; when asked about non-existence, respond with existence; when asked about the ordinary, respond with the sagely; when asked about the sagely, respond with the ordinary. From the mutual causation of these two aspects, the meaning of the Middle Way arises. For each single question and answer, handle the rest in the same way, and you will not lose the principle. Suppose someone asks: "What is darkness?" Answer: "Light is the cause, darkness is the condition. When light vanishes, there is darkness.'

passages.text:
』以明顯闇，以闇顯明，來去相因，成中道義。餘問悉皆如此。汝等於後傳法，依此轉相教授，勿失宗旨。」
時，徒眾聞說偈已，普皆作禮，並體師意，各各攝心，依法修行，更不敢諍，乃知大師不久住世。法海上座，再拜問曰：「和尚入滅之後，衣法當付何人？」師曰：「吾於大梵寺說法，以至于今抄錄流行，目曰『法寶壇經』。汝等守護，遞相傳授。度諸群生，但依此說，是名正法。今為汝等說法，不付其衣。
passages.translation_en: 'Use light to reveal darkness, use darkness to reveal light — they arise mutually as cause and condition, establishing the meaning of the Middle Way. Handle all other questions in exactly this manner. In transmitting the Dharma hereafter, pass on these mutual teachings to one another, and do not lose the essential principle.' At that time, the assembly, having heard these words, all bowed in respect, understood the Master's intent, each gathered their minds, practiced according to the Dharma, and dared not dispute further, knowing that the great Master would not remain in the world much longer. Senior monk Fahai bowed again and asked: 'After the Master enters nirvana, to whom shall the robe and Dharma be entrusted?' The Master said: 'From my teaching at Dafan Temple until now, copies have been made and circulated, entitled the "Dharma Treasure Platform Sutra." Guard and protect it, transmit it to one another in succession, and liberate all sentient beings. Simply teach according to this, and it is the true Dharma. I now transmit the Dharma to you but do not pass on the robe.'

passages.text:
蓋為汝等信根淳熟，決定無疑，堪任大事。然據先祖達磨大師付授偈意，衣不合傳。偈曰：
吾本來茲土，傳法救迷情，一華開五葉，結果自然成。」
師復曰：「諸善知識！汝等各各淨心，聽吾說法。若欲成就種智，須達一相三昧、一行三昧。若於一切處而不住相，於彼相中不生憎愛，亦無取捨，不念利益成壞等事，安閒恬靜，虛融澹泊，此名一相三昧。若於一切處行住坐臥，純一直心，不動道場，真成淨土，此名一行三昧。
passages.translation_en: 'This is because your roots of faith are pure and mature, you are resolute and without doubt, and you are capable of the great task. Moreover, according to the verse left by our first patriarch Bodhidharma for the transmission, the robe should not be passed on further. The verse says: "I originally came to this land to transmit the Dharma and save the deluded. One flower opens five petals, and the fruit ripens of itself."' The Master further said: 'Good friends! Each of you purify your minds and listen to my teaching. If you wish to accomplish the wisdom of all modes, you must penetrate the Samadhi of One Characteristic and the Samadhi of One Practice. If in all places you do not attach to characteristics, and within those characteristics you give rise to neither aversion nor love, and there is no grasping or rejecting, and you do not think of benefit, success, or destruction — peaceful, at ease, tranquil, open, and serene — this is called the Samadhi of One Characteristic. If in all places — walking, standing, sitting, or lying down — you maintain a single, straightforward mind, never departing from the place of awakening, truly accomplishing the Pure Land — this is called the Samadhi of One Practice.'

passages.text:
若人具二三昧，如地有種，含藏長養，成熟其實。一相一行，亦復如是。我今說法，猶如時雨，普潤大地。汝等佛性，譬諸種子，遇茲霑洽，悉得發生。承吾旨者，決獲菩提。依吾行者，定證妙果。聽吾偈曰：
心地含諸種，普雨悉皆萌，頓悟華情已，菩提果自成。」
師說偈已，曰：「其法無二，其心亦然。其道清淨，亦無諸相，汝等慎勿觀靜及空其心。此心本淨，無可取捨。各自努力，隨緣好去。」爾時徒眾作禮而退。
passages.translation_en: 'If a person possesses both samadhis, it is like the earth containing seeds: they are held, nourished, and brought to maturity, bearing fruit. The Samadhi of One Characteristic and the Samadhi of One Practice are just like this. My teaching of the Dharma now is like timely rain, moistening the great earth everywhere. Your Buddha-nature is like seeds — receiving this nourishing rain, all will sprout and grow. Those who receive my teaching will surely attain bodhi. Those who follow my practice will certainly realize the wondrous fruit. Listen to my verse: "The ground of mind contains every seed; with the universal rain, all of them sprout. Once the flower of sudden awakening has bloomed, the fruit of bodhi ripens of itself."' After speaking the verse, the Master said: 'The Dharma is non-dual, and so is the mind. The Way is pure and without any characteristics. Be careful not to contemplate stillness or empty your mind. This mind is originally pure — there is nothing to grasp or reject. Each of you make your own effort, and go well according to conditions.' At that time the assembly bowed and withdrew.

passages.text: 師於太極元年壬子延和七月命門人往新州國恩寺建塔，仍令促工，次年夏末落成。七月一日，集徒眾曰：「吾至八月，欲離世間。汝等有疑，早須相問，為汝破疑，令汝迷盡。吾若去後，無人教汝。」法海等聞，悉皆涕泣。惟有神會，神情不動，亦無涕泣。師云：「神會小師却得善不善等，毀譽不動，哀樂不生；餘者不得。數年山中竟修何道？汝今悲泣，為憂阿誰？若憂吾不知去處，吾自知去處。吾若不知去處，終不預報於汝。
passages.translation_en: In the first year of the Taiji era, the year renzi, in the seventh month of the Yanhe period, the Master ordered his disciples to go to Guoen Temple in Xinzhou to build a stupa, and urged them to hasten the work. It was completed by the end of summer the following year. On the first day of the seventh month, he gathered his disciples and said: 'In the eighth month I wish to leave this world. If you have doubts, ask your questions soon so I may resolve them for you and put an end to your confusion. Once I am gone, there will be no one to teach you.' When Fahai and the others heard this, they all wept. Only Shenhui remained unmoved in spirit, without tears. The Master said: 'Young Master Shenhui alone has attained equanimity toward good and bad, is unmoved by praise or blame, and does not give rise to sorrow or joy. The rest of you have not achieved this. After all these years of practice in the mountains, what Way have you been cultivating? Now you weep — for whom are you worried? If you are worried that I do not know where I am going, I know where I am going. If I did not know, I would not have told you in advance.'

passages.text:
汝等悲泣，蓋為不知吾去處；若知吾去處，即不合悲泣。法性本無生滅去來，汝等盡坐，吾與汝說一偈，名曰真假動靜偈。汝等誦取此偈，與吾意同，依此修行，不失宗旨。」眾僧作禮，請師說偈。偈曰：
一切無有真，不以見於真，若見於真者，是見盡非真。若能自有真，離假即心真，自心不離假，無真何處真？有情即解動，無情即不動，若修不動行，同無情不動。若覓真不動，動上有不動，不動是不動，無情無佛種。
passages.translation_en: 'You weep because you do not know where I am going. If you knew, you would not weep. The Dharma-nature is originally without arising or ceasing, without coming or going. All of you sit down — I will give you a verse called "The Verse of True and False, Movement and Stillness." If you recite and take up this verse, your understanding will accord with mine. Practice according to it and you will not lose the essential teaching.' The assembly bowed and requested the Master to speak the verse. The verse said: "Nothing whatsoever is truly real; do not try to see the real through appearances. If you think you see something real, that seeing is entirely unreal. If you can find the real within yourself, then departing from the false, the mind itself is real. If your own mind does not depart from the false, there is no real — so where would you find it? Sentient beings understand movement; the non-sentient do not move. If you cultivate the practice of non-movement, you become as unmoving as something non-sentient. If you seek the truly unmoving, within movement there is non-movement. But non-movement that is merely non-movement — the non-sentient have no Buddha-seed."

passages.text:
能善分別相，第一義不動，但作如此見，即是真如用。報諸學道人，努力須用意，莫於大乘門，却執生死智。若言下相應，即共論佛義；若實不相應，合掌令歡喜。此宗本無諍，諍即失道意，執逆諍法門，自性入生死。
師復曰：「汝等好住。吾滅度後，莫作世情悲泣雨淚，受人弔問，身著孝服，非吾弟子，亦非正法。但識自本心，見自本性，無動無靜，無生無滅，無去無來，無是無非，無住無往。恐汝等心迷，不會吾意，今再囑汝，令汝見性。
passages.translation_en: "Be skilled in discerning characteristics, while the First Principle remains unmoving. If you can see things in this way, this is the function of true suchness. I say to all who study the Way: make diligent effort and pay attention. Do not, at the gate of the Great Vehicle, cling to the wisdom of birth-and-death. If there is accord at the very moment of speaking, then discuss together the meaning of the Buddha's teaching. If there is truly no accord, then join palms and let there be good will. This school is fundamentally without contention; contention means losing the meaning of the Way. Clinging to disputatious approaches to the Dharma, the self-nature falls into birth-and-death." The Master further said: 'Take good care of yourselves. After my passing, do not follow worldly customs by weeping and shedding tears, receiving condolences, or wearing mourning garments — that would be unworthy of my disciples and contrary to the true Dharma. Simply recognize your own original mind and see your own original nature — without movement or stillness, without arising or ceasing, without going or coming, without right or wrong, without abiding or departing. I fear your minds may be confused and you may not understand my meaning, so I admonish you once more to help you see your nature.'

passages.text:

兀兀不修善，騰騰不造惡，寂寂斷見聞，蕩蕩心無著。
師說偈已，端坐至三更，忽謂門人曰：「吾行矣！」奄然遷化。於時，異香滿室，白虹屬地，林木變白，禽獸哀鳴。
師春秋七十有六，年二十四傳衣，三十九祝髮，說法利生三十七載。得旨嗣法者，四十三人，悟道超凡者，莫知其數。
passages.translation_en: 'After my passing, practice according to this as though I were still present. Even if you go against my teaching, then even if I were present in the world, it would be of no benefit.' He further spoke a verse: "Sitting utterly still, not cultivating good; free and at ease, not creating evil. In quietude, cutting off seeing and hearing; vast and open, the mind has no attachments." After speaking the verse, the Master sat upright until the third watch of the night, then suddenly said to his disciples: 'I am going now!' and passed away serenely. At that time, a strange fragrance filled the room, a white rainbow touched the earth, the trees turned white, and the birds and animals cried out in mourning. The Master lived seventy-six years. He received the robe at age twenty-four, was ordained at thirty-nine, and taught the Dharma for the benefit of sentient beings for thirty-seven years. Forty-three people received and continued his Dharma transmission, while those who awakened to the Way and transcended the ordinary were beyond counting.

師自言，從上以來，佛佛惟傳本體，師師密付本心。過去七佛：毘婆尸佛、尸棄佛、毘舍浮佛、拘留孫佛、拘那含牟尼佛、迦葉佛、釋迦文佛。
此土初祖菩提達磨、二祖慧可大師、三祖僧璨大師、四祖道信大師、五祖弘忍大師、六祖惠能大師。
此六代祖師，已上諸佛及祖，皆傳無相法，汝等見性，勿生疑念。
六祖大師法寶壇經終。
passages.translation_en: The robe transmitted from Bodhidharma, the mona robe and precious bowl bestowed by Emperor Zhongzong, the true likeness of the Master sculpted by Fangbian, together with his monastic implements — all were kept by the attendant in charge of the stupa, to be permanently enshrined at the Baolin monastery. The Master himself had said that from the beginning, from Buddha to Buddha, only the original essence has been transmitted; from teacher to teacher, only the original mind has been secretly entrusted. The seven Buddhas of the past are: Vipashyin Buddha, Shikhin Buddha, Vishvabhu Buddha, Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, Kashyapa Buddha, and Shakyamuni Buddha. The first patriarch of this land was Bodhidharma, the second patriarch was Great Master Huike, the third patriarch was Great Master Sengcan, the fourth patriarch was Great Master Daoxin, the fifth patriarch was Great Master Hongren, and the sixth patriarch was Great Master Huineng. These six generational patriarchs, together with all the Buddhas and ancestors above, all transmitted the formless Dharma. May you all see your true nature and give rise to no doubts. The Dharma Treasure Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch is concluded.
